title: Experiment viability and the one-fill question (strategy/quant lens)
summary: (1) One fill in three days is not the strategy working as designed; it is the fair_stale watcher rule. 7,825 of 7,997 orders (97.8%) were cancelled fair_stale (plan.py:446-456), which compares pricing-run age (now - fair_values.created_at, store.py:354-368) against a 220 s feed-fetch allowance (120 s featured cadence + 100 s tick budget, fair.py:24,35) while pricing actually recurs every 900/300/120 s plus tick duration (cadence.py:16-33, tick.py:576-583, 906-920). Weekday daytime: every order dies ~200 s after placement and cannot be re-placed for ~11 min. Game windows: 2-4 min refreshes exceed 220 s on ~5-15% of cycles, giving the observed 12-15 min median survival. Every re-placement rejoins the back of an 8,500-15,000-contract queue. Funnel: 88,107 intents -> 7,997 orders on 445 (variant,market,side) keys (18 orders/key) -> ~4,400 order-hours -> 1 queue_model fill (sharp_direct). no_watcher's 224 orders/646 rows collapse to 27 keys. (2) Gate (gate.py:119-185): >=150 fill events, >=40 games, both sports, >=80% ws-clean with dirty_minutes=0, Pinnacle CLV lower bound >0, over the whole run. The gate variant sharp_two_sided has 0. Needs ~11.5 fill events per game day to 09-28 (13 game days) or ~6 to mid-October versus 0.33/day observed. Worse: dirty_minutes accrues on quiet books (>120 s without a tape event) across the whole working life including the no_watcher track (order 157: 3,020 of ~4,200 min), so the 80% clean share is unattainable as coded even with fills. (3) Posting 3.4-7c under fair sits ~4.6c under the mid behind ~77x its own size; fills come from level pulls and sweeps, not flow. (4) worst_case_fill=true means the ask later crossed our bid on the counterfactual track, not model pessimism; the policy is the pessimist. (5) Levers: an executor-only stale bound or hold-while-intent-valid (no variant key touched), per-variant cap, fillability ordering, all under a dated Amendment 5. Honest read: the velocity filter plus the cushion on days-out markets make maker fills structurally rare and adverse; the §9.6 dataset goals remain answerable, the go-live gate likely does not.

verified_findings.title: fair_stale compares a pricing-run age against a feed-fetch allowance; the cancel is a lottery every refresh cycle
verified_findings.claim: 97.8% of cancels (7,825/7,997) come from a rule whose 220 s bound was derived from the Odds API featured cadence (120 s) plus the tick budget (100 s), while the quantity it bounds, now - fair_values.created_at, advances only when a tick refreshes Kalshi markets at interval_for's 900/300/120 s cadence plus the tick's own duration (45 s avg, 123 s p95 on 09-10). On a 900 s weekday cadence every order is cancelled at ~200 s and placement is blocked for the remaining ~680 s; in a 120 s window the 2-4 min refresh interval crosses 220 s on roughly one cycle in ten, producing the observed p25 5 min / p50 12.2 min / p75 35 min survival. This is a specification mismatch (F36 as coded), not the strategy's intended behaviour.

verified_findings.recommendation: Dated Amendment 5 (executor rule, not a variant key): either (a) add ExecSettings.fair_stale_s (e.g. 900 s = exec_intent_ttl_s) and evaluate `age > max(stale_s, stale_allowance_s, fair_stale_s)` in plan.py:456, or (b) hold the order while the newest intent inside exec_intent_ttl_s still targets its price and cancel fair_stale only when no intent is inside the TTL. The amendment states the deploy sha and time, the pre-amendment order range (all orders placed before it), tables touched (1, 3, 6; criteria 1-7 counts) and the re-score command (`harness replay --execute` over the last game day under both rules). Correct the phase reports' framing: the cadence is 900/300/120 s by interval_for and the allowance never matched it; stale_s (180) is inert because 220 dominates the max.
corrections: 97.8 % of cancels (7,825/7,997) come from fair_stale, whose 220 s bound (harness/pricing/fair.py:24,30-34: FEATURED_CADENCE_S 120 + tick_budget_s 100, settings.py:26) was designed as a feed-cadence allowance ("independent of the actual tick interval", fair.py:22-24) but is compared by plan.py:446-456 against now - fair_values.created_at (store.py:354-368), a quantity that advances only when a tick refreshes Kalshi markets (tick.py:576-583 gated on cadence.py:16-33 interval_for: 900 s weekday / 300 s weekend / 120 s in-window; pricing only `if summaries`, tick.py:906) plus tick duration (09-10 ok ticks avg 44.4 s, p95 123.1 s). Consequences, evidence-backed: (a) on the 900 s weekday cadence, placement is skipped for roughly 680-725 s of every 900 s cycle because the intent chain checks fair_stale first (plan.py:530-531); (b) resting orders become cancel-eligible ~125-165 s after placement (staleness_at_place p25-p95 57-94 s), but the order chain holds on a dirty/aged book (plan.py:499 before :501, exec_book_max_age_s 120 s), so the cancel fires at the first loop with a live book, giving time-in-book from ~2 min to hours (order 157: 35.3 min with book_dirty on every watch sample; journal 1075: 147 of 150 orders cancelled between 2 min and 2 h 20 min after an 08:04 CT placement; G by day 09-08 p75 62 min / p95 223 min); (c) in the 120 s window the refresh gap (evidence F: median 124 s, p75 150 s, max 243 s) exceeds 220 s on ~2 % of cycles (2/99), so in-window cancels are rarer than the "one in ten" figure and do not by themselves explain the observed p50 12.2 min; the observed survival is the product of the dirty-hold and the fair_stale bound together. The rule is coded exactly as the phase 3 spec (2026-09-07-phase3-paper-execution-design.md:32) specifies; the mismatch is between the F11 allowance's feed-cadence semantics and F36's reuse of it against pricing-run age, which the autopilot flagged as an unanswered strategy question in the phase 4, 4.5 (report line 8) and 5 (report line 11) reports. Severity: material for viability (placement blocked most of weekday daytime), but it is a flagged, spec-consistent design choice awaiting the owner's decision rather than an unintended coding defect.

97.8 % of cancels (7,825/7,997) come from the fair_stale rule (plan.py:446-456), which is implemented exactly as the phase 3 spec (line 30/32) and F36 ruling specify: it bounds now - fair_values.created_at by 220 s, an allowance derived from the Odds API featured cadence (120 s) plus the tick budget (100 s) (fair.py:24, 30-40), while created_at advances only when a tick refreshes Kalshi markets at interval_for's 900/300/120 s cadence (cadence.py:16-33; tick.py:576-583, 906-920) and is stamped with the pricing clock before the commit (journal 17, line 219). The defect is a spec-internal inconsistency (09-06 design line 99: 15-min weekday featured cadence vs fair.py:22-24 "a fixed 120s, independent of the actual tick interval"), not a coding error; the loop detected it on 2026-09-09 (journal 82, line 1075) and escalated it as an owner strategy question in the phase 4.5 (line 8) and phase 5 (line 11) reports, unanswered and absent from phase 6. On a 900 s weekday cadence, placement is blocked for ~680 of every 900 s (intent chain, plan.py:530) and clean-book orders are cancelled ~2-4 min after placement (evidence D4: 09-10 09:00-13:00 CT placed == cancelled hourly; evidence G 09-08 p25 1.3 / p50 4.8 min), but dirty-book orders are held (plan.py:499 precedes :501) and survive across runs (order 157: 35 min on a weekday, book_dirty on all samples), which with the 120 s game-window lottery (2/100 raw intervals > 220 s in evidence F, ~7-9/100 after commit lag and loop period) produces the observed p25 5 / p50 12.2 / p75 35 / p95 147 min. The measured cost is the no_watcher counterfactual: 646 fill rows / 18,512 contracts across 27 of 445 keys versus 1 real queue_model fill. Severity: the single most consequential open strategy decision for the experiment's fill rate, awaiting the owner's choice of cadence or bound; not a critical code defect.

Severity: critical for viability (blocking for the week-1 gate). fair_stale (plan.py:446-456) bounds now - fair_values.created_at with an allowance (fair.py:24-33, 120 + 100 = 220 s) the spec derived for pricing-time feed staleness (phase-3 spec line 7), while fair values refresh only on Kalshi-market ticks at 900/300/120 s (cadence.py:16-33, tick.py:906) plus a 45 s avg / 123 s p95 tick; it produced 7,825 of 7,997 cancels (97.8 %), placed == cancelled through the 09-10 daytime hours, tib p50 12.2 min, and exactly one queue_model-filled order against gate criterion 1's requirement of 150 across 40 games (gate.py:120-125), so no weekly gate in the 3-week experiment can pass under the rule as coded. The per-cycle loss in the 120 s window is 2-6 % of refresh gaps (evidence F: 2/99 > 220 s, 6/99 > 200 s), not one in ten, and quiet-book orders are held by the preceding dirty check (plan.py:496-497) rather than cancelled at ~200 s; the daytime placement block for ~680 s of each 900 s cycle stands. Recommendation as stated (dated Amendment 5, executor rule, EXECUTOR_VERSION bump, replay re-score) should be the first phase 6 item and the phase reports' "15-minute pricing cadence" framing corrected.

verified_findings.title: Gate criterion 1's 80% ws-clean share is unattainable as coded because dirty_minutes accrues on quiet books for the order's whole working life
verified_findings.claim: fill_events requires >=80% of fill-event orders to have book_source='ws' and dirty_minutes=0, but dirty_minutes accrues 15 s per loop whenever the market reads dirty, and a market reads dirty when its own newest tape row is older than exec_book_max_age_s (120 s), which is the normal state of a days-out market; accrual continues after cancel while the no_watcher track is open (working_orders includes nw_done=false). The one fill-event order (157) carries 3,020 dirty minutes of ~4,200 minutes alive; exec.dirty_markets averages 122.8 of ~125 working markets overnight. Even 150 fills would score a ws_clean_share near 0, so criterion 1 fails independently of the fill count.

verified_findings.recommendation: Decide before the Mon 2026-09-14 gate evaluation. Two options: (1) accrual fix (executor, dated note, no criterion text change): accrue dirty_seconds only while the watched track is open (status in OPEN_STATUSES) and only for BookState.dirty or dead_recorder, not for quiet-book age; keep the age-hold for fill simulation; (2) if the age semantics are wanted, the criterion definition must change, which is a dated user decision under invariant 2 and moves criteria_hash. Verify with a query of dirty_minutes over the 224 no_watcher-filled orders before choosing; today the gate variant's share is undefined (n=0) and sharp_direct's is 0/1.
corrections: Gate criterion 1 (harness/report/gate.py:121-125, :274-277; spec 2026-09-07-phase3 §0.7(b) R12) requires >= 80 % of a variant's queue_model fill-event orders to have book_source = 'ws' and dirty_minutes = 0. dirty_seconds accrues exec_period_s = 15 s per loop (loop.py:797-804, settings.py:54, store.py:684-693) for every working_orders row (store.py:324-341: status open/partially_filled OR nw_done = false), so accrual continues after cancel until the no_watcher track closes at expiry or a full nw fill (loop.py:877-880). A market reads dirty when its newest tape row is older than exec_book_max_age_s = 120 s, when a gap is flagged, or when the recorder itself is > 120 s behind (plan.py:246-257, settings.py:66), and overnight 122.8 of 125 (max 125/125 at the 12:30Z heartbeat) working-order markets read dirty with ws.gaps = 0 (evidence D). The one fill-event order (157) carries 3,020 dirty minutes over a ~3,185-minute working window (placed 09-08 14:36Z, watched track cancelled 35 min later, nw track closed 09-10 ~19:30-19:42Z on a full 87-contract nw fill), i.e. ~95 % of its working life and >= 2,985 minutes after cancel. Because the nw window runs to kickoff-10 min and 92 % of orders are placed > 24 h before kickoff (evidence G), a fill event with dirty_minutes = 0 is nearly unattainable as coded; the per-order dirty_minutes distribution was not pulled (n = 1 direct), so "ws_clean_share near 0 even at 150 fills" is a strong inference rather than a measurement. The code matches the spec (line 33: dirty_minutes accumulates with no open-only bound), so this is a criterion-design defect that R1 (roadmap.md:49) reserves for a dated user decision, not an autopilot fix.

Gate criterion 1's 80% ws-clean share (harness/report/gate.py:122-125, :274-277) is unattainable as specified and coded: dirty_minutes accrues 15 s per loop (loop.py:799-803, store.py:684-693) for every working order, cancelled ones included (store.py:324-349, nw_done=false), whenever the ticker's newest tape row is older than exec_book_max_age_s=120 s (plan.py:246-257, book.py:283/578-585, settings.py:66), and days-out markets get no WS deltas or REST ladders in that window (cadence.py:67-77 refreshes only same-day markets inside [-4h,+3h] of a kickoff). Evidence: exec.dirty_markets avg 122.8 / max 125 over 6 h with ws.gaps 0 and heartbeat book_dirty_markets 125 at open_orders 0; the one fill-event order (157) carries dirty_seconds 181,200 (3,020 min) over a working life of ~3,186 min (placed 2026-09-08 14:36:47Z, nw track closed 2026-09-10 19:42:20Z when nw_filled_contracts reached 87), i.e. ~95% of loops dirty, not "3,020 of ~4,200". Because 92% of orders are placed >24 h before kickoff (evidence G) and expiry runs to kickoff-10 min, the clean-eligible population is under 1% of placements, so ws_clean_share will sit far below 0.80 at any fill count and criterion 1 fails independently of the 150-fill count. Attribution: gate.py faithfully implements spec §0.7(b) line 13 ("dirty_minutes = 0", R12); the unattainability comes from the unreconciled interaction of two same-review rulings, F12/R12 (80% non-dirty, adversarial review lines 22, 195, 270) and F36 (per-ticker 120 s age reads dirty, line 46; spec line 33), while verify.md:392-394 shows the intended semantic was per-fill ("a queue-model fill attributed to a window in which the book was dirty ... must be 0"), not lifetime dirty minutes. Severity: high, not critical. GateResult.passed is already False by construction in phase 3 (gate.py:13-15), so there is no operational effect now; the consequence is a mis-scored criterion 1 in every weekly gate row from Mon 2026-09-14 and at the mid-October go-live review, and since gate criteria are invariants (roadmap.md line 89) the redefinition (e.g. per-fill clean-book test, or dirty minutes over the open life only, or a gap-only definition of dirty) requires a dated user decision and should be escalated as a gate before 09-14.

Severity major (not critical), question phase6/viability: gate criterion 1's 80 % ws-clean share is unattainable as coded because dirty_seconds accrues on quiet-book age (>120 s) for the order's whole no_watcher life (loop.py:799-804, plan.py:246-257, store.py:324-349, :684-693; order 157: 3,020 dirty min of ~3,170; exec.dirty_markets 122.8/125 with ws.gaps 0), so a dated user decision on dirty semantics (accrual only while the watched track is open and only for gap/dead-recorder dirtiness, or a criterion amendment moving criteria_hash) is required within the 3-week window; it is major rather than critical because the Monday 2026-09-14 gate fails criterion 1 on fill count first (n = 0 gate variant, n = 1 sharp_direct vs 150), nothing irreversible occurs before the decision, and the fill drought dominates viability.

verified_findings.title: At the observed rate the go-live gate cannot be reached by 2026-09-28 or mid-October; the dataset goals can
verified_findings.claim: The gate variant sharp_two_sided (GATE_VARIANT=sharp_two_sided on the NAS) has 0 queue_model fills; sharp_direct has 1 in 3 days (0.33/day). Reaching 150 fill events across >=40 games needs ~11.5 fill events and ~3 new games per game day over the 13 game days to the week-3 confirmation on Mon 2026-09-28, or ~6 per game day over ~25 game days to mid-October, a 20-35x gap. The week-2 selection frozen Mon 2026-09-21 (R7) is the H2 mispricing-map cell selection from gap snapshots, and criterion 4 (markout) is anchored on nw_fill, so the spec §9.6 week-3 success (three map cells, convergence lag, adverse-selection estimate) is answerable from snapshots and no_watcher markouts without watched fills; the go-live gate is not.

Severity MAJOR (not critical): criterion 1 (150 queue_model fills, >= 40 games, gate variant sharp_two_sided currently at 0) is the binding constraint on the mid-October go-live gate, not the 09-28 week-3 confirmation, which is already scoped to the §9.6 dataset deliverables; the observed 0.33/day is a pre-weekend number, so the owner's action in the next 1-2 weeks is to read the Mon 09-14 fill count from the first weekend tape and then answer the carried fair_stale/cadence question (phase 4.5 report line 8), preferring an exec-level or stale-allowance change over a variant YAML edit, which would reset the gate variant's count under invariant 1.

verified_findings.title: no_watcher over-counts by ~8x; the honest rest-to-expiry counterfactual is ~27 filled keys in 3 days, not 224 orders
verified_findings.claim: Each of the 7,997 orders runs its own no_watcher track from placement to expiry against the same prints, so the 18 overlapping orders per (variant, market, side) key each get filled by the same tape: 224 orders / 646 rows / 18,512 contracts collapse to 27 distinct keys. Under a rest-until-expiry policy there is one order per key, so the counterfactual fill count is ~27 fill events per 3 days pooled across three variants (~9/day; per-variant split unverified), 27x the observed 1 but still 2-3x short of the ~11.5/day the gate variant alone needs by 09-28, before any weekend uplift.

Evidence note 10 shows those fills land on only 27 of 445 distinct keys (7,997 orders, ~18 per key overall; the number of orders carrying no_watcher fills is unverified, since the brief's 224 counts orders with any fill method). 27 filled keys to date is therefore a better proxy for the rest-to-expiry fill count than 646 rows, and it is 27x the one observed queue_model fill (order 157). verified_findings.title: Levers that raise fills without breaking the pre-registration, with what each touches
verified_findings.claim: Six levers exist; none needs a variant file or a gate definition. (L1) Leave orders resting until expiry, i.e. delete the fair_stale cancel and let the watched track equal no_watcher: plan.py:501-502 and :530-531; ExecSettings/EXECUTOR_VERSION bump; invariants 1 and 2 untouched; expected ~27 filled keys per 3 days pooled (V4). (L2) Re-price instead of cancel on fair_stale: hold while the newest intent within exec_intent_ttl_s (900 s) targets the resting price, cancel only when no intent is inside the TTL or the newest fair says edge_decay/venue_move; same files; keeps F36's safety at a 15-min horizon. (L3) Executor-only stale bound fair_stale_s (e.g. 600-900 s) in ExecSettings; smallest diff. (L4) Per-variant capacity cap (settings.py:64, plan.py:589-613). (L5) Capacity ordering by fillability instead of descending edge (plan.py:602-604). (L6) New pre-registered ids (join-the-bid, near-kickoff) by dated amendment, executed beside the frozen seven. L1-L5 change the paper trader's behaviour under the pre-registration, so each carries Amendment 5 with the deploy sha/time, the pre-amendment order range, tables and criteria touched (1, 3, 6; criteria 1-7 counts) and the replay re-score command; stale_s and every other variant key stay as registered.

corrections: Six levers exist; L1-L5 need no variant file or gate-definition change, L6 does. (L1) Leave orders resting until expiry by deleting the fair_stale cancel (plan.py:501-502, :530-531; ExecSettings/EXECUTOR_VERSION bump; invariants 1 and 2 untouched). The watched track then approximates no_watcher (168 non-fair_stale cancels remain: reprice 129, signal_rejected 29, venue_move 10). Pooled no_watcher fills reached 27 of 445 keys over 3 days (evidence G, note 10), but that is an upper bound for L1 alone: the shared exec_max_open_orders 150 (settings.py:64) was binding in 41 of 53 hours (note 4) and orders resting to expiry (92 % placed >24 h pre-kick, note 9) would saturate it on the first daytime tick, so L1 only approaches 27 when paired with L4/L5 or a higher cap. (L2) Re-price instead of cancel on fair_stale: hold while the newest intent within exec_intent_ttl_s (900 s; loop.py:406 is the only consumer) targets the resting price; cancel when no intent is inside the TTL or the newest fair says edge_decay/venue_move; same files. (L3) Executor-only fair_stale_s (600-900 s) in ExecSettings; smallest diff; saves the daytime late-refresh cancels (fair refreshes every 1-3.5 min on game night, evidence F) but not the overnight ones (no fair_values 01:30-07:30 CT). (L4) Per-variant capacity cap (settings.py:64, plan.py:589-613; D10 is a §9 model ruling). (L5) Capacity ordering by fillability (plan.py:602-604). (L6) New pre-registered ids (join-the-bid, near-kickoff) require new files under harness/variants/ and raising MAX_SECONDARY from 6 (already 1 primary + 6 secondaries, variants.py:59-60,145-148), both invariant 1 (roadmap.md:85-86): a gate, not a loop ruling. L1-L5 each carry Amendment 5 with the four elements enumerated for Amendment 4 at phase4 spec:95 (deploy sha/time, pre-amendment order range, tables 1/3/6 and criteria 1-7 counts, replay re-score command); stale_s and every other variant key stay as registered.

Four executor-only levers (L1 delete the fair_stale cancel/skip at plan.py:501-502 and :530-531; L3 an executor stale bound in ExecSettings; L4 a per-variant share of exec_max_open_orders; L5 capacity ordering by fillability instead of descending edge at plan.py:602-604) need no variant file or gate-definition change and would carry Amendment 5 (deploy sha/time, pre-amendment order range, tables 1/3/6 and criteria 1-7 counts, re-score via harness replay --execute, which writes replay=true rows only). Their fill effect is bounded, not estimated, by the no_watcher counterfactual: 27 of 445 keys pooled across three variants over 3 days (~9 per variant), a ceiling because the no_watcher track ignores every watcher cancel and L1 keeps venue_move/edge_decay/reprice/signal_rejected; L1 without L4/L5 freezes the 150 shared slots on far-out orders (41 % placed >72 h to kickoff, cap already binding 41/53 h), so its net effect on fills is undetermined. L2 (hold while an intent is inside the 900 s TTL) and L3 below ~900 s + tick duration still cancel every daytime cycle because pricing runs every 900 s and intents are TTL-bounded at 900 s; a bound must exceed the cadence or exec_intent_ttl_s must move with it. L6 (new ids) needs new YAML files and a MAX_SECONDARY raise above 6, both invariant-1 items and therefore a user gate. The staleness bound itself is a user decision already carried in the phase 4.5 and 5 reports, so L1-L3 are user-authorised amendments, not loop rulings. None of L1-L6 plausibly reaches criterion 1 (>= 150 queue_model fill events across >= 40 games per variant over the run) on the observed tape.

Severity important (bordering critical for question 2): with 7,825 of 7,997 paper orders cancelled fair_stale at a 220 s bound and one queue_model fill in three days against a gate criterion of >= 150 filled orders, the owner's decision on which of L1-L5 to ship (with Amendment 5) before Sat 2026-09-12 determines whether weeks 2-3 of the experiment produce any fill data at all; the seven phase 6 items as written do not touch this. Two precisions: L3 alone leaves overnight orders (no fair_values 01:30-07:30 CT) cancelled, so its yield is materially below the 27-key L1 counterfactual; and L6 does add a variant YAML (additive, allowed by invariant 1), so 'none needs a variant file' should read 'L1-L5 need no variant file'.

title: Why fair_stale dominates: pricing cadence and budgets
summary: (1) Effective stale bound is max(stale_s 180, allowance 220) = 220 s on every order (evidence G: allow p25=p95=220), so the variant's 180 never binds. Fair_ts is the pricing timestamp (store.py:357, fair.py created_at=pricing_now), refreshed only on ticks that refresh Kalshi markets (tick.py:904), which run at interval_for: 900 s weekday daytime, 300 s weekend off-window, 120 s nominal in a game window, none 01:00-08:00 CT (cadence.py:16-33). Measured in-window (evidence F, 94 gaps): mean 137 s, p50 126, p75 152, max 326; 6/94 (6.4 %) exceed 220 s. Daytime: 900-930 s = 4.1x the bound; the executor can rest orders at most 220 of every 900 s (<=24 % duty cycle), and every order is cancelled before the next pricing (D4 09-10 09:00-13:00 placed == cancelled; journal 82). (2) Attribution: the allowance constant FEATURED_CADENCE_S=120 (fair.py:24) contradicts its own definition ("feed's configured fetch interval + tick budget", Amendment 2) and causes ~54 % of fair_stale cancels (all off-window ones); tick-duration variance on the 30 s heartbeat causes the in-window >220 s gaps (~46 %, a NAS + serial-tick effect); pricing-budget exhaustion contributes 0 (Stage 1 always runs, pipeline.py:174); credits contribute 0 (1.2-7k/day used vs ~166k/day pro-rata of 5M; featured costs 6 credits/tick). (3) The 15-min cadence is the 2026-09-06 design spec (line 75), coded 6dcb552 under the 100k tier; U1 (2026-09-07) kept it "unchanged"; not a NAS choice. (4) The report's "cadence or bound, your call" framing hides a spec inconsistency and is not symmetric: the bound fix is pricing code + a dated amendment (no invariant hit; variant YAMLs untouched); the cadence fix is cadence.py constants with ~2.5x pricing ticks and DB growth. (5) Bugs: the allowance constant; dirty-hold ordering delays the cancel to the next book event (the sole fill, order 157, exists only because of it); cross-sport repricing masks 15-min-old odds; 01:04 CT nightly wipe.

corrections: stale_allowance_s() (harness/pricing/fair.py:23,35) returns a fixed FEATURED_CADENCE_S(120)+tick_budget_s(100)=220 s for every featured row regardless of the cadence in force (evidence G: 220 on all 7,825 fair_stale orders), while outside a game window the featured-odds fetch, the Kalshi-markets fetch and therefore pricing (tick.py:523/581/904) run every 900 s on weekdays and 300 s on weekends (cadence.py:16-33; evidence E: 73 priced ticks on Tue 09-08). Each weekday-daytime fair value is therefore fresh for only 220 of every 900 s (24 %); for the remaining ~680 s placement is skipped (plan.py:529-530) and any resting order whose book is clean is cancelled fair_stale (plan.py:500-501). Orders on dirty books (plan.py:498-499; thin daytime books older than exec_book_max_age_s=120 s) are held rather than cancelled, so the cancel is deferred, not guaranteed within a cycle (journal 82: 150 placed 08:04 CT, 147 cancelled fair_stale between 08:06 and 10:24 CT; order 157 lived 35 min; G tib p50 12.2 min, p95 147 min; D3 open_orders avg 147.8 in the 09-08 15:00 CT hour). The mismatch explains the bulk of out-of-window fair_stale cancels (≈65 %, roughly 5,100 of 7,825 from D4 hourly buckets: 09-08 1,253, 09-09 ≈1,740, 09-10 ≈1,820, 09-11 288); the remaining ≈35 % occurred inside 120-s windows (Wed 09-09 and Thu 09-10 evenings, incl. the phase 5 report's 1,466) where the 220 s allowance matches design but in-window fair gaps still reach 232-243 s (evidence F). The 120 s figure is frozen by preregistration Amendment 2 (line 96: allowance = '120 + tick_budget_s' for featured) and mirrors the 2026-09-07 stale_s 90→180 amendment (design spec line 182); neither was revisited for the 900-s daytime cadence, and the 4.5/5 reports (line 8 / line 11) carry only a generic '15-minute pricing cadence' question to the user without naming the allowance mismatch.

stale_allowance_s() (harness/pricing/fair.py:24,35) returns a fixed 220 s for featured rows while the weekday-daytime pricing cadence is 900 s (cadence.py:33; tick.py:523,581,904), so every daytime fair value is fair_stale for ~680 s of each 900 s cycle and resting orders on CLEAN books are cancelled ~220 s after each pricing run; orders on dirty books (107-123 of ~135 markets, journal 101) are held by plan.py:499 ahead of the stale check and cancelled fair_stale only when the book wakes (journal 82: 147 cancels spread 08:06-10:24 CT; brief: fair_stale time-in-book median 12.2 min, mean 33.7 min), so the '24 % duty cycle' figure is unsupported. The constant is deliberate and preregistered (fair.py:22-23; Amendment 2, preregistration.md:96; F36 ruling, adversarial review line 46) and the resulting churn has been escalated to the user as an unanswered strategy question in the phase 4, 4.5 (line 8) and 5 (line 11) reports, so this is a known, deferred user decision rather than a hidden defect; it explains the daytime share of the 7,825 fair_stale cancels, but the in-window churn (>=1,466 on 2026-09-10 16:25-20:35 CT at the 120 s cadence) is driven by pricing-gap jitter on the swapping NAS (journal 101; tick.py:40-44), and the daytime/in-window split is unverified (no evidence.md). The remedy consistent with spec §6.2 (line 182, 180 s tradeable bound) is raising the daytime cadence in cadence.py:31-33 (credit headroom: 4,986,353/5,000,000), not raising the allowance to track a 900 s poll; either change alters the preregistered not_stale label (strategy/run.py:270) and needs a dated amendment. Severity: high, known, blocked on the user's answer.

Severity major (not critical): the 220 s allowance versus the 900 s weekday and 300 s weekend cadence is a genuine rule defect that guarantees fair_stale before the next pricing run outside game windows and, with the 30-queue_model-fill H1 floor (prereg line 71) against 2 fills in 3 days, is the single most important phase 6 item and must be amended before week 2; but it is not the whole story, because roughly half the cancels occur in-window (D4 09-10 16:00-20:00 CT) where the recommended fix is a no-op and the cause is tick overrun plus executor loop latency against the same 220 s (journal 57, evidence F, D2), and only 27 of 445 order keys fill even uncancelled (evidence #10), so the fix should be allowance = cadence_in_force + tick_budget_s plus overrun slack, and the owner should expect a fill sample in the dozens, not a changed verdict on edge.

verified_findings.title: The dirty-hold rule delays the fair_stale cancel to the next book event; the experiment's only real fill is an artefact of that delay
verified_findings.claim: plan.py checks market.dirty before _fair_stale and returns None (hold) on a dirty book, where dirty includes 'no orderbook event in 120 s' (book_max_age_s); on the illiquid days-out markets the executor trades (~123 dirty markets at any time), a stale order is held silently until the first book event, so median time-in-book (12.2 min) measures book silence, not fair freshness, and order 157 (the single queue_model fill) was filled 30 min after its fair went stale only because its book was dirty the whole time.
verified_findings.question: viability
evidence: harness/execution/plan.py:499-501: 'if market.dirty(now, s): return None' precedes '_fair_stale -> Cancel'; plan.py:230-243 dirty = book_dirty or book.dirty or book_age_s > book_max_age_s; harness/execution/book.py:578-585 book_age_s from the newest applied row

evidence G order 157: placed 2026-09-08 14:36:47Z (staleness_at_place 53 s, allowance 220), watch samples book_dirty = t from 14:37 to 14:57Z, queue_model fills at 15:07:15Z (38.92 contracts), cancelled fair_stale 15:12:06Z; day cadence 900 s (journal 57: real ticks 14:01, 14:16Z ...), so fair was stale from ~14:40Z

evidence G: fair_stale time-in-book p25 5.0 / p50 12.2 / p75 35.3 / p95 147 min against a 220 s bound; brief: exec.dirty_markets ~123, open_orders avg 100-150 in daytime hours (D3) despite a 24 % duty cycle
harness/execution/loop.py:432 and 450: fills are simulated before plan_actions each step, so the un-dirtying event's prints are credited before the cancel
verified_findings.recommendation: Report time-in-book split by 'held dirty' vs 'clean' minutes (dirty_seconds exists on orders) and state in the week-1 report that fill 157 occurred past the stale bound. Decide explicitly whether a silent book should hold a stale order (today it does, for hours); if the rule's intent is 'never rest on a value we cannot defend', evaluate _fair_stale before the dirty-hold, or exclude 'silent > 120 s' from dirty (a quiet book is not a broken tape). Any change is an executor-rule change: EXECUTOR_VERSION bump and a dated amendment.
corrections: plan.py:499-502 checks market.dirty before _fair_stale and returns None (hold) on a dirty book, where dirty includes no orderbook row applied in 120 s (plan.py:246-257, settings.py:66), and loop.py:799-804 also skips fill simulation while dirty, so a stale-fair order on a silent book is held (recorded only as dirty_seconds and watch-sample book_dirty, never as an order event) until the next book event, whose prints are credited (loop.py:432) before the cancel is planned (loop.py:450). Order 157, the single queue_model fill, shows this: its fair went stale at ~14:39:34Z (placed 14:36:47Z, staleness 53 s, allowance 220), its watch samples read book_dirty = t from 14:37 to at least 14:57Z, dirty_seconds 3020 s covers its whole 2,119 s residence, and it filled at 15:07:15Z and was cancelled fair_stale 291 s later; it survived past its stale bound only because of the dirty hold, though whether the fair was continuously stale for the full 28 min (versus re-priced by the 14:46Z or 15:01Z tick) is unverified. At night ~123 of the executor's markets are dirty (evidence: 6-h avg 122.8, heartbeat 125); the daytime share and the aggregate dirty_seconds across the 7,825 fair_stale cancels are not in evidence, so how much of the 12.2 min median time-in-book is book silence versus late fair refreshes (controller note 1; 09-08 p50 4.8 min sits near allowance minus staleness) remains unquantified.

plan.py:499-501 holds an open order on a dirty book before the fair_stale check, and loop.py:799-802 skips both fill tracks while dirty; dirty (plan.py:230-243) is the per-sid seq-gap flag, the dead-recorder flag, or book_age_s > 120 s. This is the spec's rule (phase3 design spec line 33; plan line 192; tests/test_exec_plan.py:234-250) and is instrumented (dirty_seconds per order, book_dirty_markets, Skip(book_dirty)), so a stale order on a dirty book is held by design until the book reads clean (a clean snapshot after a gap, or a book event inside 120 s), and the cancel then lands in the same step as any fills the tape produced meanwhile (loop.py:432/450). Consequences: (a) fair_stale time-in-book is not a clean measure of fair freshness, but the evidence does not show the hold is its main driver: per-day p50 is 4.8 min on 09-08 (15-min daytime fair cadence, journal 57) and 15.5 min on 09-10 (game night with fair refreshes every 1-3.5 min, evidence F), which points to fair-refresh cadence; a per-order join of hold time vs time-in-book is needed and dirty_seconds cannot supply it because it keeps accumulating after cancel while nw_done = false (order 157: 181,200 s vs a 2,119-s open window). (b) Order 157, the only queue_model fill, survived its first stale window only because its book was gap-dirty (BookState.dirty, loop.py:1113) from 14:37Z to at least 14:57Z; app-exec was then restarted by the 1911a4f deploy at 15:02-15:06Z (journal 59), the 15:07:15Z prints were credited and the fair_stale cancel written in the 15:12:06Z step. The fill itself required the 6,401-contract queue to collapse to 0 with 25 contracts printing ahead (recovery clamp loop.py:829-835 or cancels-ahead attribution; unverified which), so it is an artefact of the gap-dirty stretch plus the queue rule, not of the 120-s age rule. Whether the fair was refreshed by the 14:46Z/15:01Z ticks is unverified (staleness_at_place 53 s is the feed's pricing-time staleness, not the fair's age at placement). The ~123 dirty markets figure is the night-time nw-tracked set; the daytime dirty share of resting orders is unverified. Severity: important as a measurement caveat for the fill-realism and fair_stale tables, with the design question (hold vs cancel on a dirty book) belonging to the owner alongside the phase 4.5 report's unanswered cadence question.

Severity: important (viability, decision-blocking before the 2026-09-14 gate). The dirty-hold at plan.py:499-501 defers the fair_stale cancel until the next book event, so on the ~123 quiet days-out markets the 220 s stale bound is unenforced (time-in-book p50 12.2 min, p95 147 min, n = 7,825) and the experiment's only queue_model fill (order 157, filled ~28 min past its stale bound while book_dirty = t throughout) exists only because of that hold; additionally, because cancelled orders stay in the working set until nw_done and dirty_seconds accrues post-cancel (store.py:323-336, loop.py:797-803; order 157 = 181,200 s dirty vs 35 min in book), the gate's criterion 1 clean-share test (dirty_minutes = 0 on >= 80 % of fill events, gate.py:120-125/274-277) is structurally unattainable on these markets, so the week-1 report must label fill 157 as past-bound, report held-dirty vs clean time from order_watch_samples.book_dirty (not dirty_seconds), and the owner must decide the cadence / stale bound / dirty-hold ordering as a dated executor-rule amendment with an EXECUTOR_VERSION bump before the gate is read.

verified_findings.title: The phase 4.5/5 report mis-frames a spec inconsistency as a symmetric user strategy choice and never quantified it

corrections: The phase 4.5 and phase 5 reports (2026-09-09-phase4.5.md:8, 2026-09-10-phase5.md:11) frame the fair_stale churn as a symmetric user choice ("whether the cadence or the staleness bound moves; the loop will not change either"), which is defensible on the letter (U1 at roadmap.md:37 pins the featured cadence; Amendment 2 pins the allowance at "120 + tick_budget_s") but is really a spec-internal inconsistency the loop has precedent to amend: the phase 3 design spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-07-phase3-paper-execution-design.md:7, implemented by Amendment 2) defines stale_allowance_s as "the feed's configured fetch interval ... plus the tick budget" yet fixes featured at 120 s, while the recorder's featured daytime tick is 900 s (cadence.py:33; journal 57/64) and fair.py:22-24 concedes the 120 s is "independent of the actual tick interval"; no roadmap invariant (roadmap.md:85-103) covers FEATURED_CADENCE_S, tick_budget_s or ExecSettings (only stale_s in harness/variants/*.yaml under invariant 1); and Amendment 4 (preregistration.md:117-121; journal 57 -> 61 D8 -> 63, 09:55-11:44 CT on 2026-09-08) changed price_budget_s 20 -> 45 by a controller-ruled dated amendment with no user gate. The reports under-quantified the question: phase 5 gave only the 1,466-order churn figure and omitted that fair_stale is 97.9 % of all cancels (7,825 of 7,993), that the 220 s allowance is a quarter of the 900 s daytime cadence, and that the sole real (queue_model) fill, order 157, was a worst_case_fill = true fill while the 646 no_watcher fill rows are counterfactual. Note: "24 % duty cycle" is a derived ceiling, not an observed one; measured fair_stale cancels sit a median 12.2 min (avg 33.7 min) in book because fair_ts refreshes on each re-pricing, so the operative mechanism is markets missing re-pricing for > 220 s, not a fixed 220 s order life. The "order of magnitude in cost" contrast is unverified (roughly 7.5x featured credits, trivial against the 5M tier).

The phase 4.5/5 report (2026-09-09-phase4.5.md:8; 2026-09-10-phase5.md:11) presents the fair_stale churn as a symmetric user choice between "the cadence or the staleness bound" when the two levers are not symmetric in governance: the featured cadence is pinned by user decision U1 ("featured cadence unchanged", roadmap.md:37; Decisions are gate-protected user text, roadmap.md:80-82), so declining to move it is correct; the staleness bound is loop-authored (FEATURED_CADENCE_S = 120 "independent of the actual tick interval", harness/pricing/fair.py:22-24; F36 rule, adversarial review line 46; Amendments 2 and 4 recorded by the controller without a user decision, preregistration.md:96 and journal 63) and could have been moved or at least recommended by dated amendment. The report also mislabels the mechanism as a "15-minute pricing cadence" (fair_ts = fair_values.created_at, store.py:357; in-window refreshes every 1-3.5 min and 281/243 priced ticks on 09-09/09-10, evidence.md:965 and E section), gives raw counts (1,466 -> 150; 150/147 in journal 82) but not the decision-relevant figures (7,825 of 7,997 cancels = 98 %, evidence.md:732; one queue_model fill, order 157, evidence.md:739-745; pricing budget exhausted on 45 % of 09-10 ticks, evidence.md:966; a 120 s weekday featured cadence costs ~7.5x credits, ~14k/day, inside the U1 band), offers no recommendation despite the user's standing "recommend, ask only operational questions" position (memory strategy-trust-model.md), and mis-cites its origin as the phase 4 report (that file has no fair_stale text; the question is from journal 82, 2026-09-09 10:56 CT). Unverified: the reviewer's "24 % duty cycle" (220/900) applies only to weekday hours with no event inside 36 h, and "order of magnitude in cost" is not established for either lever.

Severity important (upgrade candidate to the review's lead viability finding): the executor's fair_stale rule uses a featured-feed allowance of 220 s (fair.py:24,35: 120 + tick_budget_s) against a recorder featured cadence of 900 s on weekday daytime (cadence.py:33), so an order placed >24 h before kickoff (92 % of the 7,997) can rest only ~24 % of each pricing cycle; this, not edge, cancelled 7,825/7,997 (97.8 %) of all paper orders (median 12.2 min in book, one real fill), kept the 150-order cap binding 41/53 hours, and is why the owner sees one open position. The phase 4.5/5 reports posed it twice as a symmetric 'your call' with no diagnostic numbers, despite the journal 63 precedent of a dated pricing-code amendment; it must be resolved before the Mon 2026-09-14 gate evaluation or week 1's fill data is an artifact. Present Option C (executor-only max age in ExecSettings, labels and criterion 8 untouched) as the default and Option B (allowance = cadence in force + tick budget) as the alternative, noting B changes the not_stale label per Amendment 2; separately, in-window churn (fair values refreshing every 1-3.5 min per evidence F) is driven by 50-115 s executor loops and belongs to the NAS/Mac mini question, not this lever.

refuted_findings.title: Odds API credits are not the constraint: the recorder uses 1-4 % of the 5M tier's pro-rata budget and the 15-min cadence's credit rationale expired at U1
refuted_findings.claim: The featured fetch pair costs 6 credits per tick; the 900 s daytime cadence was coded on 2026-09-06 under the 100k-credit tier, and U1 (2026-09-07) raised the tier to 5M while explicitly keeping the featured cadence unchanged; a 120 s featured cadence from 08:00 to 01:00 would cost about 3,060 credits/day against a pro-rata allowance of ~166k/day, so credits do not justify the current cadence, whereas NAS load and database growth do bound the cadence option.
reasons: evidence: The quantitative half of the claim verifies; the historical half (the title's "credit rationale expired at U1") is contradicted by the record. VERIFIED: (1) git show 6dcb552 (2026-09-06 12:29:30 -0500) creates harness/recorder/cadence.py with interval_for returning None (01:00-08:00) / 20 / 120 / 300 / 900, and alternates 120-inside-3h / 900-otherwise; design spec 2026-09-06 §4.1 Recorder-tick row reads "5 min all day Sat/Sun; 15 min otherwise; none 01:00-08:00 CT". (was 900)`; roadmap.md:37 U1 says "alternates cadence 900 s → 120 s ... (featured cadence unchanged)". Current settings.py:44-51 still 5_000_000 / 120 / 120 / 36. (5) journal.md:1111 (entry 86, 2026-09-09 14:35 CT): "about 1,870 used in 24 h (a Wednesday on the 15-minute weekday cadence), at the lower edge of the 2,000-170,000 band" verbatim; roadmap.md:99 invariant 7 names "the Odds API credits-per-day band"; verify.md:417 defines the band as 2,000-170,000 after U1, so 3,060 + alternates sits inside it. (6) evidence.md section C: signals 14,649,311 rows / 8828 MB, fair_values 2,323,192 / 1513 MB, db.growth_gb_per_day 8.94; section E: 243 priced ticks on 09-10; sample run 10445 gaps 3929 with per-variant rejected 3,741-3,929 (two-sided 7,730), consistent with ~4k gap snapshots and 7 x ~4k signals per tick; journal line 449 shows 2,626 featured fair_values rows on run 2322. REFUTED: "the 900 s daytime cadence was coded on 2026-09-06 under the 100k-credit tier" and "the 15-min cadence's credit rationale expired at U1". (2) The material half ('NAS binds') is already established: pricing.budget_exhausted on 109/243 priced ticks 09-10 (45 %, evidence E) against the phase 6 item 4 10 % trigger, executor p95 101-115 s in the 18:00-19:00 CT hours (evidence D2), roadmap fixes 31/34. (4) Storage is overstated as a bound: signals ~2.2->5.5 GB/day is dwarfed by the tape (17 GB in the one-week orderbook partition, evidence C) and the U3 ceiling is 2 TB against 47 GB. Keep the one operational nugget (cadence.py's constants are code, not settings) as info.

title: Fill model and execution realism
summary: (1) Bias: the queue model is net OPTIMISTIC, and the one money fill is an artifact. Order 157 (38.92 of 38.92 queue_model contracts, the only open position, the -17.68 ledger) was produced by the gap-recovery branch (loop.py:828-836): queue cut to the HEAD book's resting size (25, post-trade) and cursor jumped to head, but the print watermark was not moved (R10's branch at :823 does move it), so 63.92 contracts of prints already reflected in that book were replayed against it; traded_at_price 63.92 with zero delta offset proves the deltas were skipped. Two further optimistic mechanics: deltas-before-prints at equal ts double-counts each new-max print (fills.py:44-47; 196/196 fixture prints share the ms with their delta), bounded by the largest print; and late joiners' cancels are credited as ahead of us (fills.py:307-320). Pessimistic offsets (join behind all, late REST prints skipped) are smaller. no_watcher:queue_model = 646:2 rows, 18,512:38.92 contracts. (2) Yes, structurally: fair_stale at 220 s (plan.py:456) plus a 2-15 min pricing cadence gives a median 12.2 min life; every re-place rejoins the back of an 8.5k-15k queue (loop.py:1009). Even the never-cancel track fills on 27/445 keys, and its 18,512 contracts is a union over ~18 overlapping tracks per key, not what one resting order yields. (3) Held orders count before any intent (plan.py:590-609): earlier low-edge orders block later high-edge ones; bound 41/53 h. apply_caps false disables per_game, daily and max_open (per-bet is clamped at sizing, run.py:322); README:71 and prereg:14 disclose it, but the gate variant rests ~95 orders vs max_open 25 and the same code runs live. (4) Watched track simulates to `now`, not `min(now, expiry)`, while a lagging ticker withholds Expire: post-kickoff prints can fill a pre-game order (loop.py:852 vs :867, plan.py:492). (5) Ranked below.

verified_findings.title: Deltas-before-prints at equal timestamp double-counts the first (and each new-max) at-price print
verified_findings.claim: fills.py:44-47 orders deltas before prints at equal ts, but the per-price accumulator (traded_at_price) only explains a delta AFTER the print has been applied. With delta first, cancels = max(0, |delta| - traded) treats the trade's own book change as a cancel, then the print consumes the queue again. On the committed tape fixture every one of 196 prints shares the exact millisecond with its matching delta (0 before, 0 after), and both streams carry the venue's ts_ms (ws_sink.py:125, :159), so the tie-break applies to every WS print. tests/test_fills.py:191-201 pins the wrong outcome (queue 5, print 3 + delta -3 at one ts asserts fill 1 / queue 0; the physical answer is fill 0 / queue 2, which the test's own comment describes under print-first). The overshoot is bounded by the largest at-price hitting print per order (25-160 contracts on this tape), i.e. ~0.2-3 % of a 5k-15k queue, and the dangling accumulator then absorbs a genuine cancel of the same size later.

verified_findings.recommendation: Apply prints before deltas at equal ts (the accumulator then explains the delta as traded, not cancelled) and invert the test's expectation; re-run the chunking-invariance and fixture tests. Small in magnitude today, but it is the core arithmetic and every replay/re-score inherits it.
corrections: fills.py:47 orders deltas before prints at equal ts (sort key at :253-271), but the per-price accumulator traded_at_price only explains a delta after the print has been applied (:290-294 vs :307-320). With delta first, cancels = max(0, |delta| - traded) treats the trade's own book change as a cancel and the print then consumes the queue again; the cumulative overshoot equals the running maximum at-price hitting print size per order, and a later genuine cancel of up to that size is silently absorbed (verified by running simulate_fills: queue 1000 with same-ts pairs 50/30/80 -> 760 vs physical 840; a further genuine -80 leaves 760). Every one of the 196 prints on the committed fixture shares the exact millisecond with its matching delta (0 ms offset, all source ws), and ws_sink.py:125/:159 stamp both streams from the venue ts_ms, so the tie-break applies to every WS print. tests/test_fills.py:191-201 pins the wrong outcome (queue 5, print 3 + delta -3 asserts fill 1 / queue 0; the physical answer is fill 0 / queue 2, which the test comment itself describes under print-first). The code follows spec §2 line 42 ("prints after deltas at equal ts"), which contradicts the F1 rule it was meant to implement (adversarial review F1: print consumes the queue, then the delta is charged to the accumulator), so the fix is a spec amendment plus a one-line swap and test correction. Magnitude: the error is optimistic (queue shortened early) and bounded by the largest at-price hitting print seen per order; the fixture cannot size it for in-band orders (its prints are all at yes 0.02/0.03) and recorded queue_ahead_at_place medians are ~1.7k-2.8k (p75 ~6.8k-8k), so the percentage impact is unverified. Paper impact to date is small (one queue_model-filled order), but the bias is in the direction that inflates the gate's fill count.

fills.py:44-47 orders deltas before prints at equal ts, but the per-price accumulator (traded_at_price) can only explain a delta after its print has been credited (fills.py:12-15 docstring; F1 ruling text 'attributed to trades first'). Delta-first therefore treats the trade's own book change as a cancel and the print then consumes the queue again: queue 5, print 3 + delta -3 at one ts gives fill 1 / queue 0 (pinned by tests/test_fills.py:191-201) where the physical answer is fill 0 / queue 2. The ordering is a recorded design decision carried from the spec (phase3 design line 42) and the adversarial quant report (quant.md:51) into code and the fix-22 print hold-back (loop.py:759-770), with no section-F ruling on the tie-break; the decision contradicts the accumulator's algebra. On the committed fixture all 196 prints share the exact millisecond with a resting-side delta equal to the print count, so the tie-break governs every WS print whose delta is read in the same or an earlier executor loop (the common case: one ws_sink commit batch). Per order, the over-cancel equals the running max of at-price hitting prints; its queue component is later absorbed by genuine cancels of the same size, but any early queue_model fill persists as a money fill (store.py:589) and the no_watcher counterfactual track (18,512 contracts in the brief) is inflated by the same mechanism. Magnitude in production (queue sizes, the '25-160 contracts' bound, order 157's 38.92-contract fill) is unverified; the fixture is an end-game slice with 4,102-5,000-contract at-price prints and cannot bound it.

Severity important (not critical, not minor): the equal-ts delta-before-print order in fills.py:44-47 makes the core queue model optimistic by up to the largest at-price print per order (~25-160 contracts on the fixture, 0.2-3% of typical queues), the test pins the wrong answer, replay/no_watcher/R14 all inherit it undetectably, and the owner's only real fill (order 157: 38.92 contracts, queue 6,401) sits inside that band, so it belongs in phase 6 as a must-fix (swap the two constants, invert test_fills.py:191-201, re-run chunking-invariance and tape tests, re-simulate order 157) before any fill metric, weekly report, or gate evaluation is trusted, while the owner's decisions about the NAS, the Mac mini, and the experiment's viability do not hinge on it.

verified_findings.title: Late joiners' cancels are credited as queue ahead of us (optimistic cancel attribution)
verified_findings.claim: A positive delta at our price is ignored ('late joiners sit behind us') but any later unexplained negative delta at our price shortens queue_remaining as if it were ahead of us (fills.py:307-320; test_positive_delta_never_changes_queue). A participant that joins behind us and cancels, or a quote-refreshing maker at our level, moves us up the queue in the model but not on the venue. At the touch (sharp_two_sided posts 0.8 c inside mid on average, queue 15,336) this can clear a real queue quickly; magnitude unverified (would need order_watch_samples queue trajectories vs prints, 228,510 rows available).
verified_findings.question: quality
evidence: harness/execution/fills.py:307-320 (_apply_queue_delta: delta >= 0 returns; cancels = max(0, size - traded_at_price); queue_remaining -= cancels)
tests/test_fills.py:129-134 (positive delta never changes queue)
spec §2 line 42 ('A positive delta at q never changes the queue (late joiners sit behind us)')
evidence.md G: sharp_two_sided mid_minus_price 0.0081 (at or near the touch), queue_ahead avg 15,336
evidence.md C: order_watch_samples 228,510 rows (unqueried here)
verified_findings.recommendation: Track queue_behind from positive deltas after placement and attribute cancels behind-first (pessimistic bound), or pro-rata; report both bounds in table 6 beside queue_ahead. Quantify first with a query over order_watch_samples: share of queue_remaining decline explained by hitting prints vs unexplained deltas.
corrections: A positive delta at our price is ignored (fills.py:307-320, test_positive_delta_never_changes_queue, spec §2 line 42 'late joiners sit behind us'), but the model keeps no record of size that joined behind us, so any later negative delta at our price beyond traded_at_price shortens queue_remaining as if it were ahead of us. A participant that joins after us and then cancels, or a maker at our level that refreshes repeatedly (correct on the first refresh if it was originally ahead, mis-credited on every subsequent one), moves us up the queue in the model but not on the venue. This is the rule the F1 resolution specified (quant.md §1.1), so it is a design gap, not an implementation bug, and it is unmentioned in the journal or roadmap. sharp_two_sided rests 0.81 c below mid on average with queue_ahead 15,336 (evidence G), so it is the variant most exposed. The one queue_model fill (order 157) drained a 6,401 queue to 0 with only 63.92 traded at price, so its fill rested almost entirely on cancel attribution. Magnitude unverified; order_watch_samples (228,510 rows, evidence C) queue trajectories against prints would measure it.

Cancels by participants who joined our price level after us are credited as queue ahead of us (fills.py:307-320): the model tracks no 'joined behind' mass, so any negative delta at our price not explained by prints shortens queue_remaining. A maker resting at placement is credited correctly on its first cancel (its re-post is genuinely behind us); the optimism accrues from second and later refresh cycles and from genuinely later joiners, bounded by cumulative positive deltas at our price since placement, and converts to a fill only when a hitting print at our price follows. The case is not discussed in F1, spec §2 line 42, the SDD ledger or section F (only the join is), so it is an unanalyzed optimistic bias, not an accepted one. It lands on the gate population (queue_model ∪ no_watcher, tables.py:99; 646 no_watcher rows vs 2 queue_model) because the no_watcher track runs to expiry. Magnitude unverified; no fill flood is visible (1 queue_model fill in 7,997 orders; 27/445 sides with any no_watcher fill), but scarcity is dominated by fair_stale cancels (median 12.2 min) and thin books. Reversible by replay re-score with a pessimistic rule (charge unexplained cancels to a joined_behind accumulator first) since the tape is retained (roadmap lines 39, 66; spec lines 95, 110-111); recommend doing that before the week-3 claim rather than treating it as a live-path blocker.

Severity minor (phase 6 measurement item), conditional: the queue model credits every unexplained negative delta at our price as queue ahead of us (fills.py:315-320, spec line 42), so late joiners' cancels and maker quote refreshes move us up the queue in the model but not on the venue; the only money fill (order 157) had its 6,401 queue cleared by deltas, not prints, so the direction of the bias is optimistic and its magnitude is unverified. It is immaterial this week because 7,825/7,997 orders are cancelled fair_stale at median 12 min before any queue clears and the 09-14 gate has zero queue_model sample; it escalates to important the moment the churn/cadence fix lets orders rest, so the order_watch_samples query (share of queue_remaining decline from prints vs unexplained deltas) and a queue_behind pessimistic bound beside queue_ahead in table 6 should land in phase 6 before the first gate that counts queue_model fills.

verified_findings.title: no_watcher is not 'what resting would have yielded': overlapping tracks per key, mostly dirty, and the same recovery artifact
verified_findings.claim: Every fair_stale re-placement spawns a new nw track on the same (variant, market, side) that runs to the same expiry; with ~18 orders per key (7,997 / 445) the 646 nw rows / 18,512 contracts are a union over many attempts at the same prints, not a per-order counterfactual. order_episodes collapses only reprice chains (129 of 7,997 cancels), so t3/t6 'episodes' are ~one order each. nw tracks spend most of their life on dirty or age-dirty books where nothing is simulated (exec.dirty_markets ~123 of ~135 working tickers at night; order 157 dirty 3,020 of ~4,000 minutes alive) and, on recovery, inherit FM-2's watermark artifact. Adverse selection is deferred to nw_fill markouts by design, but with 27 keys there is nothing to measure. The nw working set also costs the executor: every cancelled order stays in working_orders until its expiry days out (7,388 of 7,997 orders were placed > 24 h before kickoff), one savepoint and one UPDATE per order per loop (orders table 107 MB for 7,997 rows = 13 KB/row).
