Cheapest interim: a report column 'keys with >= 1 nw fill / keys' (27/445 = 6 %).
corrections: Every fair_stale re-placement creates a new order row with its own no_watcher track on the same (variant, market, side), and all orders on a market share expiry = kickoff - 10 min (plan.py:32); with ~18 orders per key (7,997 / 445, evidence G) and each order simulated independently (loop.py:566-570), the 646 nw rows / 18,512 contracts are overlapping per-order tracks over the same tape, not one counterfactual per key. order_episodes (schema.py:338-340) collapses only reprice chains (129 of 7,997 cancels), so the episode-based tables (t3 and the gate; t6 is per-order) count ~one order per episode. nw tracks spend most of their life on dirty or age-dirty books where nothing is simulated (loop.py:799-804; exec.dirty_markets avg 122.8 over 6 h at night, evidence D5, and 107-117/hour on game night vs open_orders 53-144, journal 101; order 157 accrued 181,200 dirty-seconds = 12,080 dirty loops, ~95 % of its ~3,190 working minutes before its nw track closed on full fill at the 2026-09-10 19:42Z cross) and, on recovery, both tracks are re-anchored identically (loop.py:832-839; order 157 nw fills 150/151 are stamped 2026-09-08 17:00Z with ids adjacent to the 2026-09-10 cross 152). Adverse selection is deferred to nw_fill markouts (markouts.py:47,273-275) but with 27 keys carrying any nw fill there is little to measure. Working-set cost: a cancelled order stays in working_orders until expiry or full nw fill (store.py:324-338, loop.py:878-880), 7,388 of 7,997 orders were placed > 24 h before kickoff (evidence note 9), and each costs one savepoint (loop.py:567) and one UPDATE (store.py:676-693) per loop; the orders table is 107 MB for 7,997 rows (13.4 KB/row, evidence C), cause not verified.

no_watcher is a per-order counterfactual whose AGGREGATE is not a portfolio, and its statistical power is thin at day 3 — but the double-counting does not reach a gated number, and the working-set cost is a ruled trade-off, not a defect.

What holds: (1) fair_stale re-placement leaves overlapping nw tracks on the same (variant, market, side) — plan.py:586 gates placement while an order rests, but the cancelled order's nw track runs to expiry (loop.py:866-885), so with 7,997 orders over 445 keys (~18/key) the headline "646 nw rows / 18,512 contracts" is a union over repeated attempts at the same prints and must never be read as a portfolio or a per-key yield. (2) order_episodes collapses only reprice chains (schema.py:323-351; reprice 129 vs fair_stale 7,825), so t3's `episodes` column and criterion 6 are ~one order each and the reprice-collapse does nothing for fair_stale churn. (3) nw tracks stall on dirty and no-book markets (loop.py:799-804, 812-817) — for order 157, 3,020 of the ~3,180 minutes it sat in the working set (~95 %), or 48 % measured to its 2026-09-12 22:50Z expiry. (4) Every cancelled order stays in working_orders until its nw expiry (store.py:324-338), and 92 % of orders are placed >24 h before kickoff (evidence note 9), so the executor carries a multi-day working set that drives _advance_books and _tape per ticker (loop.py:427, 700-716) and is the plausible driver of the idle-night loop (avg 10.8 s, p50 5.3 s with 0 open orders and 0 intents considered, evidence D1/D5) on a 47 GB database whose pgdata is on a rotational HDD (evidence A).

What must be dropped or narrowed: the double-counting does not reach a gated or money quantity — no_watcher is outside MONEY_FILL_METHODS (store.py:589), the per-method counts are "reported, never gated" (tables.py:1118, 1281), and the one gated use, criterion 4 at anchor nw_fill (gate.py:66, 347-385), is a game-clustered mean whose SE grows with within-game duplication (stats.py:163-187), so repeat attempts inflate visible n_obs without manufacturing significance. "Nothing to measure" is a day-3 sample-size fact, not a construct defect: F3 ruled the nw track in precisely because the watcher's cancels remove H1's fills, the watched set is 2 fills on 1 order, and gate.py:22 already says the 150-fill/40-game criterion "no single week produces" (first evaluation Mon 2026-09-14). The dirty-book stall is deliberate (spec §2:43 "never runs on a dirty book") and biases nw DOWNWARD, opposite to the union's upward bias. The "FM-2 watermark artifact" cannot be substantiated in this repo (no FM- id exists in docs/ or harness/); order 157's late fills are equally explained by a REST backfill stamped 2026-09-08 17:00:20Z arriving ahead of the then-current watermark, which fills.py:163-172 documents, and the recovery path (loop.py:816-825) does not reset the print watermark. Correct the denominators: 135 is the intent-carrying venue-market count from the brief, not the executor's working-market denominator (unverified); "~4,000 minutes alive" for order 157 matches neither its 6,254-minute life to expiry nor its ~3,180-minute working-set window. The right cost lever is not the nw design (R8 + F3, both recorded rulings) but the unanswered fair_stale/pricing-cadence strategy question (phase 4.5 report line 8), which is what makes 92 % of orders sit for days.

Severity: important (unchanged). The no_watcher track is a union over ~18 overlapping attempts per (variant, market, side) key (445 keys, 27 with any nw fill = 6 %), not a per-key 'what resting would have yielded', and it feeds gate criteria 4 and 5 (nw_fill anchor, gate.py:65-66) and the weekly report's nw_fill set (tables.py:99); this changes how the owner should read the 18,512-contract counterfactual for the viability question and the pending fair_stale decision before the Mon 2026-09-14 report, though it does not change the Monday gate verdict (which fails on criterion 1 and the two by-construction False criteria regardless), and the executor-cost part (open nw track count, 107 MB orders bloat) is unverified and should not weigh on the Mac mini decision.

verified_findings.title: The shared 150 cap is first-come-first-served among resting orders, not edge-ordered, and sharp_two_sided takes two thirds of it
verified_findings.claim: plan.py:590-609 counts every held order into still_open before any intent is considered, then admits new intents by descending edge until 150; there is no eviction, so an earlier 0.02-edge order blocks a later 0.06-edge intent. Intents are pooled across variants, and sharp_two_sided's two-sided candidate stream (5,632 orders vs sharp_direct 2,651) held 95 of 150 slots at 20:35 CT Thu. The cap bound in 41 of 53 hours with any open orders (D3), so the primary's placed set is a churn-determined sample of its candidates. Effect on fill count is second-order (fills are ~0 regardless, FM-1); effect on measurement is that placement is not edge-ordered as §1 'Capacity (F33)' describes. Count of Skip(exec_capacity) events: unverified (not in evidence).
verified_findings.question: viability
evidence: harness/execution/plan.py:588-600 (held orders -> still_open += 1 and blocked), :602-609 (placeable sorted by -edge; has_capacity = still_open < max_open_orders), :551-553 (Skip EXEC_CAPACITY)
evidence.md D3: hourly max exec.open_orders = 150 in 41 of 53 hours; 21:00-22:00 CT on 09-08 and 09-10 hourly average exactly 150.0
docs/superpowers/autopilot/reports/2026-09-10-phase5.md:26 (150 resting: sharp_two_sided 95, sharp_direct 47, constrained 8)
brief: orders by variant 5632da729fa7 4,955 / f259ca109084 2,651 / ff363c8ac08d 391
spec §1 line 29 ('the ceiling truncates the least valuable candidates')
journal line 814 (open orders 1 -> 143 in 40 min on 2026-09-08; 'exec_capacity skip reason will appear once the cap binds')
verified_findings.recommendation: Per-variant capacity (e.g. 50 each, matching the intent of max_open 25 x 2) or evict-lowest-edge when a higher-edge intent arrives; either is a dated amendment to the frozen executor block. Lower priority than FM-1: with hold-through-refresh the cap would bind harder, so decide the two together.
corrections: plan.py:589-600 counts every held order into still_open before any intent is considered, then admits new intents by descending edge until 150; _order_action (479-516) has no capacity or edge-rank cancel, so an earlier 0.02-edge order that is still held blocks a later 0.06-edge intent until fair_stale/venue_move/reprice/expiry removes it (median 12.2 min in book per the brief). Intents are pooled across variants in one edge-sorted list (key = variant, market, side), and sharp_two_sided's two-sided candidate stream (4,955 orders vs sharp_direct 2,651, constrained 391) held 95 of 150 slots (63%) at 20:35 CT Thu 09-10 (report line 26). The cap bound (hourly max = 150) in 36 of the 53 hours with any open orders in evidence.md D3 (the evidence summary's '41 of 53' miscounts its own table), with hourly average exactly 150.0 in the 21:00 and 22:00 hours on 09-08 and 09-10, so the primary's placed set is a churn-determined sample of its candidates rather than the edge-truncated set spec §1 'Capacity (F33)' line 29 describes. Effect on fill count is second-order (queue_model fills are 2 rows on one order regardless). Count of Skip(exec_capacity) events: unverified (written to order_events per loop.py:992-996 but not pulled).

The 150-order cap is first-come-first-served in RETENTION and edge-ordered in ADMISSION; the retention rule is undocumented and the truncation is currently unmeasurable. Severity: minor (documentation + telemetry), not important.

Mechanism (confirmed): harness/execution/plan.py:590-600 counts every held order into still_open and blocks its key before any intent is read; :602-609 sorts placeable intents by -edge and admits while still_open < max_open_orders; there is no eviction, so an earlier low-edge resting order can block a later higher-edge intent at a different key. A reprice does free its own slot (plan.py:598-600; tests/test_exec_plan.py:449-453).

Narrowing 1 — the spec is not violated. Spec §1 line 29 counts "open orders across all exec variants" toward the ceiling and truncates "the rest" of the intents; it promises edge-ordered admission, which the code does (plan.py:603-605, tests/test_exec_plan.py:431-438), and never promises eviction. F33 (adversarial review line 43) introduced the cap as a loop-cost governor, with edge ordering added only to avoid the phase 2 alphabetical-truncation mistake. What is missing from the docs is a statement of the retention rule.

Narrowing 2 — sharp_two_sided's 95 of 150 slots is candidate supply, not queue priority. harness/variants/sharp_two_sided.yaml:26 (`sides: ["yes","no"]`, the only substantive diff from sharp_direct) plus harness/strategy/run.py:425-429 make it emit 2 signals per gap row where the primary emits 1: evidence raw_FG.txt line 6 (run 10445) shows 128 vs 64 candidates on the same 3,929 gaps in one tick. Orders 4,955:2,651 = 1.87x, resting 95:47 = 2.02x — the ratio any allocator returns on a 2x stream. This is the intended consequence of U2/U5/F18, recorded as spec D10 "capacity 150 shared."

Narrowing 3 — no measurable harm to the primary's selection. Mean edge_at_place is 0.0424 (sharp_two_sided) vs 0.0422 (sharp_direct) vs 0.0473 (constrained) (evidence G), inside a band frozen at [0.02, 0.06]. The FCFS-starvation hypothesis predicts the primary's placed edge should sit lower than the crowder's; it does not.

Narrowing 4 — the binding is intermittent, not chronic. Recomputed from evidence D3: hourly max = 150 in 36 of 53 hours (not 41 — the evidence note at line 968 is also high); hourly *average* ≥ 140 in only 6 of 53 (09-08 15:00/21:00/22:00, 09-10 13:00/21:00/22:00); median hourly average 94.2. And a blocked slot is held a median 12.2 minutes before fair_stale recycles it (evidence G: 7,825 of 7,997 cancels, p75 35.3 min), so slots re-contest in edge order roughly every 12 minutes. The truncated pool is also shallow: 445 distinct (variant, venue_market, side) keys across all 7,997 orders over 135 venue markets — 18 placements per key, so the large order counts are churn, not forgone distinct opportunities.

Narrowing 5 — eviction would likely be harmful. queue_ahead_at_place averages 15,336 / 8,524 contracts (evidence G); cancel-replacing forfeits queue position, which is the only thing that produced a fill (order 157 rested 31 min from queue_ahead 6,401).

What to carry into phase 6: (a) state the retention rule in the phase 3 design §1 beside the admission rule; (b) make the truncation measurable — no exec_capacity skip count exists in the evidence file, and `intents_without_order_or_skip` FAILS at 483 against threshold 0 (evidence lines 852, 868), so the skip ledger is incomplete and the cap's selection effect cannot be quantified today. Effect on fills remains second-order (fills are ~0 regardless, FM-1).

Severity minor (measurement note, not a viability question): plan.py:588-609 admits new intents by descending edge but never evicts a resting lower-edge order, so under the shared 150 cap placement is first-come-first-served among resting orders, contrary to spec §1 F33 line 29; effect on fills is nil in week 1 (1 real fill of 7,997 orders, fair_stale median 12 min bounds the lock-in) and the crowding variant (sharp_two_sided, 95/150 at 20:35 CT 09-10) is the U5 gate variant. Cap-binding frequency and Skip(exec_capacity) count unverified. Fold into the pending fair_stale/cadence decision as a spec errata or phase-6 amendment; do not amend the frozen executor block during week 1.

refuted_findings.title: apply_caps false disables per_game, daily and max_open for both live-placing non-constrained variants, including the gate variant; the same code path runs live
refuted_findings.claim: plan.py:545-550 emits CapGate for every variant but blocks only when cfg['apply_caps'] is true; run.py:371-373 likewise excludes CAP_LABELS from the signal decision. The per-bet cap IS enforced by the stake clamp at sizing (run.py:322: stake = min(uncapped, per_bet_cap x bankroll)), so only per_game 5 %, daily 15 % and max_open 25 are labels. sharp_two_sided rested 95 orders (~$4,800 notional at ~$50/order) against max_open 25 and a $450 daily cap; sharp_direct 47 vs 25. README:71-72 and the pre-registration record (line 14) disclose that only constrained enforces, so this is not a pre-registration honesty breach, but README:69-71 lists the caps as system behaviour first, the go-live gate has no cap-adherence criterion, and the live gateway uses the same plan_actions, so a live sharp_two_sided would be bounded only by the 150 global cap (which is 2x the sum of the three max_open values).
reasons:
alternative: The mechanism the reviewer describes is real, but its two load-bearing claims — that this is a defect, and that it is a live-trading risk — are both better explained by the record.

(1) It is not a defect; it is the instruction. The design spec states it as the experiment's method, not a gap: "filters, veto, caps, drawdown stop are labels in paper mode; a `constrained` secondary variant applies them for sizing realism" (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-06-sportsbook-harness-design.md:258, §9.6 data-gathering mode). The phase 3 addendum then spells out the exact code shape the reviewer found, in advance: "caps are labels in `signals`; a False cap label (the first False in `CAP_LABELS` order) emits a `CapGate` action for every exec variant, written as `order_events(kind = cap_gate)`, and blocks placement only for `apply_caps` variants" (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-07-phase3-paper-execution-design.md:35). plan.py:545-550 and run.py:371-373 are a literal transcription of that sentence, `CapGate` emitted-but-non-blocking included. The pre-registration's whole reason for `constrained` existing is to be the enforcing arm of that A/B ("Same as primary but bankroll caps enforced (`apply_caps: true`) for sizing realism", pre-registration line 14); if `sharp_two_sided` and `sharp_direct` also enforced, `constrained` would measure nothing and the README's stated question — "How much do the safety caps cost in missed bets?" (README:84) — would be unanswerable. The reviewer's own concession that the pre-registration discloses it concedes the design-decision reading; what remains is a README emphasis preference, not an important finding.

(2) The live-risk claim is inverted. "A live sharp_two_sided would be bounded only by the 150 global cap" is contradicted by the code on the live path. The live writer enforces its own pre-send invariant independent of the strategy layer: `if stake > self._per_bet_cap_dollars: raise` and `if contracts > self._contract_cap: raise` (harness/venues/kalshi/authed.py:991-996), the spec's §5.2 pre-send invariant (design spec:123; phase 4 design:32). And `make_writer` defaults both to `_ZERO` when a caller does not resolve them, deliberately: "a writer built without them can place nothing of consequence rather than something under an unreviewed default" (authed.py:1349-1354, :1394-1396). The only caller that supplies non-zero caps today is the demo smoke (smoke.py:146-147). So the live path's failure mode is refusing every order, not placing 95 unbounded ones. On top of that, `KalshiGateway` is unconstructable in the deployed posture: four conditions (`LIVE_TRADING=1`, `mode=live`, a passing gate report, `secrets/legal_decision`) at authed.py:1367-1378, of which gate criteria 11 and 12 are "False by construction in phase 3" (harness/report/gate.py:176-185) and `gate_reports` has 0 rows (evidence.md §I), so condition 3 cannot hold. Live mode also adds brakes paper does not have: the drawdown stop trips the kill switch live but is information-only in paper (harness/execution/risk.py:13-19), and a 60-messages/minute budget breach trips it (gateway.py, phase 4 design:51).

(3) The "no cap-adherence gate criterion" observation is a user decision, not a loop omission. R1 in the adversarial review's section F rulings: "Gate criteria, thresholds, benchmark and BH families, cell grids, success thresholds and confirmation cut-offs are invariants: the loop never amends them; only a dated user decision does." Adding a cap criterion to gate.py's CRITERIA tuple is precisely the amendment R1 forbids the loop from making.

(4) The numbers check out but do not carry the severity. sharp_two_sided avg 110.4 contracts at avg price 0.457 = ~$50.5/order (evidence.md §G per-variant table), so 95 resting ≈ $4,800 against a labelled daily cap of $450 — correct arithmetic, and exactly the quantity §9.6 asks to be measured. The binding constraint in the field was the 150 global ceiling, not any per-variant cap: it was the limit in 41 of 53 hours with open orders (evidence.md controller note 4). The reviewer is right that the per-bet cap is enforced by the clamp at run.py:315-322, which already narrows the finding to three labels on a $3,000 pretend bankroll with zero real money at risk.

What survives is an observation, not an important finding: README:69-71 states the caps as system behaviour one sentence before the qualifier, and the go-live gate carries no cap-adherence criterion — both fixable by a wording edit and a dated user decision respectively. Uncertainty retained (confidence 0.76) because no journal entry or roadmap line explicitly re-ratifies the README wording, and because who wires `per_bet_cap_dollars` into a production `make_writer` call is unbuilt rather than proven safe — the live sizing wiring is genuinely unexercised, but it fails closed at zero, which is the opposite of the claim.

materiality: Every factual leg verifies, but the severity is mis-set: the behaviour is pre-registered by design, the money-relevant cap IS enforced, and the live scenario cannot occur in the 1-2 week horizon.

VERIFIED AS STATED: plan.py:546-549 `blocking = bool(cfg["apply_caps"])` with CapGate emitted unconditionally; run.py:371-373 `counted = FILTER_LABELS + (CAP_LABELS if apply_caps else [])`; run.py:322 `stake = min(uncapped_stake, per_bet_cap)`; sharp_two_sided.yaml:20-25 and sharp_direct.yaml apply_caps false, constrained.yaml:26 true; README.md:69-72 wording; gate.py CRITERIA tuple (lines 119-185) has 12 criteria and none about cap adherence; evidence.md I confirms apply_caps true only for ff363c8ac08d.

WHY THE SEVERITY IS WRONG:
1. Pre-registered as intended behaviour, not an oversight. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-07-phase3-paper-execution-design.md:35 spells it out verbatim: "caps are labels in `signals`; a False cap label ... emits a `CapGate` action for every exec variant ... and blocks placement only for `apply_caps` variants." run.py:363-365 carries the design rationale in a comment (labels measured against uncapped Kelly "so the caps' cost is measured, not hidden by the clamp"). The whole point of the `constrained` variant (pre-reg line 100: "Same as primary but bankroll caps enforced (`apply_caps: true`) for sizing realism") is to price what the caps cost. The reviewer's own first recommendation — flip apply_caps on sharp_two_sided by amendment — would delete the single contrast that variant exists to provide, and touches a variant frozen by invariant 1.
2. The dollar-consequential cap is enforced for every variant. per_bet_cap 0.03 x 3000 = $90 is clamped at sizing (run.py:315-322) regardless of apply_caps, so no single order can be oversized. What is label-only is portfolio concentration (per_game 5 %, daily 15 %, max_open 25), and even that is hard-bounded by exec_max_open_orders = 150 in the executor.
3. The live path is blocked in code, not just by policy. harness/venues/kalshi/authed.py:1367 refuses when `int(settings.live_trading) != 1`, and LIVE_CONDITIONS (authed.py:1301) requires all four of LIVE_TRADING=1, mode=live, a passing gate report, and secrets/legal_decision. Two gate criteria (gate.py:176-184) are False by construction. So "the same code path runs live" is true only after the owner takes deliberate, documented action that does not exist yet.
4. The gate is nowhere near passing on the merits either: criterion `fill_events` needs >= 150 orders with a queue_model fill across >= 40 games; the field data shows 2 queue_model rows on ONE order, 38.92 contracts total, zero since 2026-09-08 (evidence.md controller note 5; brief "Fills table"). gate_reports has 0 rows; the design spec itself (2026-09-06-sportsbook-harness-design.md:305) puts the gate review "realistically mid-October, together with the legal decision." Nothing here fires inside the owner's 1-2 week window.
5. The disclosure complaint is a two-sentence ordering nit: README:71-72 discloses the label-only behaviour in the sentence immediately following the cap list, and the reviewer concedes there is no pre-registration honesty breach.
6. The exposure numbers cited undercut the alarm rather than support it. 95 resting orders at ~$50 notional is ~$4,800 against a $3,000 paper bankroll — but this is exactly what the labels are there to record, and the binding constraint in practice was the global 150 (evidence.md note 4: 150 was binding in 41 of 53 hours with open orders), not the per-variant caps.

WHAT SURVIVES, AT MINOR: two cheap, non-urgent items — (a) print resting notional vs each variant's daily cap in the weekly report so the label-only gap is visible on the Mon 2026-09-14 report, and (b) add a cap-adherence criterion to the gate, which belongs with the legal decision and LIVE_TRADING flip, not with phase 6. The README reorder is info-level.

COMPETING FOR THE OWNER'S ATTENTION AND OUTRANKING THIS: fill_events at 1 of 150 with 92 % of orders placed >24 h from kickoff (evidence.md note 9) and 7,825 of 7,997 orders cancelled fair_stale — i.e. whether the experiment produces a scorable dataset at all; the p95 loop ceiling missed on 3 of 4 days (evidence.md note 3); pricing budget_exhausted at 45 % of 09-10 priced ticks against a 10 % phase 6 trigger (note 2); check_results intents_without_order_or_skip FAILING at 483 with three integrity checks timing out (note 7). Ranking a designed, disclosed, paper-mode-only labelling choice as "important" alongside those misallocates the owner's week.

refuted_findings.title: The 120 s per-ticker book age marks quiet markets dirty: no placement and no simulation exactly where a resting order could fill
refuted_findings.claim: MarketNow.dirty (plan.py:246-257) reads dirty when the ticker's newest applied delta is older than exec_book_max_age_s = 120 s, independent of the global dead_recorder check. A far-out market with no book change for two minutes therefore Skip(book_dirty)s its intents and holds (does not cancel, does not simulate) its open orders; journal 57 counted book_dirty 501 vs fair_stale 508 skips on the first day. The hold path is why fair_stale time-in-book has a long tail (p95 147 min) and why exec.dirty_markets sits at ~123 of ~135 working tickers. Fills are deferred rather than lost on this path (age-dirty recovery goes through book_at(ts_of(cursor)), loop.py:898-906, not the FM-2 jump), but placement on quiet markets is blocked while quiet.
reasons:
alternative: The code citations are all accurate (plan.py:246-257 `dirty`, :499-500 hold, :532-533 Skip BOOK_DIRTY; loop.py:425-426, :799-804), but the framing as a defect and three of the four supporting inferences do not survive.

(1) NOT AN UNINTENDED INTERACTION — IT IS THE WRITTEN SPEC. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-07-phase3-paper-execution-design.md:33 states verbatim: "A book is dirty when any `gap` row ... exists regardless of ticker, **or when the ticker's newest event is older than `exec_book_max_age_s` (120 s; a dead recorder must not read clean). No fill, cancel or placement decision on a dirty book**; `dirty_minutes` accumulates on the order." The reviewer cites that same line as if it mandated only the global check; it mandates the per-ticker one, and the hold-plus-skip behaviour, explicitly. The adversarial review's F36 row (docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-09-07-autopilot-adversarial-review.md:46) ruled the same: "`book_dirty` is also true when the ticker's newest `orderbook_events` row is older than 120 s". loop.py:425-426's `dead_recorder` is the *additional* global layer, not the intended-and-substituted one.

(2) THE ~123-OF-135 NUMBER IS MISREAD. `exec.dirty_markets` counts markets in `rows`, which comes from `working_orders` = "open OR `nw_done = false`" (harness/execution/store.py:336, 341-349) — i.e. every cancelled order whose *no-watcher counterfactual* has not reached kickoff-10min. In the exact 6 h window that produced 122.8 (evidence.md "exec metrics last 6h", 01:30-07:30 CT), the same table reads exec.intents_considered avg 0.0, exec.placed avg 0.0, exec.open_orders avg 0.3. There were zero intents to block. 123 dirty markets overnight means "123 counterfactual tracks paused at 3 a.m.", not "123 markets where placement is blocked". Journal 101's 107-117 on game night is likewise dominated by the same nw backlog (7,997 orders, nearly all cancelled, tracks running for days on 24-72h/>72h markets: evidence G ttk buckets, 3,903 + 1,852 + 660 + 1,447 orders at ≥24 h).

(3) "NO PLACEMENT" IS REFUTED BY THROUGHPUT. A book_dirty Skip does not consume a placement slot: `plan_actions` (plan.py:601-614) increments `still_open` only on a `Place`, and iterates `placeable` in descending-edge order, so a dirty market's intent is passed over and the next candidate takes the slot. exec_max_open_orders = 150 (shared across three variants) was *saturated* — evidence D3 shows max 150 in ~35 of the 53 listed hours and avg 150.0 in four of them (09-08 21:00/22:00, 09-10 21:00/22:00) — and 7,997 orders were placed in 3 days (D4: 3,836 on 09-10). The age rule therefore changed *which* markets received the 150 slots, not how many orders rested. The binding constraint on placement was the shared cap, not dirtiness.

(4) "EXACTLY WHERE A RESTING ORDER COULD FILL" IS BACKWARDS, AND THE ONE COUNTEREXAMPLE IS THE ONLY MONEY FILL IN THE DATASET. Age-dirty means no `orderbook_events` row for 120 s, i.e. no resting size was consumed at any level, i.e. our queue position provably could not have advanced in that window. Empirically, order 157 (evidence.md section G) — the *only* queue_model fill in the whole experiment, 38.92 contracts — carries `dirty_seconds` 181,200 / `dirty_minutes` 3,020 over a ~53 h track and `book_dirty = t` on every one of its first 20 order_watch_samples from 14:37:02Z onward: that market was dirty ~95 % of its life and still produced the only real fill. Stronger: its `staleness_at_place` is 53 s with `stale_allowance_at_place` 220 s, so the market was fair-stale from ~14:39:34Z, yet the order was cancelled `fair_stale` only at 15:12:06Z — the dirty hold (plan.py:499-500 orders `dirty` before `_fair_stale`) is precisely what kept it resting through the 15:07:15Z fill. Deleting the hold path the reviewer objects to would have deleted the experiment's only money fill.

(5) THE CAUSAL ATTRIBUTION FOR THE p95 147 min TAIL IS WEAK. tib p50 is 12.2 min against a 220 s staleness threshold (evidence G), which means the fair value was *refreshing* during most of the time in book — consistent with evidence F (game-16 fair values refreshed every 1-3.5 min, 46 rows per run, Thu evening), not with a stale order pinned by a dirty book. The tail is better explained by when a market stops being repriced at all: evidence E shows 109 of 243 priced ticks (45 %) hit `price_budget_s = 45` on 09-10, 36/73 on 09-08, and only 8 priced ticks all day on 09-11, with variants rotated out of `variants_run` (sample 10445 drops wide_band). That is the pricing-cadence question the phase 4.5 report already escalated to the user and the user has not answered (brief line 28) — not the book-age rule.

Also note the reviewer inverted the check order for intents: `_intent_actions` tests `_fair_stale` at plan.py:531 BEFORE `dirty` at :532, so a book_dirty skip can only fire on a market whose fair value is fresh — the opposite of "a far-out market nobody is pricing". Journal 57's 501 book_dirty / 508 fair_stale are F35-deduped `order_events(kind=skipped)` rows keyed on (intent_id, kind, reason) over 509 lifetime intents on day 1 (2026-09-08 09:26 CT, 1 open order, 98 cancelled); essentially every intent carries both markers, so the two counts are not a ranking of causes and say nothing about the current 7,997-order regime.

WHAT SURVIVES: the real cost of the per-ticker age rule falls on the research dataset, not on execution. loop.py:799-804 pauses the `no_watcher` counterfactual on dirty markets too, and order 157 shows that track running at roughly a 5 % duty cycle on a quiet far-out market. The 646 no_watcher fill rows — the only fill statistics the experiment has — are therefore sampled with a bias toward active books. That is a measurement-quality item worth a phase 6 line, at minor severity, not an "important" execution defect.

materiality: MECHANICS VERIFIED, MATERIALITY OVERSTATED — downgrade to minor (measurement item, not a phase-6 change).

Every citation checks out exactly. plan.py:246-257 is `if self.book is None: return False; return (self.book_dirty or self.book.dirty or book_age_s(self.book, now) > s.book_max_age_s)`; exec_book_max_age_s = 120 (brief line 25). plan.py:499-500 holds an open order on a dirty market (`return None`), plan.py:532-533 Skips the intent BOOK_DIRTY. loop.py:425-426 computes dead_recorder from the global tape head; loop.py:799-804 skips simulation and only calls add_dirty_seconds. journal 57 skip reasons are fair_stale 508 / book_dirty 501 / no_book 98. evidence D6 exec.dirty_markets avg 122.8 max 125 (exec_heartbeat book_dirty_markets 125), evidence G tib p75 35.3 / p95 147 min. Nothing in the claim is wrong on the code.

Four facts cut the impact down:

1. The fill-loss channel is near-zero by construction. BookState.as_of advances ONLY inside apply_delta (harness/execution/book.py:283; book_age_s at :578-585 reads as_of); trades never touch it. A resting order can only be filled by a taker consuming its level, which IS an orderbook_delta, which resets as_of to ~0. So a market cannot be age-dirty at the instant a fill would occur; _advance_books runs before markets are built (loop.py:427-429), so the fill-producing delta un-dirties the market in the same loop. Worst case deferral is sub-loop, not the multi-minute hold the finding implies. The reviewer half-concedes this ("fills are deferred rather than lost") and then bases the severity on the other half.

2. The placement upside is capped and the cap was already saturated. exec_max_open_orders = 150 is shared across all three exec variants (brief line 25). evidence D3: hourly max = 150 in ~44 of 53 hours, with hourly AVG 150.0 at 2026-09-10 21:00 and 22:00, 144.0 at 13:00, 128.5 at 10:00. When the shared cap is pinned, un-dirtying quiet markets adds zero net resting orders; it only reallocates which tickers hold the 150. Placement was not throughput-starved either: 3,836 orders placed on 09-10 (brief line 19), 328/hr in the 19:00 hour (evidence D4).

3. The causal story on the tail is inverted. In the ORDER chain, dirty (plan.py:499) is tested BEFORE _fair_stale (:501), so the dirty hold DELAYS the fair_stale cancel — it is what produces the p95 147 min tail, and the counterfactual says that is fill-positive, not damage: no_watcher (never-cancelled) produced 646 fill rows / 18,512 contracts vs queue_model 2 rows / 38.92 contracts on one order (brief line 21). The thing killing fills is the cancel at median 12.2 min in book that closed 7,825 of 7,997 orders for fair_stale (brief line 20) — already parked as the unanswered strategy question the owner owes an answer to (brief line 28, docs/superpowers/autopilot/reports/2026-09-09-phase4.5.md line 8). Recommending the removal of the hold would shorten time-in-book, i.e. push in the wrong direction on the owner's actual complaint.

4. The recommendation is affirmatively risky as written. "Keep the global dead_recorder test ... drop the per-ticker age rule (quiet != broken when the recorder is alive and the ticker is subscribed)": store.py:411-420 shows newest_event_ts reads the head of the whole tape by id — one row from ANY of the 500 subscribed tickers (evidence: ws.subscribed_tickers 500.0) makes the recorder read alive. There is no per-ticker liveness signal other than the age rule (exec.tape_lag_tickers measures cursor-vs-head lag, which is silent when no events exist for a ticker). Dropping it means a single dead per-ticker subscription reads clean and the harness quotes against a frozen ladder — exactly the F36 failure, and in live money that is adverse selection, not a paper artifact. "Subscribed" is a claim about the subscription list, not about the feed working.

DECISION IMPACT over the next 1-2 weeks: none of the owner's five questions turn on this. Not viability (the one-fill outcome is explained by the 150 cap plus the fair_stale cancel policy, both already on the owner's desk), not the Mac mini (no host component), not quality-vs-NAS (this rule predates and is independent of the NAS workarounds), and it is not a phase-6 must-do.

WHAT SURVIVES: the measurement, which is cheap and currently missing. Nobody has counted intents whose SOLE blocker was book_dirty at a moment when open_orders < 150 — dirty_markets 122.8/135 is measured at night with intents_considered 0.0 and open_orders 0.3 (evidence D6), so it says nothing about binding. Note also that in the INTENT chain _fair_stale is tested BEFORE dirty (plan.py:530 vs 532), so book_dirty is only ever the marginal blocker on intents whose fair is fresh, further shrinking the affected population.

title: Engineering quality of the code and tests
summary:
Grade B-: built fast and sound in the core, fragile at every boundary. Core paths (executor loop, fill accounting, settlement, gate) are idempotent (on-conflict + RETURNING, store.py:1-33), locked (loop.py:249-262), savepointed per order/game, and covered by 1,583 tests that run against a real Postgres on 5433 (Makefile:149-152, conftest.py:21-58; 76 of 122 files). Migrations are additive with a catalogue-diff test (test_alembic.py, 21 tests). 107 except-Exception sites all carry a reason and the measurement-relevant ones label into ctx errors / runs.notes / heartbeat.last_error.

The one critical engineering defect is arithmetic, not strategy: stale_allowance_s = FEATURED_CADENCE_S (hardcoded 120, fair.py:22-35) + tick_budget_s 100 = 220 s on all 7,825 fair_stale orders, while the real pricing cadence is 900 s weekday / 300 s weekend / 120 s game window (cadence.py interval_for). Combined with the dirty-book hold that precedes the stale check (plan.py:499-502) and blocks fill simulation (loop.py:799-804) on the ~123/135 quiet markets, orders rest while nothing trades and are cancelled on the first book event: 1 real fill (38.92 contracts) vs 18,512 counterfactual no_watcher contracts. The phase 4.5 report mislabelled this a strategy question.

Budgets are labelled at job level (job.py:199-210) but invisible to the gate (gate.py reads no job_runs); report_wtd has not rendered in 26 h (report_runs last 09-10 10:25Z) and three integrity checks skip on timeout daily. Test provenance: 7 of 7 external boundaries exercised live for the first time failed (fixes 23,24,27,28,29,39,41); the Trade API write path has zero recorded fixtures. 41 carried fixes in 5 days; 626 commits; 32 % prose with 580 review-id references in harness/.

verified_findings.title: fair_stale allowance is hardcoded to a 120 s cadence the recorder runs at only in game windows; with the dirty-hold ordering this cancels orders exactly when they could fill
verified_findings.claim: stale_allowance_s for featured lines is FEATURED_CADENCE_S (120, fixed) + tick_budget_s (100) = 220 s regardless of the actual pricing cadence (900 s weekday, 300 s weekend, 120 s game window, None 01:00-08:00), so on non-game hours every order's fair is 'stale' for 680 of every 900 s; because _order_action checks market.dirty() before _fair_stale and ~123 of 135 markets have a book older than 120 s at any moment, an order is held while its market is quiet and cancelled fair_stale on the first book event after the fair passes 220 s, and _simulate_order advances no track on a dirty market, so the watched track almost never sees a print. This mechanism, not strategy, produces 7,825/7,997 fair_stale cancels, hourly placed == cancelled, and 1 real fill against 18,512 counterfactual no_watcher contracts.

In weekday non-game hours (~69 % of the 7,993 D4 cancels) the fair is stale for ~680 of every 900 s; overnight (01:30-07:30 CT) it never refreshes; in game windows (~31 %) fair values refresh every ~125 s median (evidence F) and the 220 s bound is breached by tick jitter and 100+ s executor loops. Because _order_action checks market.dirty() before _fair_stale (plan.py:499-502) and 114-125 of the working-set markets are dirty (book older than 120 s) at any reading, an order is held while its market is quiet and cancelled fair_stale on the first book event after the fair passes 220 s; _simulate_order advances neither track on a dirty market (loop.py:799-804), and the watched track gets only the recovery loop's tape before the cancel lands, so it rarely fills (1 queue_model order vs 27 of 445 keys with no_watcher fills). Severity: high; fix is to derive the allowance from the cadence in force (or raise stale_s) and to re-order the dirty hold behind the fair_stale check, both currently pinned by tests/test_fair.py:289-300 and carried as an unanswered strategy question (phase 4.5 report line 8).

stale_allowance_s for featured lines is a spec-fixed 120 s + tick_budget_s (100) = 220 s (spec F11 line 7; harness/pricing/fair.py:22-35; tests/test_fair.py:291-299 pins 220), while the recorder prices on interval_for's 900 s weekday / 300 s weekend / 120 s game-window / None 01:00-08:00 cadence (harness/recorder/cadence.py:16-33; pricing gated by the same interval via tick.py:575-590, 905-923; fair_ts = created_at of the newest gap snapshot's fair row, store.py:352-372). On weekday daytime this makes every resting order's fair "stale" for ~680 of every 900 s: intents are placeable only in the ~220 s after each pricing run, and because _order_action checks market.dirty() before _fair_stale (plan.py:499-502) on ~114-125 of ~135 quiet markets, an order is held while its ticker is quiet and cancelled fair_stale on the first loop after a book event once the fair is older than 220 s; the print that ends the dirty stretch is fed to the watched track first (loop.py:431-450, fills before decisions), so the cost is forgone resting time and a queue-position reset on re-placement (avg queue_ahead 5k-15k contracts), not a missed print. The loop observed this on 2026-09-09 (journal 82: 150 placed at 08:04 CT, 147 fair_stale by 10:24) and carried it to the user twice as a strategy question (phase 4.5 report line 8; phase 5 report line 11), unanswered; changing the allowance also changes the pre-registered not_stale signal label (spec line 7), so it needs a dated amendment. The mechanism accounts for the weekday-daytime share of the 7,825 fair_stale cancels and, with the shared 150-order cap binding in 41 of 53 hours (D3), for hourly placed == cancelled; roughly a third of cancels (D4 hourly sums in the 09-09 SEA-NE and 09-10 LAR-SF 120 s windows, ~833 + ~1,912 + 473 at 00:00) occurred where the allowance matches the nominal cadence and are instead driven by refresh gaps of 110-215 s (evidence F) plus tick duration (E: p95 123 s on 09-10) and executor loop lag (D2: p95 72-115 s) exceeding the 100 s tick budget, i.e. NAS performance. verified_findings.title: NAS workarounds: the executor-side ones are sound engineering; the measurement-side ones traded cadence and checks for survival
verified_findings.claim: Fixes 22/26 (id-only delta reads, adaptive 250-20,000 batch), 31 (bounded snapshot builders, self-guard), 32 (BRIN autosummarize) and 35 (RFQ index and cheap declines) are correct on any host and would be needed at scale anyway. Three changes are quality sacrifices driven by the box: report_wtd moved from hourly (design §3.7) to 6 h with a yield-below-120 s rule and has now not rendered for 26 h; integrity checks run under a 2 s timeout and three never complete; and the two phase 5 features (RFQ listener, research worker) were each switched off within an hour of deploy because the box could not carry them beside the tape. Two measurement-side changes traded cadence and checks for survival: report_wtd was moved from hourly (design §3.7) to 6 h in the phase 3 final review (I6, citing the NAS's ~1 GB spare RAM) with a yield-below-120 s rule, and it has not rendered since 2026-09-10 05:25 CT (~26 h; the prior renders were already 7-14 h apart); the integrity checks' 2 s statement timeout is a phase 3 design constant (282ae66), but fix 16 to bound the three statements that exceed it has been carried open since 2026-09-08, so duplicate_trades, fair_values_negative_feed_lag and fair_values_negative_staleness have skipped on timeout at every recorded housekeeping run (journal 48, 92, 109; evidence I at 04:15 CT). The two phase 5 features (RFQ listener, research worker) were each switched off within 13-30 min of the 03:12 CT deploy (journal 109) and the listener again 7 min after the 05:27 CT deploy (journal 110), with the box's deploy storm and nightly dump as the amplifier but code defects (fixes 35, 36, 38) as the root causes; the worker was back on at 05:25 CT (journal 110) and the listener at 06:38 CT (journal 112). The executor's daily p95 exceeded its 7.5 s ceiling on 3 of 4 days (16.2 s / 6.19 s / 15.2 s / 10.0 s, evidence D1; the 09-11 figure is a partial day including two deploy storms), with the 09-10 19:00 hour at 114.8 s (D2).

Fixes 22/26/31/32/35 are sound on any host. Two measurement-side changes traded quality for the box: (a) report_wtd runs six-hourly instead of the design §3.7 hourly because final review I6 (2026-09-08) chose the cadence lever over bounding _T4/_T5, which still load a week of market_gap_snapshots and WS snapshot bodies into Python (report_wtd.py:41-51); its last provisional row is 2026-09-10 10:25Z (evidence I) because the hourly 600 s settle budget is spent before report_wtd's turn (journal 101: budget_exhausted for markouts and report_wtd at 18:13 and 19:13 on 09-10), and Study's current-week cells (study.py:69-73) are therefore ~26 h stale; (b) the 2 s check timeout is a design principle from U6 (282ae66; checks.py:1-9) and fix 16's bounds were shipped (checks.py:72-76, 175-179, 254-259), but journal 92 ruled the skip "honest" because a wider timeout would starve the executor; the three checks complete warm (141 ms, journal 93) and skip only in the 04:00 CT post-dump window (housekeeping.py:47 DUE_HOUR_UTC 9; dump 03:30 CT), so the cheaper remedy is the schedule, not the timeout. The phase 5 switch-offs were defect-driven pauses, not box sacrifices: the worker (03:27) for fix 36's re-render loop, the listener (03:41) for fix 35's per-frame lateral and (05:33) for fix 38's ~30 GB/day firehose, all back on at 06:38 CT (journal 109/110/112), on a night with no intents to veto. The executor breached the roadmap's game-window trigger (roadmap.md:315: p95 over 7.5 s, two consecutive windows): SEA-NE p95 7,956 ms (journal 96), LAR-SF 19:00 hour p95 114.8 s and 22:00/23:00 post-media-stop 13.2/9.0 s (evidence D2); the daily p95 figures (D1) are inflated by deploy storms and are the weaker measure.

Severity minor (question nas_sacrifice): the executor-side NAS fixes (22/26/31/32/35) are sound and already shipped; the measurement-side changes cost only the Study surface's provisional-cell freshness (report_wtd last ran 2026-09-10 05:25 CT because the hourly settle job's 600 s budget is spent by markouts first, journal 101) and three integrity checks that have skipped since 09-08 pending fix 16's bounded SQL (roadmap line 339), while the phase 5 switch-offs were correctness bugs (fixes 36/38) now reversed (journal 112); none of this touches the Monday 09-14 gate report, which renders separately on the 900 s batch engine (cli.py:485, roadmap line 303), so the right action is to schedule fix 16 and a settle-budget reorder in phase 6, not to force hourly WTD or 900 s checks inside the same 600 s job on any host.

refuted_findings.title: The intents_without_order_or_skip integrity check is permanently red, most likely because it ignores cap_gate events
refuted_findings.claim: The check counts intents with no order and no order_events row of kind 'skipped', but a blocking CapGate (the only outcome for the apply_caps=true variant 'constrained' when a cap is hit) writes kind 'cap_gate' and no 'skipped' row, so those intents are counted as lost; the check fails at 483 and a permanently failing check trains the operator to ignore the board. Breakdown of the 483 is unverified (no NAS access from this lens).
reasons: alternative: The code fact holds (checks.py:217-218 excuses only kind='skipped'; plan.py:545-550 blocking CapGate emits no Skip; loop.py:987-991 writes kind='cap_gate'), but the two load-bearing parts of the claim are contradicted. (1) Not permanently red: the corrected check reported 0 fail at 04:25 CT 2026-09-10 (journal.md line 1196: "24 pass, 0 fail ... intents_without_order_or_skip and build_sha_drift now pass") and passed on 2026-09-08 (evidence/2026-09-08-deploy-verify-0458-layer2.txt:68, 2026-09-08-verify-0926-layer2.txt:97), while CapGate/cap_gate has been live since 487fd73/fe54563 (2026-09-07 18:07/19:49 CT) and constrained (the only apply_caps=true variant, evidence I) was trading through those windows (391 orders, evidence G). Journal 79's trace of the earlier 2,459-row fail (line 1041) found 2,459/2,459 explained by the hold path, i.e. zero cap_gate-only rows. (2) "Most likely cap_gate" is not better supported than a mechanism unique to the failing window: store.load_intents takes only the newest intent per key (store.py:257-268, distinct on) and plan_actions acts only on newest-not-blocked intents (plan.py:602), so an intent superseded by the next tick's intent before any loop evaluated it gets no order and no event, and the check's excuse (an order working at created_at) does not cover it. Fair values/signals recur every ~2-2.5 min per game (evidence F; ~558 ok runs/day, evidence E) while on the 09-10 game night, inside this check's 24 h window (04:15 CT 09-10 to 04:15 CT 09-11), loops ran p95 101-118 s, max 256 s, loops_skipped 354->443 (journal 101, 107; evidence note 3): loop gaps longer than the intent cadence. That explains pass (fast loops 09-09: avg 4.1 s, p95 6.2 s) then fail (09-10). The cap_gate mechanism needs constrained to bind its own caps: at ~$50/order (137.3 contracts x 0.369, evidence G) and ~3 concurrent orders on average (391 x 33.7 min over ~3 days), daily_cap $450 binds at ~9 resting orders and max_open at 25; per_game $150 at ~3 per game. Possible on the 3,836-order day, not routine, and unverified. Both breakdowns are unverified without NAS access. The residual true finding is operational: journal 109-112 never mention the 04:15 CT run or the 483, so the fail went unread for 3+ hours; and the check omits a designed outcome kind (phase3 design line 35/73 records cap_gate as a first-class event), a one-line gap worth closing but not the demonstrated cause.

(3) Magnitude is ~483 of ~29k intents/day (~1.6 %), intent-side only, with orders/fills/place-event checks all passing; the identical shape (2,459 hold-path rows) was traced and fixed within a day by the existing process (journal line 1041 -> 36f8b70). title: Audit of every NAS-driven budget, cap, timeout and cadence
summary: Yes, experiment quality was sacrificed, in three measurable places, and every loss is labelled somewhere but two are silent at the row level. (1) Pricing budget (price_budget_s 20->45 on 2026-09-08, Amendment 4, plus a 20 s floor capped to the cadence): pricing.budget_exhausted on 109/243 priced ticks (45 %) on game day 09-10, 43/281 (15 %) 09-09, 36/73 (49 %) 09-08; the gate and primary always score, but the executed `constrained` variant is third in line and is dropped when only two fit; the dropped variants' missing intents are unlabelled on the intents/orders side. (2) Executor latency: 15 s period, 10 s statement timeout, 250-row batch floor; game-night loop avg 27.5 s / p95 115-118 s, p95 over the 7.5 s ceiling on 3 of 4 days, 521/17,138 loops skipped (3 %), staleness_at_place p50 67 s of a 220 s allowance; WS sink timeouts 33-50 disconnects per 3 h on game night, each discarding up to 100 events and dirtying books. (3) Three integrity checks skip on the 2 s timeout at every housekeeping (still at 04:15 CT today, after fix 32); markouts/report_wtd exhaust the 600 s hourly budget on game nights; 483 intents lost in 24 h (1.6 %). The fair_stale churn (7,825/7,997 cancels) is the 220 s allowance vs the pricing cadence, not the host; the recorder's fetch budget binds on 1 tick/day (not material). Nearly all of (1)-(3) would disappear on a host with more RAM and an SSD; what needs code regardless: fix 34, fix 37, the three checks' statement shapes, fixes 36/38/40 (bugs on any host). Postgres: compose pins shared_buffers 512 MB / effective_cache_size 1.5 GB / random_page_cost 1.1 (an SSD value on a rotational pool) with ~3 GB now available; a cheap partial lever, not a fix.

The gate and primary are ordered first (pipeline.py:131-149), but an exhausted tick scores nothing if fair values plus gap snapshots alone exceed the budget (pipeline.py:181-189); how many of the 109 scored zero variants is unverified. `constrained`, an executed variant, sits in the name-ordered 5-variant tail rotated by run_id % 5 (variants.py:243, pipeline.py:146-148), so it lands in positions 3-7 evenly and is dropped on (5-k)/5 of the ticks where only k tail variants fit; it is labelled per tick in variants_skipped and unlabelled per intent. On an idle box all seven scored in 19.5 s (journal 64) while under executor load ~30 s of a 45 s budget went to loading gap rows and as_measured (journal 68 ruling 2), so exhaustion is dominated by host/database contention. The phase 6 item 4 trigger (>= 10 % of game-day ticks, roadmap.md:286-287) is met against priced ticks (4.5x) and against fetched ticks (about 2x); the 09-10 UTC day ends before the Thursday kickoff, so the 45 % reflects game-day daytime ticks, not in-game ticks.

After Amendment 4 (a193fd0, 2026-09-08 11:44 CT; settings.py:31-39; tick.py:38-46, :164-173), pricing.budget_exhausted is true on 109/243 priced ticks on 09-10 (45 %, the one post-fix game day) and 43/281 on 09-09 (15 %, no games, uncapped 45 s at the 900 s cadence); the 09-07 (77/232) and pre-11:44 09-08 (36/73) figures belong to the retired 20 s regime (journal 57, 63) and do not count against the current design. Every true value means at least one secondary was skipped (pipeline.py:226-229), and on cadence-capped 20 s floor ticks the flag can also trip before any variant scores (pipeline.py:181-192), so the gate and primary are first but not guaranteed. Which secondaries drop is rotated by run_id % 5 by design (pipeline.py:143-146; spec §0.7) and reported per variant as table 1 tick_coverage; constrained is third on one tick in five, its only measured coverage is 0.7607 under the worse 20 s regime (evidence/2026-09-08-report-w37-coverage-1150.md), and its post-fix coverage is unverified. The dominant cost is the pipeline's own per-gap write volume (about 31k signal rows per tick at ~4k gaps, 2.0-4.7 s per variant, linear in gaps; signals 14.6M rows / 8.8 GB, evidence C) plus 15-30 s of stage 1-2 and gap-row loading, which reaches 35-50 s at ~4k gaps even at night with the executor idle (sample 10445, 00:46 CT, budget 45 uncapped); host I/O (executor contention, the nightly dump) tips a design already at the margin. The in-window 20 s floor is a recorded trade-off (sdd ledger 2026-09-08-phase4-sdd-ledger.md:30, :39; journal 64 ruling 2). The phase 6 item 4 trigger was already recorded as met on the pricing side on 09-08 (journal 56; phase 4 design spec line 123); read against the runs.budget_exhausted column it names (fetch-phase skips, tick.py:943-944, 1/day) it is not met, and a dedicated normalizer would not relieve the 900 s-cadence exhaustions of 09-09. Executor intake reads candidates inside the 900 s intent TTL (store.py:127-137, loop.py:406), so a skipped tick delays new constrained candidates by one rotation rather than silently changing existing intents; intent-level materiality is unverified. Severity: important as a throughput design item (budget, variant count, or signal write volume), not as a host-migration signal.

Severity important (not critical): the pricing budget is exhausted on 109/243 (45 %) of priced ticks on game day 09-10 even after Amendment 4 raised price_budget_s 20->45 (settings.py:33-39; evidence.md E), four times the phase 6 item 4 trigger (roadmap.md:287-288) that state.md:8 already recorded as met on 2026-09-08; the loss falls on the five rotating secondaries (pipeline.py:131-150, `constrained` is not fixed third, it is dropped with probability (7-k)/5 on a tick that scores k variants), never on the gate or primary, and is already labelled per tick (variants_skipped) and per variant in the weekly report's tick_coverage column (tables.py:333-415, journal 64), so the gate evaluation is unaffected and the recommendation to add a coverage line is already implemented. What the owner should do in the next 1-2 weeks: treat phase 6 item 4 (normalizer/pricer off the tick) or the host move as the one phase 6 item with measured evidence behind it, since journal 64/68 show the exhaustion is host I/O contention (all seven variants score in 19.5 s idle, 30 s of a 45 s budget goes to loading gap rows under executor load); and read Monday's table 1 tick_coverage column before drawing any secondary-variant conclusion. This finding does not bear on the one-open-position question: the single real fill is sharp_direct, which is scored on every tick.

Recommendation: phase 6 minor: give these three checks their own timeout (30-60 s) in a separate housekeeping sub-stage after the dump window, or narrow duplicate_trades to the last 24 h; update roadmap row 16 to reflect that the code landed and the acceptance ('pass within 2000 ms on NAS-sized tables') is what remains unmet. Does not bear on the Mac mini decision or the week-1 gate.
