Task-review fix-round rates: phase 4 12 of 17 tasks (11 one round, Task 6 two), phase 5 15 of 20 (14 one round, T14 two). Almost all of these are cross-task seams or in-code correctness defects, and almost all of the 20 production escapes (roadmap carried fixes 21-32, 34-41) are environmental or venue-behavioural rather than code-internal — but not all: carried fix 30 (roadmap.md:350, journal 89) was a pure in-code cross-task defect (float('nan') from harness/report/stats.py:31 reaching a jsonb upsert through snapshots/study.py:144) that both the task review and the phase 4.5 final review missed, and fixes 23/24 were decoder errors against the venue's documented shapes. The phase 5 plan (11,731 lines) carried wrong sample code that survived a 12-Critical plan review (journal 99) and was caught by review — two of the three at the final whole-branch review, one at task review (reports/2026-09-10-phase5.md:30 says "all caught by review", not "task review"). The phase 4.5 plan (8,453 lines) had a five-Critical plan review (journal 84) and no source attributes its Criticals to the plan's sample code.

Final reviews are the highest-yield stage in the pipeline: they caught defects that survived 20 task reviews and 15 fix rounds (phase 5 C1 veto grader, C2 annotator bullets — final-review.md:26-31 vs reports/2026-09-10-phase5.md:26), and they are not confined to code-internal defects — 3 of the 4 phase 4 findings are deploy/runbook/config (phase4-final-review.md:46-50, 101-110, 113-118), and phase 4.5 I5 and phase 5 I2/I3 are deploy-topology and resource findings. The real boundary is observability, not category: what is determinable from repo artifacts is caught by review (though imperfectly — fix 30's NaN at stats.py:181 and fix 41's 1,024-token ceiling are deterministic in-code defects that still escaped), while what depends on a live counterparty or live load (fixes 23, 24, 27, 28, 29, 38, 39, 40 venue/API shapes and rates; 26, 31, 34, 35 cold cache and swap) can only be found by the verify stage — which is where the adversarial review's §F rulings (R17 box sizing, R18 disk, U3 ceiling, R4 window) deliberately put it, and where roadmap.md:337-361 shows the loop actually found all ~20 escapes itself, within hours, before the user did.

Severity Important (confirm as claimed), because it is the only structural account of the project's defect distribution and it lands on the phase 6 planning gate inside the 1-2 week window — but restate the evidence and split the recommendation: the two-lens opus final review is demonstrably earning its seat (7 Criticals across phases 4/4.5/5, including one, veto.py:225-227, that would have made H9 measure nothing), while the escape channel is entirely environmental — roadmap.md:337-361 shows 21 of 22 carried fixes were found by verify or deploy on the live NAS and exactly one (fix 33) by a review — so the actionable half is adding an environment lens before the phase 6 branch (a deploy rehearsal against a live-shaped box, a real first call to every external API, and a measured frame/row rate for every new venue channel, which is precisely what fixes 37, 39 and 38/40 each cost after the fact), whereas capping plan sample code should be filed as an unproven experiment, not a prescription, since phase 5's wrong sample code was caught by review in every instance and its measured cost was fix rounds (14/20 tasks), not a production escape.

verified_findings.claim: state.md's header has read 'Updated: 2026-09-10 14:10 CT' since commit 8c422dd (09-10 13:55, itself stamped ahead of the clock) through 20 rewrites to 6eed2d8 (09-11 06:44). corrections: state.md's header has read "Updated: 2026-09-10 14:10 CT" since commit 8c422dd (09-10 13:55, itself stamped 15 minutes ahead of the clock) through 20 rewrites to 6eed2d8 (09-11 06:44) — a 16h34m-stale stamp on a file rewritten 20 times since. NAS on 3ca32dd = main" and "Branch: main at b4f0156 (NAS on 5f18601)" both contradict the Position line's "DEPLOYED 7c3d555": the NAS has taken three deploys since 3ca32dd (0488e22 journal 108, 5f18601 journal 110, 7c3d555 journal 112). A fresh session reading only state.md would misread the NAS build by three deploys; nearly every fact it needs is in journal 108-112 (open fix 33 only in journal 103 and the roadmap).

state.md is rewritten only in part at each unit boundary, and the lines it exclusively owns are the stale ones. Verified at HEAD 6eed2d8: :3 "Updated: 2026-09-10 14:10 CT" is byte-identical across all 21 blobs from 8c422dd (commit 09-10 13:55, stamped 15 min ahead) to 6eed2d8 (09-11 06:44) — 20 rewrites, no refresh — and survived 14ee721, a commit whose whole purpose was "state timestamps corrected to the commit times", which fixed :5 and left :3. :7 still names phase 5 task agents impl-5-T16/T11 9.5 h after journal 103 closed the phase (09-10 21:16 CT). The file carries three different NAS shas: :5 7c3d555 (correct, evidence.md:3/:937), :6 5f18601, :9 3ca32dd — a three-deploy gap (0488e22 journal 108, 5f18601 journal 110, 7c3d555 journal 112), and :9's "Deploys pending: none" contradicts :5's fixes 40-41 in flight. :11 stops at carried fix 32 against roadmap.md:337-361's 21-41. :14 day counters are dated 2026-09-09; :10 game window is Thu 09-10. :15 is 25 semicolon-joined items in 3,029 characters (not 1,900) and :12 adds a 616-character run-on whose "judge after 2026-09-09" items are two days past.

Two narrowings. First, the resume-hazard framing is overstated: the Position line :5 is current and correct, and SKILL.md forbids reading state.md alone — :453 mandates state.md plus the journal's last two entries plus the ledger, :56-58 Orient requires re-deriving from `git log`, `make status-nas` and the clock "never from memory", and :38-40 preflight checks the deployed stamp against main. A protocol-following resume recovers the build from three independent controls, so "would misread the NAS build" is a second-order risk, not the primary one. Second, the stale NAS/branch/carried-fix/game-window lines are redundant duplicates of fields whose authority is elsewhere (`make status-nas`, git, roadmap.md:337-361, the verify.md game-window query), which lowers their cost.

What survives, and is the real finding: the fields no other control re-derives are exactly the ones left stale. Day counters (SKILL.md:341 routes failure counts here; the ceilings table sets 2 failed deploys/day against them) have been dated 2026-09-09 through three deploys and a deploy recipe that failed twice at the schema step (journal 110) — the daily ceiling has no live counter. The R3 notification record (SKILL.md:50: "state.md records the day they ran") is unresolvable, since :4 and :14 both read "test notifications sent today: yes" under a 09-09 date; journal.md:328 shows the loop has already skipped a duty on the strength of that exact line ("already sent today at 11:15 CT per state.md; not repeated"), so the field is load-bearing, not cosmetic. And "Agents in flight" (SKILL.md:17, a state.md-only field) names dead agents. The defect is therefore partial-rewrite drift against the file's own contract (state.md:1 "rewritten ... at every unit boundary"; SKILL.md:387 same-commit update), with no ruling in the 2026-09-07 adversarial review sanctioning it. Severity: important for the day-counter/R3 control gap; minor for the duplicated NAS and carried-fix lines. Fix is cheap: the rewrite step should regenerate the whole file (clock-read stamp per the loop's own lesson on state.md:15), drop :6/:9/:11 in favour of their authorities, and split :12/:15 into bullets.

Severity: important (low end) — question: process. state.md's header stamp is frozen at 'Updated: 2026-09-10 14:10 CT' across 21 consecutive revisions of the file (8c422dd 09-10 13:55 → 6eed2d8 09-11 06:44), and only the Position line (:5) is actually rewritten per unit boundary: the remaining lines name three mutually exclusive NAS builds (:5 7c3d555, :6 5f18601, :9 3ca32dd = main; the truth is 7c3d555, evidence.md:3/:30), a stale HEAD (:6 b4f0156 vs 6eed2d8), carried fixes 21-32 omitting 16 and 33-41 (roadmap.md:335-361), phase-5 task agents 9.5 h after the phase closed (:7 vs journal 103, 21:16 CT), day counters two days old (:14), a past game window (:10), and a 3,030-character 25-item Lessons paragraph (:15). Correct the reviewer's two overstatements: the agents line is 9.5 h stale, not 16 h, and a compliant resume would NOT misread the build, because SKILL.md:17-22 and :453 already require the journal's last two entries and the ledger alongside state.md, and journal 111-112 carry 7c3d555 in full. It rates important rather than minor not on observed harm — there is none in 112 entries, and the R6 resume drill passed in both halves (journal 18, 29) — but because the file breaks its own contract as stated in SKILL.md:22 ('state.md carries what matters') on the single fact that gates a deploy, days before a Mac mini migration that forces a restart on a new host. Recommendation stands and is cheap: make state.md generated (header from TZ=America/Chicago date, Branch from git log -1, NAS build from /healthz, carried fixes from the roadmap table, Position from the journal's last heading) as a phase-6 item, and move the 25 Lessons into the skill as a checklist; until then the existing 'read the journal's last two entries' rule is the working mitigation and should be restated as 'the journal outranks state.md wherever they disagree'.

verified_findings.title: 'Nothing here can send an order to Kalshi' rests on software guards; the NAS key can sign writes
verified_findings.claim: README:154 states 'nothing here can send an order to Kalshi'. The production key on the NAS is the default write-scoped key: roadmap.md:114 says 'the default scope is write, so today the "no wagers" property rests only on software guards', the read-scoped-key TODO is still open (roadmap.md:319-320), and the phase 4 report §1 repeats 'the prod key today can sign writes'. app-run, app-ws and app-research mount that key (docker-compose.yml:75-88, 127-133). The fence is PaperModeViolation in http.py:104,177 plus make_writer's four-condition guard, and the demo smoke does place, amend and cancel real orders on the demo venue (journal 82: 15/15). README:161 also promises 'Game days (Thursday to Sunday) the system is watched, not touched', but Thu 09-10 had two deploys (journal 95, 98) and Fri 09-11 three (108, 110, 112), all inside R4's rule and outside the README's.

verified_findings.recommendation: Change README:154 to 'nothing here is allowed to send an order to Kalshi: a transport guard refuses every non-GET call and the writer needs four conditions that do not exist' and finish the read-scoped-key TODO (the one user action that makes the claim physical). Align README:161 with R4 or adopt a no-deploy Thu-Sun rule for operator mode (see P12).
corrections: README:154 states, without qualification, "nothing here can send an order to Kalshi" — and the README nowhere mentions the key scope, the demo venue, or the prod tripwire (grep: zero hits). The production key on the NAS is still the default write-scoped key: roadmap.md:114 says "the default scope is write, so today the 'no wagers' property rests only on software guards", the read-scoped-key TODO is still open (roadmap.md:319-320), and the phase 4 report §1 (reports/2026-09-09-phase4.md:8) repeats "the prod key today can sign writes; only the paper guard and the tripwire stop them". Two containers mount that key — app-run (docker-compose.yml:75-76, 87-88) and app-ws (127-133) — and neither runs the execution loop; app-research mounts only the Anthropic key (docker-compose.yml:164-170, ruling A-M2, verified live in journal 109) and app-exec has no volumes and no credentials at all (docker-compose.yml:144-146), so for the executor the separation is physical. The software fence is PaperModeViolation (http.py:104, raised at :177 and :188), KalshiTransport's writes_enabled=False default (authed.py:150, :167), and make_writer's four-condition guard (LIVE_CONDITIONS, authed.py:1301, enforced :1368-1376). Two residual honesty gaps: the harness demonstrably can send orders to Kalshi's demo venue — place, amend, cancel, expiry, 15/15 (journal 82) — which the README's absolute never mentions; and docker-compose.yml:73-74 asserts "Both key files are read-scoped", contradicting roadmap.md:114. README:161 also promises "Game days (Thursday to Sunday) the system is watched, not touched", but Thu 09-10 had two deploys (journals 95, 98) and Fri 09-11 three (108, 110, 112). All five were journaled as outside any game window and are permitted by R4 (roadmap.md:52); the conflict is that the README's public promise is stricter than the rule the loop actually follows, not that a rule was broken. Severity: important (documentation honesty and one unearned physical-safety property), not critical.

README:154 ("nothing here can send an order to Kalshi") is accurate as a statement about the deployed software, and is stronger than "software guards": the paper transport holds no write-capable HTTP client at all (http.py:167, _ReadOnlyClient at :77-102), scheduler.py:68-72 builds the only long-running prod transport with writes_enabled=False, KalshiWriter is unconstructible outside make_writer (_FACTORY_TOKEN, authed.py:526/940-953), make_writer's prod branch fails on all four LIVE_CONDITIONS (authed.py:1298) — condition 3 provably, since gate_reports has 0 rows — and would default caps to zero anyway (authed.py:1394-1397). The property is also continuously measured, not just asserted: the venue_requests prod tripwire requires non-GET = 0 AND prod GET > 0 (verify.md:158, :369), is kept non-vacuous by the hourly limits read (recorder/tick.py:372), and has read 0 non-GET at every check (phase4 report line 3; journal 1016, 1024, 1039, 1055, 1074). Phase 5's RFQ path is fenced by a repo-wide static test (tests/test_rfq_refusal.py: no file under harness/ contains "communications/quotes"; rfq_socket.py imports no HTTP client).

The residual, correctly stated, is Minor-to-Important credential hygiene, not a false README claim: the production key's scope is unverified — reports/2026-09-09-phase4.md:8 and journal 1242 assume it can sign writes, while journal 74 records the user replacing both key files and revoking the old key on 2026-09-07 10:54 CT with the F64 TODO left open only because the user never confirmed (reports/2026-09-07-drill.md:11). Until confirmed, the blast radius of an exfiltrated secrets/kalshi_private_key.pem is write-capable even though nothing in the harness can use it that way. The phase 4 report itself grades the fix "Optional, your call".

The demo-smoke citation (journal 82, 15/15) does not weaken README:154: separate account, no funds, non-interchangeable credentials (roadmap.md:116), hostname-asserted on the parsed host (authed.py:1358-1361), and run only as a controller one-off `docker compose run` (journal 828 ruling).

Separately and at Minor: README:161 ("Game days, Thursday to Sunday, the system is watched, not touched") lacks R4's deploy carve-out (roadmap.md:52, :64). All five deploys (journals 95, 98, 108, 110, 112) ran 03:12-07:14 CT with game window 0|0|0 and 12+ hours before kickoff, so R4 was honored; the README sentence should read "not touched inside the game windows" or name R4.

SEVERITY: minor (documentation accuracy), question: process. Three documents overstate or misstate the paper-mode safety property, while the property itself is held by four independent layers. (1) README.md:154 says "nothing here can send an order to Kalshi"; the accurate statement is "nothing here is allowed to send an order to Kalshi" — the production key is still default write-scoped (roadmap.md:114, reports/2026-09-09-phase4.md:8, F64 open at roadmap.md:319-320), so the property rests on software: app-exec holds no credential at all (docker-compose.yml:145-146), the two containers that do hold it (app-run docker-compose.yml:87-88, app-ws :135-137) build transports with writes_enabled=False and raise PaperModeViolation before signing (harness/venues/kalshi/http.py:176, and again at :189 as an -O-proof second guard), and make_writer refuses a prod writer on four conditions all false today plus a fifth key-file check (harness/venues/kalshi/authed.py:1367-1382), with KalshiWriter unconstructable outside the factory token (:952-953). Last verified tripwire: 5 GET rows, 0 non-GET on env='prod' (reports/2026-09-09-phase4.md line 3); the current-day count is unverified. (2) docker-compose.yml:74-75 flatly asserts "Both key files are read-scoped" — false as of today and contradicting roadmap.md:114; this is the sharpest of the three and the one-line fix. (3) README.md:161's "Game days (Thursday to Sunday) the system is watched, not touched" does not match R4 (roadmap.md:52), the rule actually followed; all five cited deploys (journals 95, 98, 108, 110, 112) ran between 03:12 and 07:14 CT, outside every R4 window and every game. ACTION: fix the docker-compose comment and the two README sentences (README:161 to point at R4 rather than at days of the week), and do the F64 read-scoped key swap opportunistically during today's Mac mini migration, when the secrets are being recopied anyway — not as a standalone interrupt. CORRECTION TO THE ORIGINAL FINDING: app-research does not mount the Kalshi key (docker-compose.yml:163-166).

corrections:
The "Needs you" channel does not close: the fair_stale strategy question is ~44 h old (first journaled as an observation at entry 82, 2026-09-09 10:56 CT: 150 orders placed 08:04, 147 cancelled fair_stale by 10:24 — journal.md:1075), mis-attributed, and mis-framed. Worse than stale: the question as posed cannot be answered as written. It offers the user two levers, and neither is one the user can usefully pull. The staleness bound in the rule is max(variant.stale_s, stale_allowance_s) (harness/execution/plan.py:446-456); variant.stale_s = 180 is frozen by invariant 1 (harness/variants/*.yaml:15,17), and stale_allowance_s is a derived settings value the loop already owns (harness/pricing/fair.py:30-40: odds_alt_interval_near_s/far_s 120 or FEATURED_CADENCE_S 120, plus tick_budget_s 100 = 220 s). The "15-minute pricing cadence" is not a setting either — harness/recorder/cadence.py:33 hard-codes `return 900` under ALLOWED_CADENCES (harness/recorder/tick.py:765) — and the field data says it is not the mechanism: evidence.md:965 finds fair_values refreshing every 1-3.5 min (median ~2 min) for game 16, stale_allowance_at_place = 220 s on every one of the 7,825 orders (p25 = p95 = 220, evidence.md:679-681) with staleness_at_place p50 67 s, so cancels fire when a refresh is late by >~2.5 min (a 100 s+ executor loop, or a tick with no pricing), not on a 15-minute clock.

The loop has precedent for deciding a pricing setting itself by dated amendment rather than asking: Amendment 4 (journal 61 ruling D8; journal 63) raised price_budget_s from 20 to 45 mid-phase, deployed by the controller (harness/config/settings.py:32-40). Note that amendment moved the per-tick pricing time BUDGET, not the cadence — so it is a precedent for the loop amending a pricing setting under its own authority, not evidence that the cadence is settings-controlled. Combined with the user's standing instruction to research and recommend strategy and ask only operational questions (memory strategy-trust-model.md), the correct action was to diagnose the 220 s allowance against observed refresh lateness and propose an amendment, not to carry an unanswerable multiple-choice question across three reports.

The same channel failure shows in the fix 20 nag (copy the backup private key off the Mac), open since 2026-09-08 21:17 CT (roadmap.md:340) and repeated verbatim in all three reports (phase4.md:6, phase4.5.md:6, phase5.md:10) with no escalation, no alternative, and no deadline.

The fair_stale item in "Needs you" is mis-framed rather than merely unanswered, and the framing was never re-derived from the data in three consecutive reports (2026-09-09-phase4.5.md:8; 2026-09-10-phase5.md:11). It is put to the user as a choice between "the 15-minute pricing cadence" and "the staleness bound," but neither number is the one that fires: the game-window cadence is 120 s (harness/recorder/cadence.py:29-30) and the binding threshold is stale_allowance_s = 220 s (harness/pricing/fair.py:23,30-40), measured at exactly 220 on all 7,825 fair_stale orders (evidence.md:732), above the variant's stale_s 180. The actual driver is in the loop's own scope: cancels fire when a fair refresh is late by more than ~220 s because of executor loops of 100+ s or a tick that priced nothing (evidence.md:965), with pricing-budget exhaustion on 45 % of priced ticks on 09-10 and 49 % on 09-08 (evidence.md:966) — 4.5x the explicit phase 6 trigger at roadmap.md:287 ("Dedicated normalizer process only if `budget_exhausted` appears on >= 10 % of game-day ticks"), which the loop has measured but not yet acted on. Severity: the real finding is that the loop is carrying a triggered, in-scope engineering item (roadmap.md:287) as a user strategy question, which also delays the answer the user actually needs. Two sub-findings are minor: the phase 4.5 report attributes the observation to the phase 4 report, which does not contain it (journal 82, 2026-09-09 10:56 CT, is the origin; journal 57 has the earlier skip-reason ancestor); and carried fix 20 is not a loop failure at all — roadmap.md:340 records it as "n/a (user action)" with "none" for deploy, so only the user can close it. The claim that "the pricing cadence is a settings value the loop already changed once by dated amendment (Amendment 4)" should be dropped entirely: Amendment 4 changed price_budget_s (a within-tick compute allocation) and explicitly left the cadence and tick_budget_s untouched (harness/config/settings.py:36-40; phase 4 design spec:15,95,144), and the only cadence change on record was made under the user's standing authorization U1.

Severity: important (confirmed, not downgraded) — but re-scope the finding from "the item is 46 h old" to "the item is unanswerable as written, and it gates the week-1 gate read." All eight cited facts verify, including the mis-attribution (phase 4 report contains zero 'fair_stale' occurrences; the observation originated as a plan-next note in journal 82 and the phase 4.5 report invented its provenance). A 12.2 min median time-in-book therefore means the cancel fired when a refresh ran ~2.5 min late (a 100 s+ executor loop or an unpriced tick), so fair_stale is substantially a NAS-latency artifact rather than a strategy parameter — which folds this item into questions 3 and 4 as well as question 2. It is important rather than critical because paper mode puts no capital at risk and one settings change reverses it; it is important rather than minor because it is the terminal state of 97.8% of the order book (7,825/7,997), it killed the only real queue_model fill (order 157, 38.92 contracts), and the first gate evaluation on Mon 2026-09-14 09:00 CT will otherwise score week 1 on ~0 resting orders. refuted_findings.title: README overstates freshness and hides the operative caps
refuted_findings.claim: README:44 says 'Every two minutes or so the system pulls the current lines'; the featured odds fetch and pricing run on a 15-minute daytime cadence (journal 79; settings.py:47-50 give 120 s only for alternates inside 36 h) and the evidence shows 243 priced ticks on 09-10, about one per 6 minutes. The gap is the mechanism behind fair_stale cancels (7,825 of 7,997 orders, avg 33.7 min in book). README:69-72 honestly says only `constrained` enforces caps (apply_caps true only in constrained.yaml:23) but lists 'at most 25 open orders' as a cap while the operative one is exec_max_open_orders = 150 shared across three variants, which bound at 150 in 40 of 53 game-window hours (evidence D3) and is never mentioned.
reasons:
evidence: The caps half verifies cleanly; the freshness half — the headline and the claimed causal mechanism for 7,825 fair_stale cancels — is wrong on the code and contradicted by the reviewer's own cited evidence section.

VERIFIED CITATIONS
- README.md:44 quote is literal: "Every two minutes or so the system pulls the current lines from the sharp books and every price on Kalshi."
- README.md:70-71 literally lists "at most 25 open orders"; :71-72 literally says "Most strategy variants only note when a cap would have applied; one variant, `constrained`, actually enforces them".
- apply_caps: true only in constrained.yaml:23; false in the other 6 (sharp_two_sided.yaml:25, others :23). All 7 carry max_open: 25.
- settings.py:64 `exec_max_open_orders: int = 150  # D10: shared across the executed variants`; enforced at plan.py:609 (`still_open < s.max_open_orders`), while variant max_open 25 is only a label (plan.py:412, strategy/run.py:368) gated by apply_caps.
- README never mentions the 150 bound: grep "150" in README hits only line 139 ("150 pretend fills", a gate criterion), not the open-order cap.
- brief:20 fair_stale 7,825; brief:19 7,997 orders. Evidence §G confirms n=7825, tib_p50 12.2 min.
- journal 79 (journal.md:1039) does literally contain "pricing on the 15-minute cadence".

REFUTING FINDINGS
1. "settings.py:47-50 give 120 s only for alternates inside 36 h" is FALSE. The featured-odds/pricing cadence is not in settings.py at all — it is harness/recorder/cadence.py:16-33 `interval_for`: 20 s for NFL at T-60..T-100 min (:26-27), **120 s whenever a sport has a game in progress or on the day's card, from 3 h before first kickoff through last kickoff (:29-30)**, 300 s on weekends (:31-32), and 900 s only as the quiet-weekday fallback (:33), with no fetch 01:00-08:00 local (:21-22). tick.py:155-161 `cadence_in_force` takes the min across sports and that is the wall clock pricing runs against (tick.py:164-173). So 120 s is the operative game-window featured cadence, which is exactly what README:44 describes. The 15-minute figure is the game-free weekday fallback (tick.py:50 DEFAULT_CADENCE_S = 900).
2. journal 79 is dated 2026-09-09, a **Wednesday** — a game-free weekday. journal.md:1111 makes this explicit: "about 1,870 used in 24 h (a Wednesday on the 15-minute weekday cadence)... not an anomaly on a game-free weekday." The quote is real but does not generalize to game windows, which is when orders are placed.
3. The reviewer's own cited evidence refutes them. evidence.md §F:672 reads: "on Thu evening the game-16 fair values refreshed every 1-3.5 min (median gap ~2 min, 46 rows per run), **not every 15 min**." The 100 sampled fair runs span 2026-09-10 21:01Z-00:34Z (3.55 h) = one per 2.1 min.
4. "243 priced ticks on 09-10, about one per 6 minutes" is arithmetically right (1440/243 = 5.9) but is a 24 h average across a day with a 7 h no-fetch window (cadence.py:21-22) and a bimodal 120 s / 900 s split. It cannot be used to infer a uniform cadence, and §F measures the game-window value directly at ~2 min.
5. The causal claim ("the gap is the mechanism behind fair_stale cancels") is contradicted by evidence §G: staleness_at_place p25/p50/p75/p95 = 57/67/77/94 s against stale_allowance 220 s on every order (p25 = p95 = 220). Fair values are ~1 minute old at placement, not 15. plan.py:446-456 fires fair_stale only above max(stale_s 180, allowance 220) = 220 s. A better-supported mechanism sits in the same evidence file, uncited: evidence §E:558 — 109 of 243 priced ticks on 09-10 (45 %) exhausted the 45 s pricing budget, so individual markets go unpriced within a tick (sample 10445: 3,929 gaps in one tick).
6. "bound at 150 in 40 of 53 game-window hours (evidence D3)" — actual count is **36** of 53 rows at mx = 150, not 40. Also the 53 rows are every hour with samples across 3 days (including 00:00, 01:00 and 08:00-15:00 hours), not "game-window hours".

alternative: The load-bearing half of the claim (freshness/mechanism) rests on a misread of where the cadence lives, and field data contradicts it directly.

1) The 15-minute figure is one of five cadence tiers, not "the" cadence. harness/recorder/cadence.py:16-33 (`interval_for`) returns: None 01:00-08:00 local when nothing is in progress; 20 s for NFL 60-100 min before kickoff; 120 s whenever a game of that sport is in progress or from 3 h before today's first kickoff through the last kickoff; 300 s on weekends; 900 s only on a weekday outside every game window. The reviewer cites settings.py:47-50 and concludes 120 s exists "only for alternates inside 36 h" -- but the featured 120 s is in cadence.py:29-30 and is restated as a design constant at harness/pricing/fair.py:23-24 (`FEATURED_CADENCE_S = 120`, "Featured-market lines refresh every tick"). The reviewer never read cadence.py, so the central evidentiary support for "README:44 is wrong" is absent. README:44's "every two minutes or so" is the game-window tier and the harness's own named constant.

2) Field data measures ~2 min, not 15. evidence.md §F: fair_values for game_id 16 over 2026-09-10 21:01 - 2026-09-11 00:34 UTC (16:01-19:34 CT) refresh 100 times at 1-3.5 min spacing (median ~2.1 min), 46 rows per run -- during exactly the hours §D3 shows open_orders pinned at 150. The "243 priced ticks on 09-10 = one per 6 min" figure is a 24 h average across four tiers including a ~7 h null window (cadence.py:21-22); it is not the refresh interval any resting order experienced.

3) The distribution rules out a flat 15-min cadence as the mechanism. The bound is `max(variant.stale_s=180, stale_allowance_s)` (plan.py:446-456), and `stale_allowance_s` = FEATURED_CADENCE_S 120 + tick_budget_s 100 = 220 s (fair.py:30-40), matching §G exactly (allow p25=p50=p75=p95=220 on all 7,825; feed_kind featured on 7,959/7,997). §G also shows staleness_at_place p50 = 67 s, p95 = 94 s -- the sharp line is ~1 min old at placement. Under a genuine 900 s cadence an order placed on a 67 s-old fair would be cancelled ~153 s later, i.e. ~2.5 min in book. Observed time-in-book is p50 12.2 min, p75 35.3 min, p95 147.0 min (§G). Orders survive many refresh cycles and die on an occasional missed one; a flat 15-min cadence cannot produce a 147-minute p95.

4) The cancels are the specified design and are not hidden. `fair_stale` is finding F36 of the adversarial review (docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-09-07-autopilot-adversarial-review.md:46, "FIX in phase 3", prescribing the exact `now - fair_ts > max(cfg["stale_s"], stale_allowance_s)` rule now at plan.py:446-456). The churn was journaled at first sight (journal 82, "147 cancelled fair_stale between 08:06 and 10:24 CT ... deserves a look in the phase report's numbers") and put to the user as an open strategy question in the phase 4.5 report line 8, repeated in the phase 5 report (brief line 28).

5) The real defect the data supports is a code inconsistency, not a README one: `stale_allowance_s()` (fair.py:23, 30-40) hard-codes the 120 s tier while `interval_for` can return 300 or 900 for the same market, so the allowance never tracks `cadence_in_force` -- which tick.py:914-917 already computes for the pricing budget. §G's sport/ttk split supports this narrowed version: 5,811 of 7,825 fair_stale cancels (74 %) are ncaaf, and `interval_for` is per-sport, so ncaaf drops to the 300/900 s tier on a day with no college game while NFL markets on the same evening reprice every ~2 min. Editing README:44 fixes nothing; deriving the allowance from the cadence in force would.

6) On the caps half, the README is accurate where the reviewer says it misleads. plan.py:547 (`blocking = bool(cfg["apply_caps"])`) and strategy/run.py:371-372 show `max_open: 25` IS evaluated for every variant and blocks only for constrained -- precisely what README:71-72 says ("Most strategy variants only note when a cap would have applied; one variant, `constrained`, actually enforces them"). `exec_max_open_orders = 150` is a different object: an engine-level capacity bound producing `Skip(EXEC_CAPACITY)` (plan.py:97, 107, 551-553, 609), not a bankroll cap, and README §"How much it bets" is a bankroll-sizing section. So "hides the operative caps" is wrong; "omits an engine bound that matters" is right. The reviewer's D3 count is also overstated: 36 of 53 hourly rows hit mx=150 (counted from evidence §D3), not 40, and those 53 rows are hours with executor samples, not "game-window hours".

What survives: README never mentions 150 anywhere (grep README.md for "150|open order": hits at :56, :70-71, :139, :153, none the executor bound), and the shared 150 does bind and does confound the constrained-vs-unconstrained comparison, since all three variants' intents compete for the same 150 slots sorted by descending edge (plan.py:602-604). That is a real but different and lesser finding than the one claimed.

materiality: Two halves, both mis-cut. (a) The freshness half is contradicted by the field data the finding itself cites. `_fair_stale` is measured against `fair_values.fair_ts`, not the odds fetch (harness/execution/plan.py:446-451, threshold max(stale_s 180, allowance 220) = 220 s, and evidence.md §G shows stale_allowance_at_place = 220 on all 7,825 rows). Evidence.md §F shows game-16 fair values refreshing every 1-3.5 min (median ~2 min, 46 rows/run, 100 runs in 3.5 h on 09-10 evening) — i.e. the README's "every two minutes or so" matches the fair-value cadence in the window that produces orders, and a 15-minute *featured odds* pull (journal:287 "the featured fetch keeps its 15-minute cadence") cannot by itself trip a 220 s bound on fair_ts. The "243 priced ticks = one per 6 minutes" figure is a whole-day average diluted by unpriced night hours, not the game-window cadence. A likelier mechanism, unexamined by the finding, is pricing-budget exhaustion: evidence.md §E shows 109 of 243 priced ticks (45 %) on 09-10 hit `budget_s` 45, and sample run 10445 dropped `wide_band` from `variants_run` mid-list, so coverage truncation leaves some markets unrefreshed past 220 s. Acting on the finding would point the owner at the wrong lever on the one carried strategy question he still owes an answer to (phase4.5 report line 8). (b) The caps half is factually right — constrained.yaml:23 is the only `apply_caps: true` of seven; settings.py:64 `exec_max_open_orders: int = 150  # D10: shared across the executed variants`; plan.py:609 gates on a single `still_open < s.max_open_orders` counter with placeable intents globally sorted by descending edge (plan.py:602-604); evidence.md §D3 shows 36 of 53 hours pinned at exactly 150 (the finding says 40, a slight overcount) — but the recommendation is a README prose rewrite, which changes nothing the owner does in the next 1-2 weeks. He has already been told the operative consequence in owner-facing form (phase 5 report line 11: "1,466 orders placed and cancelled between 16:25 and 20:35 CT to arrive at 150 resting ones"), so the README omission is not what is holding back a decision. The genuinely material fact buried under the doc framing is the *shared, edge-ranked* nature of the 150 cap: when it binds (36/53 hours), the three variants compete for one queue and the higher-intent-volume variant crowds the others out (orders 4,953 sharp_two_sided / 2,650 sharp_direct / 390 constrained, brief line 19), which contaminates the cross-variant comparison the experiment exists to run. That belongs as its own experiment-design finding, not as a README §3 edit.

Item 5 is half done, not done: carried fix 12 (journal entry 19 ruling 2, line 248; verified entry 28, line 367: "NFL 772 markets 100 % matched ... 0 unmatched") closed the bare-city alias half, while the alias-pass automation half remains a manual operator duty (roadmap.md:304) and global matching is 81.5 % (brief: 4,959 of 6,084 venue_markets; NFL's current rate unverified). Item 3 DOES touch week-1..3 measurement — t9 is a live report table key for spec hypothesis H3 (tables.py:53, :1589 "H3's flow imbalance is a later phase."; spec §9 lines 220, 266) — but it is safely deferrable because the inputs are already recorded (venue_trades 1.97 M rows; taker side on both paths since carried fix 1), so H3 can be back-computed after the experiment at zero data cost. Item 4's trigger is met on the pricing-side reading (evidence E: 109 of 243 priced ticks on 09-10 = 45 %; 4.9 % of all 2,220 ticks that day, and the tick-level boolean budget_exhausted is 1/day), and the project already ruled it this way and deprioritised it: phase4 design doc:123, "the 10 % threshold is now measured as met on the pricing side; §6.1 relieves the symptom, the normalizer stays phase 6"; Amendment 4 (docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-09-07-phase2-preregistration.md:117-125, confirmed live by evidence sample 10445's order list) keeps the gate variant and primary at 100 % tick coverage but explicitly leaves secondary coverage asymmetric and flags table 2 and family C as touched. Item 2 is uncited and unverified. Item 7's trigger fires (31 % free, evidence A) but has fired continuously since 2026-09-07 (journal entries 8 and 16, lines 100 and 219) and is driven by 7.5 TB of unrelated user data; archiving harness partitions reclaims ~46 GB of 11 TB. The real argument for touching sealed partitions is performance, not space: pgdata sits on the single rotational HDD (evidence A:24) and the nightly 1.3 GB pg_dump plus the RFQ replay drove exec.loop_ms to 235-336 s (journal entries 109/110), which makes item 7 the only phase 6 item adjacent to the measured blocker. Citation hygiene: the three journal references are line numbers, not entry numbers — journal.md has 112 entries; read them as entries 19, 28 and 13.

Phase 6 as written contains no fix for the actual blocker — the fair_stale cancel churn (7,825 of 7,993 cancels, avg 33.7 min in book; `stale_allowance_at_place` = 220 s on every order, evidence G; `harness/execution/plan.py:446-456`), which is an unanswered user question carried since the phase 4.5 report (reports/2026-09-09-phase4.5.md:8). That is the correct headline. But the per-item ranking behind it does not hold: item 5 is half done (fix 12 closed the NFL bare-city pair, journal.md:367, but the alias-pass automation is unshipped and the live match rate is 81.5 %, 1,125 of 6,084 venue markets unmatched, brief:22 — and the manual pass it replaces costs ~6-9 full deploys over the 3-week window, each a cold-cache storm per journal 109/110 and carried fixes 34/37); item 4 is a pre-registered measurement item at 4.5x its own trigger (109/243 = 45 % vs 10 %, evidence E) and Amendment 4 (preregistration.md:123) names the damage to table 2 and family C rather than curing it; item 1 is blocked by `MAX_SECONDARY = 6` (harness/strategy/variants.py:60, already at 6 active secondaries) and needs a user decision plus a dated amendment, and adds ~2.1 s/tick to the budget item 4 is about; item 3 makes H3 unmeasurable for all three weeks (`tables.py:1589` `_not_collected("t9", "flow", ...)`; H3 pre-registered at adversarial-review.md:108); item 6's "no failing consumer" is a vacuous pass — R11's gate criterion (phase3 design spec:13) exists precisely so the check "cannot pass vacuously", and with one queue_model fill ever the set it measures is empty; item 7's trigger has been tripped since 2026-09-07 (journal.md:100, :219, "3.5T free of 11T (31 %)") on media, not harness data, with ~380 days of runway at 8.94 GB/day — the trigger's definition is the defect, and the real archiving value is IO on a rotational pgdata volume (evidence A/B), which belongs to the host decision. Only item 2 (duplicate quote rows) is fairly characterised as hygiene. Correct ranking: the unanswered fair_stale/cadence question and `intents_without_order_or_skip` = 483 (evidence I) outrank everything in phase 6; within phase 6, items 4 and 5 are due now on the roadmap's own stated triggers, item 6 is gate-relevant but untestable until fills exist, item 1 is user-gated, and items 2, 3 and 7 are deferrable — 7 only after its trigger is rewritten to count harness-owned bytes.
