corrections:
The harness's own integrity wall is partly blind and partly failing. At the 2026-09-11 04:15 CT housekeeping (evidence §I, all rows ts 09:15:53Z), of 27 checks 23 pass, three skip on 'timeout' — duplicate_trades, fair_values_negative_feed_lag, fair_values_negative_staleness — and one fails: intents_without_order_or_skip = 483 against a threshold of 0.

The three skips mean fix 32's closing criterion (roadmap.md:352, "the three skipped checks pass at the next housekeeping") is not met on the first housekeeping after its 2026-09-10 07:13 CT deploy, and db.brin_ranges_summarized = 0 at the same timestamp (evidence D5) shows autosummarize is working and is not the remaining cause. Carried fix 16 (roadmap.md:339), which owns two of the three statements, is still open as "phase work — the next plan-next's first task". Journal 92 (journal.md:1196) already ruled the skips "FAIL by environment, deferred ... the skip is the honest state; a wider timeout would starve the executor", and journal 109 (journal.md:1317) notes the same three skip "as after every restart" on a cold box — the 04:15 CT sample ran ~30 min after the 03:16-03:45 CT dump/RFQ storm and the 03:29 CT restart, so it is one post-fix data point, not a measured steady state.

The 483 failure means 483 non-replay intents in the 24 h window had no order, no 'skipped' event, and no order working on their (variant_id, venue_market_id, side) key at their created_at (harness/ops/checks.py:192-232). The likely cause is not intents aging past exec_intent_ttl_s (900 s): the largest observed loop is 336 s (evidence D1) and the largest skipped-loop run is 24 periods ≈ 360 s (evidence D), both well short of 900 s. The likely cause is the executor's supersession path — harness/execution/store.py:280-288 loads only the newest intent per key inside the TTL, and harness/execution/plan.py:431/581/602 drop every non-newest and every blocked-key intent with no action at all — while pricing re-creates an intent per key every 1-3.5 min (evidence §F). The check excuses a superseded intent only when an order was working on its key at creation time, and with exec.open_orders averaging 0.3 over the last 6 h most superseded intents have no such order. This is therefore most likely the same class of check-definition gap phase 4.5 corrected once for the hold path (journal 88, journal.md:1041: 2,452 of 2,459 intents "superseded by the next pricing run's intent"), and belongs with fix 16 as phase work — not as an executor-liveness or TTL-tuning item. Confirming which mechanism dominates needs one query the review has not run: the created_at distribution and per-key counts of the 483 rows.

Two separate, smaller findings, neither of which is "the integrity checks do not run" (23 of 27 pass at 04:15 CT on 09-11, and the one that fails is one that ran):

(a) Scheduling defect, minor: housekeeping's daily gate is DUE_HOUR_UTC = 9 (harness/ops/housekeeping.py:47, _due at :333-336), so the 27 checks fire on the first settle tick after 04:00 CT — roughly 30 minutes after the 1.3 GB nightly pg_dump finishes (03:46 CT, evidence §A) has flushed the page cache on a rotational pgdata volume. The three heaviest checks (duplicate_trades over the growing week-37 venue_trades partition, and the two 24 h fair_values scans) therefore blow the fixed 2 s SET LOCAL statement_timeout (harness/ops/checks.py:25) and record the designed `skip` (checks.py:1-9, :380-388). This is not fix 16 being open — fix 16's bounds are in the code (checks.py:46-82, :174-180, :253-260) — and it is not fix 32 failing: db.brin_ranges_summarized = 0 in the same sample (evidence §D5) shows autosummarize has nothing left to do, and journal 93 measured the same fair_values check at 141 ms warm. Fix 32's verify clause "the three skipped checks pass at the next housekeeping" (roadmap.md:352) is unmet, but journal 92 already ruled the skip "FAIL by environment, deferred ... the skip is the honest state". The remedy is a schedule change (run the checks on a settle tick well away from the dump, or re-run only skipped checks once later in the day), not a wider timeout; the durable exposure is that duplicate_trades will keep skipping as the weekly partition grows, so one check with real content (the REST/WS trade dedupe, guarded only by a non-unique index, schema.py:495) is effectively unaudited.

(b) The 483 is an executor-throughput artifact plus a known check-definition gap, not TTL expiry and not 483 lost intents. exec_intent_ttl_s (900 s) cannot orphan an intent: the loop inserts and loads intents in the same body against the same `lower` bound (harness/execution/loop.py:406-410), and the worst observed loop is 336 s (evidence §D1). The code paths that actually leave an intent with no order and no `skipped` event are (i) in-loop supersession — only the newest intent per (variant_id, venue_market_id, side) is ever acted on (store.py:257-269; plan.py:581), so any loop spanning two or more pricing runs silently drops the older siblings; (ii) the hold path on a key blocked by a resting order that was not working at the intent's created_at, the remainder the phase 4.5 §0.4a excuse deliberately does not cover; (iii) a Place/Skip whose per-action savepoint rolled back on an error (loop.py:960-968). The 150-order cap is NOT one of them (plan.py:552 writes an exec_capacity Skip). 483 is ~1.5 % of a day's intents, and the same check read 0/pass 24 h earlier (journal 92), so its real signal is the 09-10 game-night and 03:16-03:45 storm loop inflation (evidence §D2: p95 101-115 s against a 15 s period), i.e. the same NAS-throughput root cause the rest of the review is chasing. One query settles it: group the 483 by hour and by whether a newer intent exists on the same key within five minutes.

Severity important (unchanged), because it is the one finding that forces a caveat into Monday 09-14's first gate report and it is direct evidence for questions 3-4 — but the claim needs three corrections. (a) Fix 16's prescribed bounds are ALREADY implemented and deployed: duplicate_trades names the weekly partition through sql_for (harness/ops/checks.py:57-65 and 70-85), fair_values_negative_staleness is bounded to 24 h (checks.py:177-181), fair_values_negative_feed_lag likewise (checks.py:253-260), and commits 06cff74, 40d3cca, 36f8b70 are all ancestors of the running build 7c3d555. The residual cause is therefore not an unwritten fix but the flat 2,000 ms STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS (checks.py:25) applied at 04:15 CT against a page cache churned by the 03:30 CT 1.3 GB nightly dump on rotational pgdata (evidence A); the recommendation must change from "bound the statements (fix 16 as specified)" to "move housekeeping off the dump window, or give the tape/fair_values checks their own timeout, and re-measure cold". Separately, roadmap.md:339 is stale — it still reads "**phase work** ... the next plan-next's first task" for work that shipped 2026-09-08 — which will misdirect the next plan-next. (b) The materiality is concentrated in duplicate_trades, not the three together: the (venue, trade_id) index is non-unique and the PK includes ts by partitioning necessity (models.py:185-192), so a WS/REST double-print is structurally possible and only this dark check would see it; the two fair_values sign checks are minor. (c) The 483 is best stated as a symptom, severity minor on its own: intents older than exec_intent_ttl_s 900 (settings.py:65) are silently excluded at harness/execution/loop.py:406 with no event written, while the capacity path does write Skip(EXEC_CAPACITY) (harness/execution/plan.py:552), so slow loops (09-10 19:00 CT avg 27.5 s / p95 115 s, max 336 s on 09-11; exec_heartbeat loops_skipped 521 of 17,138) are the plausible cause — ~1.7 % funnel loss with near-zero economic loss, worth the Skip(ttl_expired) row but not a week-2 headline.

verified_findings.title: Missing from phase 6: a load test against a NAS-sized database before any further phase deploy
verified_findings.claim: Every phase deploy since 4.5 produced a storm (journal 89, 109, 110) because local measurements did not reflect the NAS (builders 26-103 ms locally vs 12.5 s on the NAS; the RFQ lateral 10 ms warm vs 14 s cold; three checks over their 2 s budget), and nothing in the phase 6 list adds a scale test.
verified_findings.question: phase6
evidence: journal 89 (line 1170): 'the plan's local measurements (26-103 ms at 2x season) did not reflect the NAS'
journal 109: 11 RFQ quote timeouts, pulse self-guard tripped, floor funnel timing out
roadmap.md:355 fix 35: 16,264 rows read for 236 kept, 14 s cold / 10 ms warm
evidence.md A: nightly dump 1.3 GB at 03:44 CT exists; backups dir with restore drill (fix 20/phase 4 D10)
tests/ listing: no scale or NAS-sized fixture beyond fixture_day.py / day_synthetic
verified_findings.recommendation: Week 2 (needs the Mac mini or a scratch Postgres on the Mac): restore the nightly dump into a scratch database, run every snapshot builder, every check statement and every executor read cold, record p95 per statement in evidence, and make 'cold p95 under budget on the scratch restore' a gate in verify.md for phase 6 tasks that add a read. Cost M. When: by 09-21, before any phase 6 deploy.
corrections: Both phase deploys since 4.5 stormed the box — phase 4.5 f851128 (journal 89, journal.md:1170: Floor 12.5 s / Pulse 11.9 s per tick against a 250 ms budget and exec.loop_ms 54.7 s avg vs 5.3 s before, where "the plan's local measurements (26-103 ms at 2x season) did not reflect the NAS") and phase 5 0488e22 (journal 109: pulse self-guard tripped at 6,334/4,617/4,298 ms, floor's funnel timing out every 2 min, 11 RFQ quote errors, loops 91-129 s). The recurring database-scale mechanism is real and still unmeasured before deploy: the RFQ fair lateral reads 16,264 rows to keep 236, 14 s cold vs 10 ms warm (roadmap.md:355), and three integrity checks still skip on the 2,000 ms timeout (harness/ops/checks.py:25; evidence.md §I, 2026-09-11 04:15 CT). Nothing in tests/ (124 entries, no perf assertion; only fixture_day.py and fixtures/day_synthetic, a 30-minute game) or the Makefile exercises a NAS-sized database, and phase 6 as written (roadmap.md:279-294) adds no scale test. Two qualifiers: (1) not every deploy storms — the full deploy 3ca32dd on 2026-09-10 (journal 98) was clean once fix 32's BRIN autosummarize landed, and the repo's own later root cause for the 4.5 storm is unsummarized BRIN ranges (journal 93, roadmap.md:352), not only the measurement gap; and much of phase 5's pain came from venue and API behaviour a DB load test would not catch (the RFQ firehose at 11-14k frames/min, fixes 38/40 at roadmap.md:358/360, and the Anthropic schema 400, fix 39). (2) The docket is not empty: carried fix 16 (roadmap.md:339) is queued as "the next plan-next's first task" with the covering test "both checks return pass on the NAS-sized tables within 2000 ms", and the phase 5 report §9 lists "test_housekeeping under load" as a phase 6 input. The finding should be framed as "promote fix 16 into a real NAS-sized scale harness that gates full deploys", not "phase 6 contains nothing".

Narrowed and re-pointed: local measurement is not predictive on this host and the repo says so (journal 89, line 1170: "the plan's local measurements (26-103 ms at 2x season) did not reflect the NAS"), but the deploys that stormed are not "every deploy since 4.5" — journal 95/96 (app-only, loop 39 % better than baseline) and journal 98 (full deploy with migration) were clean on the same box and the same database. Storms correlate with full deploys that add a new always-on workload (4.5's snapshot scheduler; phase 5's research worker + RFQ listener), and their causes were cold page cache on a 47 GB database with 512 MB shared_buffers and pgdata on a rotational HDD (evidence A line 24), unsummarized BRIN ranges (journal 93: 39.6 s → 2.8 ms), an unbounded re-render loop (fix 36), and 11-14k external RFQ frames/minute the design assumed would be a trickle (fix 38/40) — none of which a NAS-sized database fixture would reproduce. The real gap in phase 6 is therefore not a scale test but a written deploy rule: (a) any deploy that adds an always-on workload ships it behind a flag that defaults OFF, with a mandatory bounded first-hour measurement on the box and a documented off-switch — done ad hoc and successfully in journals 109/110, but it is not a required verify.md row the way "Scheduler re-enable" (verify.md:199) is; (b) fix 34 (self-guard warm-up window) stays open, since journal 109 shows every full deploy on this box will otherwise pause a builder on cold cache; (c) two cheap host-side items outrank any test — move pgdata off the rotational HDD and correct `random_page_cost 1.1` on spinning media (evidence B line 56) — and both are superseded by the Mac mini migration, which also means a fixture calibrated to the current NAS would be stale on first use; (d) phase 6 item 7 (archive-and-drop) is the item that addresses scale, because 8.94 GB/day (evidence C) is what turns every cold read into a seek.

Severity IMPORTANT (confirmed, not raised to critical), scoped and re-costed: every phase deploy since 4.5 degraded the live executor (journal 89: 54.7 s avg loops, emergency SNAPSHOTS_ENABLED=0; journal 109: 91/129 s loops, pulse self-guard tripped, three checks still skipping on their 2 s budget; journal 110: executor down 4 minutes, 99.9 s cold loop), because the failure mode is page-cache eviction on a 7.7 GB box holding a 47 GB database on a rotational HDD — a 1,400x cold/warm gap (14 s vs 10 ms, roadmap.md:355) that no local measurement reproduces — and phase 6 as written (roadmap.md:279-294) adds an eighth pricing variant to a pass already exhausting its 45 s budget on 45% of game-day ticks, a five-minute read over the 453 MB venue_trades partition, and a new WS channel, with no gate anywhere in verify.md requiring a cold measurement first; but the fix is two-staged, not one M-sized task: WEEK 1 (cost S, no second host needed) extend tests/test_snap_bounds.py's BOUNDED/TINY rule from the dashboard builders to harness/ops/checks.py, harness/execution/store.py and harness/research/*, which is the discipline that already exists and would have caught fix 35's unbounded lateral and the three perennially-skipping checks; WEEK 2 (cost S, not M — deploy/backup/drill.sh and the verify.md:210 drill row already restore the 1.3 GB nightly dump into a scratch database) add the cold-p95-per-statement timing to that existing drill and make it a verify.md gate for any phase 6 task that adds a read — but only on a host pinned to production's memory-to-database ratio and rotational-equivalent I/O, or on the Mac mini once it IS production, because a cold p95 measured on NVMe with more RAM repeats the exact 26-103 ms laptop error the finding is written to prevent.

refuted_findings.title: fair_stale allowance is a constant that matches only game-day cadence; it is the fill blocker
refuted_findings.claim: stale_allowance_s = FEATURED_CADENCE_S (120, a constant) + tick_budget_s (100) = 220 s on every order, while the featured feed refreshes every 900 s on weekdays, 300 s on weekends and not at all 01:00-08:00 CT; so every featured-only order is cancelled fair_stale before its fair value can refresh, which is 7,825 of 7,997 orders (97.8 %) and the direct cause of 1 real fill in 3.5 days.
reasons: evidence: The constants are real but the causal mechanism is refuted on code and on the claim's own data. (1) Wrong cadence: fair_ts = fair_values.created_at (harness/execution/store.py:357, docstring :372) and uq_fair_value_row is keyed on run_id (migrations/versions/0001_baseline.py:824-826), so on_conflict_do_nothing (harness/pricing/fair.py:126) never suppresses a row across runs -- every priced tick writes a fresh created_at. Pricing fires on "if summaries:" -- "Only price when this tick actually refreshed Kalshi markets" (harness/recorder/tick.py:904-920) -- not on the Odds-API fetch. recorder/cadence.py:16-33 interval_for governs the odds fetch only; it is not the cadence _fair_stale measures. (2) Data contradicts "cancelled before its fair value can refresh": evidence G tib_p25 = 5.0 min = 300 s > 220 s, so >=75% of the 7,825 fair_stale orders outlived the allowance (avg 33.7 min = 9.2x). Order 157 -- the one real queue_model fill, feed_kind=featured, stale_allowance_at_place=220, Monday 09-08 -- rested 14:36:47Z to 15:12:06Z = 35.3 min (9.6x the allowance) and filled at 15:07:15Z, 30.5 min in; its no_watcher fills landed +1h48 and +2 days, so that track cannot price a 220 s change. (3) The weekday/game-day contrast is cherry-picked: Tue 09-09 p50 12.2 min and Fri 09-11 p50 10.0 min sit beside game-day 15.5, not near Mon 4.8. (4) D4 is misread: placed==cancelled on 09-10 09:00-13:00 CT is cap saturation, not a timer -- D3 shows exec.open_orders max 150 in every one of those hours (avg 121.9/128.5/78.6/90.5/144.0) against exec_max_open_orders=150 shared, so at the cap each placement requires a cancel. The 01:00 CT hour cancels 150 (09-10) and 64 (09-11) but only 13 (09-09): ~227 of 7,825 = 2.9%. (5) Minor citation errors: plan.py:501-502 is the fair_stale cancel, :503-504 is _venue_moved; journal line 1075 sits in entry 82, not 86; evidence note 9's "7,388 (92%)" contradicts its own buckets (3,903+1,852+1,447+660 = 7,862 = 98.3%). Verified as written: fair.py:24 and :30-35 (220 s), cadence.py:16-33 tiers, plan.py:446-456 max() rule, G percentiles (n=7,825, allow p25=p95=220, tib p50 12.2), D4 hourly figures, settings.py:51 odds_alt_window_h=36, preregistration :55 and :117.

alternative: The claim's code observation is real but its magnitude and its causal headline ("it is the fill blocker", "direct cause of 1 real fill") are not supported; a better-supported alternative is that the fill count is set by queue position and absence of taker flow, with fair_stale acting as a capital-rotation mechanism under a binding order cap.

WHAT SURVIVES (verified): stale_allowance_s for featured is the constant FEATURED_CADENCE_S + tick_budget_s = 120 + 100 = 220 (harness/pricing/fair.py:24,30-35), and the featured odds fetch is gated by the same interval_for ladder as everything else (harness/recorder/tick.py:521-526 `interval = interval_for(sport, now, kickoffs, ...)`; harness/recorder/cadence.py:16-33 -> None 01:00-08:00 CT, 120 game day, 300 weekend, 900 weekday). fair.py's own docstring ("Featured-market lines refresh every tick ... a fixed 120s") and the spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-07-phase3-paper-execution-design.md:7, "featured: 120 + 100 = 220 s") both assume a 120 s featured cadence that interval_for only delivers on game days. So the allowance is mis-derived on non-game-day weekday hours. That part is correct and material.

ERROR 1 - wrong staleness clock. The rule reads fair_ts = fair_values.created_at, not the odds line's last_update (harness/execution/store.py:356-357,372). uq_fair_value_row is keyed on run_id (harness/db/schema.py:139-141), so every pricing run writes a fresh row and advances fair_ts even when no odds line changed, and pricing fires on any tick that refreshed Kalshi market summaries for EITHER series (harness/recorder/tick.py:904-905, 920), not on the odds feed. Evidence F: game-16 fair values refreshed every 1-3.5 min (46 rows/run) on Thu evening; evidence.md controller note 1 states this contradicts the brief's "15-minute pricing cadence".

ERROR 2 - "every featured-only order is cancelled before its fair value can refresh" is false for most of the distribution. Evidence G: time-in-book p50 12.2 min (732 s), p75 35.3 min, p95 147 min - all far beyond 220 s, i.e. the median order survived roughly six fair refreshes. Under the claimed mechanism no order could outlive 220 s past its last refresh. fair_stale is a late-refresh detector; what trips it is a missing pricing pass (the 01:00-08:00 None window - D4 cancels the whole book at 01:00 each night, 150/64/13; a 900 s-cadence hour; or an executor loop of 100+ s), not a fixed 220 s clock on every order.

ERROR 3 - the "featured-only" framing is moot under current settings. The alternate branch of stale_allowance_s returns odds_alt_interval_near_s/far_s + tick_budget_s = 120 + 100 = 220 as well (settings odds_alt_interval_near_s 120 / far 120 after U1, adversarial review U1 line 253). Every order would carry 220 regardless of feed_kind, and feed_kind is featured on 100 % of the 7,997 orders anyway (evidence G, controller note 9).

ERROR 4 (the load-bearing one) - fair_stale is not shown to be the fill blocker.
(a) Ceiling on recoverable fills: the no_watcher counterfactual runs the SAME queue model to the order's natural expiry (harness/execution/loop.py:108, 864-872), and it produces fills on only 27 of 445 distinct (variant, market, side) triples (evidence.md controller note 10). The 7,825 cancels are ~445 positions re-placed ~18x each, not 7,825 distinct chances. Removing fair_stale entirely has an upper bound of tens of positions, not thousands.
(b) Queue position is the dominant blocker: avg queue_ahead_at_place 15,336 / 8,524 / 5,353 contracts for sharp_two_sided / sharp_direct / constrained against 110 / 110 / 137-contract orders (evidence G, controller note 10), with ws.trades_per_min 19.6 across 500 subscribed tickers (evidence D). The single real fill, order 157, had the atypically small queue_ahead 6,401 and filled 30.5 min after placement (placed 14:36:47Z, queue_model fills 15:07:15Z) - inside its existing 35.3-min life. The one fill the system got did not need a longer allowance.
(c) No flow to fill against: 7,388 of 7,997 orders (92 %) were placed >24 h before kickoff, and only 47 orders were placed inside 6 h of kickoff (nfl 1-6h 38, <1h 9; evidence G ttk buckets, controller note 9).
(d) The counterfactual is not a policy estimate: no_watcher ignores exec_max_open_orders. Placement is gated on still_open < 150 (harness/execution/plan.py:609, 551, 97) and the cap was binding in 41 of 53 hours with any open orders (controller note 4, max = 150). If fair_stale stopped cancelling, the first 150 orders would hold every slot indefinitely and later intents would be skipped exec_capacity - fewer distinct positions exposed, not more. The churn is how the system rotates 150 slots across 445 positions.
(e) Time in book is not time at risk of filling: a dirty book both suspends the whole cancel chain (harness/execution/plan.py:501 `if market.dirty(now, s): return None`) and freezes both queue tracks (harness/execution/loop.py:799-803). Order 157 carries dirty_seconds 181,200 over a ~53 h no_watcher track (~95 %), and its first 20 order_watch_samples are all book_dirty = t with queue_remaining pinned at 6,401. exec.dirty_markets averages 122.8 of 125 book_dirty_markets.

ERROR 5 - severity/classification. The cancel is the documented F36 rule with a stated rationale in code ("holding an order on a market we can no longer value is the mistake this rule exists to prevent", harness/execution/plan.py:447-451; spec line 32), and the tension was already escalated to the owner and deliberately left undecided: phase 4.5 report (docs/superpowers/autopilot/reports/2026-09-09-phase4.5.md:8) "Your call whether the cadence or the staleness bound moves; the loop will not change either", repeated in the phase 5 report. This is an open owner-gated parameter decision, not an undetected critical defect.

Unverified: the per-hour split of the 7,825 fair_stale cancels by the cadence in force (I could not attribute cancels to 900 s vs 120 s vs the night window); the markout sign of the 646 no_watcher fills, so whether those counterfactual fills would have been profitable or adverse selection is unknown.

refuted_findings.title: The go-live gate is unreachable at the current fill rate, but no game weekend has been traded yet
refuted_findings.claim: Criterion 1 needs 150 queue_model fill events across >= 40 games (cumulative, no lower time bound); the book has 1 in 3.5 midweek days, so the gate cannot be met by mid-October without the P6-01 change; however the paper book has only seen Tue-Thu (phase 3 deployed 2026-09-08), and Saturday 09-12 (103 NCAAF scheduled) and Sunday 09-13 are the first days with orders inside 24 h on the 120 s cadence, so the weekend is the first real fill measurement and should run unchanged.
reasons: evidence: Gate arithmetic half verifies; the premise the recommendation rests on does not. VERIFIED: gate.py:119-125 is verbatim the fill_events criterion (>=150 orders with a non-replay queue_model fill, >=40 distinct games, both sports, >=80% book_source='ws' and dirty_minutes=0), enforced at gate.py:267-280; _VARIANT_ORDERS (gate.py:251-255, cited as 250-256) bounds only `o.placed_at <= :now` with `o.replay = false`, so the count is cumulative with no lower time bound and cannot be manufactured by replay (gate.py:239-242); evaluate_all/evaluate_gate (gate.py:689-703) pass only `now`, no window. The gate variant is sharp_direct (harness/config/settings.py:83) = f259ca109084, the variant that owns the single fill, so the gate variant stands at 1 fill event across 1 game. Mid-October is real but uncited: roadmap.md:312 "Mid-October (user) | Go-live gate review". REFUTED, load-bearing: (1) "Saturday 09-12 and Sunday 09-13 are the first days with orders inside 24 h" is contradicted by the reviewer's own citation 3 - nfl <1h 9, 1-6h 38, 6-24h 32 plus ncaaf 6-24h 56 = 135 orders already placed inside 24 h of kickoff (evidence.md sec G ttk buckets), i.e. Thursday-night NFL was already traded near kickoff, and it produced zero queue_model fills (evidence.md:969, exec.filled_contracts over 3 days = 38.92, all in the 09-08 10:00 CT hour, zero since). The near-kickoff fill measurement has already started and reads 0/135; the weekend is a larger sample, not the first one. (2) The causal story is unsupported: the sole queue_model fill, order 157, was placed 2026-09-08 14:36:47Z against kickoff_utc 2026-09-12 23:00:00Z (evidence.md:739) = ~4.3 days to kickoff, the >72h bucket - the one fill the book has came from the far-from-kickoff regime, not the near one. (3) "the P6-01 change" has zero hits in docs/ or harness/ (repo-wide grep) and appears in none of the five cited items, yet "the gate cannot be met by mid-October without the P6-01 change" is load-bearing. (4) Numbers: "1 in 3.5 midweek days" is 2.97 days (phase 3 deploy 09-08 ~08:00 CT to 09-11 07:20 CT, brief:14,19); "only seen Tue-Thu" omits the 288 orders already placed Fri 09-11 (brief:19). (5) Minor: the no_watcher-to-natural-expiry sentence is loop.py:20-22, not 15-19 (15-19 is intake and books). Note also an internal inconsistency in evidence.md itself: line 973 says "7,388 of 7,997 orders (92 %) were placed more than 24 h before kickoff", but its own bucket table sums to 7,862 >24h (98.3 %) and 135 <24h.

alternative: The alternative explanation is better supported on every load-bearing element of the claim.

1. "Unreachable" is the coded invariant, not a defect, so severity critical is wrong. `legal_decision` and `live_trading_env` return `False` unconditionally (harness/report/gate.py:605-612), and the module docstring states it outright (gate.py:13-16): "`GateResult.passed` ... can never be true from this code. That is the invariant, not an oversight: going live is a decision made outside the harness." Roadmap invariant 3 hard-forbids "any code that would make `harness gate` pass", invariant 1 freezes `harness/variants/`, invariant 2 freezes the criteria and thresholds (R1). A finding whose headline is "the gate is unreachable" and whose remedy is a change that raises the gate variant's fill count is pointed at three hard-forbidden invariants at once.

2. The shortfall was pre-registered as expected, with a named fallback. docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-09-07-autopilot-review-reports/experiment.md:211: "Expect tens of confirmed fills a week, not hundreds. Pre-register the floor: >= 30 fills across >= 10 games, else the week-3 report prints 'insufficient' for H1 rather than a number. The go-live gate's 150 fill events across 40 games is realistically a five-to-eight-week target; 'mid-October' is optimistic." quant.md:191 modelled ~630 candidates over three weeks and concluded "even at a generous 20 % the fill count lands near 150... below the gate's 150". The adversarial review's decision 2 (2026-09-07-autopilot-adversarial-review.md:170) put the consequence in writing: "no -> ... the gate's fill count is probably unreachable in three weeks" — and the ruling taken was F18/Task 4b (NO-side, two-sided primary), which shipped (roadmap "Closed since the reviews: NO-side signals moved into phase 3 as Task 4b (U2)"; sharp_two_sided is now 4,955 of 7,997 orders, evidence G per-variant table). The three-week product is a dataset, not a passed gate (spec 2026-09-06 design §1 line 10; README.md:111; roadmap.md:312 puts the gate review in mid-October as a user decision). `INSUFFICIENT` is a first-class status in gate.py (line 55). So "cannot be met by mid-October" restates a documented prior, at the optimistic end of a 5-8 week pre-registered band (2026-09-08 + 5-8 weeks = 2026-10-13 to 2026-11-03).

3. The cited remedy does not exist. `grep -rn "P6-0" docs/` returns nothing in the repo. Roadmap phase 6 item 1 (roadmap.md:281-284) is the key-number model, which "ships as a **new variant** `sharp_plus_derived_kn` ... never as a change to the derived model under an unchanged id (F57, F17)". A new variant cannot raise the gate variant's fill count: `Settings.gate_variant` defaults to `sharp_direct` (harness/config/settings.py:83) and every criterion is scoped to one `variant_id` (gate.py:251-256, `_VARIANT_ORDERS`). The rereview ruling B (rereview-phase3-plan.md, ruling B) already refused moving the gate property onto another variant precisely because it changes what the gate is computed over.

4. The causal attribution is wrong, and the real lever is a user question, not a code fix. 7,825 of 7,997 cancels (97.8 %) are `fair_stale` (brief line 20) at median 12.2 min in book with `stale_allowance_at_place` = 220 s on every single order (evidence G percentiles: allow_p25 = allow_p95 = 220). The never-cancel counterfactual already measured on the same tape produced 646 no_watcher fill rows over 224 orders (brief line 21) against 1 `queue_model` fill event — a 224:1 ratio. The binding suppressor is therefore the cancel policy, which the phase 4.5 report line 8 and the phase 5 report §1 both carried to the user verbatim as a strategy question ("your call whether the cadence or the staleness bound moves; the loop will not change either"), unanswered. Calling this a "fill rate" and routing it to a phase 6 code change misroutes an open user decision into engineering work the loop is forbidden to do unilaterally.

5. A factual sub-claim is contradicted by the evidence it cites. Evidence G ttk buckets show nfl 1-6h 38, nfl <1h 9, ncaaf 6-24h 56 = 103 orders already placed inside 24 h of a kickoff. The Thursday 2026-09-10 NFL opener was traded to the `exec_kickoff_cutoff_min` = 10 boundary with 150 resting orders at 20:35 CT (phase 5 report §4) and evidence D4 shows `filled` = 0.000000 in every hour of 2026-09-10. So Saturday is not "the first day with orders inside 24 h"; one in-window game night has already been traded and returned zero queue_model fills.

6. What actually binds first is game coverage, not the count of 150 — and that half of the claim survives. The 224 counterfactual-filled orders collapse to only 27 distinct (variant, market, side) against 445 for all 7,997 orders (evidence line 974), and the whole book has touched 58 games (brief line 22) versus criterion 1's >= 40 distinct games with both sports. No cancel-policy change reaches 40 games on a midweek board; only game-day volume does. That is the genuine reason to run the weekend, and it is a power/coverage argument, not a gate-feasibility argument.

7. "Run unchanged" is also not free of risk the claim does not price: on the one in-window game night the executor ran p95 114,768 ms in the 19:00 hour (evidence D2) against `exec_period_s` = 15, with 521 cumulative `loops_skipped` on the heartbeat; Saturday has 103 NCAAF scheduled. The first real fill measurement is at risk of being host-confounded on a box whose Mac mini trigger was met 2026-09-10 20:10 CT (brief line 31, journal 101). "Unchanged strategy" and "unchanged host" are separable decisions and the claim conflates them.

What survives: the weekend is the first high-game-count measurement and the strategy config should not be touched before it. What does not survive: the critical severity, the "gate is unreachable" framing, the mid-October deadline as a live constraint, the P6-01 remedy, and the attribution of the one-fill rate to a fill rate rather than to the cancel policy.

refuted_findings.title: Monday n=1 does not break R7 or invariant 2 if week 1 is treated as a pre-fix range for the execution track only
refuted_findings.claim: The week-2 selection frozen Mon 2026-09-21 is over table-4 gap_mid cells (BH family) and table-2 Holm contrasts; table 4 comes from market_gap_snapshots/gap_outcomes and needs no fills, so week 1 still counts there; the execution track (t2, t3, t6, gate criteria 1-6) can carry a dated measurement amendment that states the pre-fix run range and excludes or re-scores it, which the protocol allows without a user decision; moving the 09-21/09-28 dates, lowering 150, or redefining a fill event would be an invariant-2 user decision and a pre-registration change.
reasons:
alternative: Clauses 1, 2 and 4 verify; the load-bearing clause 3 ("the execution track — t2, t3, t6, gate criteria 1-6 — can carry a dated measurement amendment that excludes or re-scores the pre-fix range, which the protocol allows without a user decision") is contradicted by the code the escape hatch would have to run in.

VERIFIED PARTS (so the synthesizer keeps them):
- Selection object: harness/report/weekly.py:143-171 `select_cells` reads only t4's `bh` column (CELL_KEY = fair_source, price_bucket, ttk, sport, market_type; weekly.py:40) and t2's `holm(pinnacle_t5)` column (weekly.py:42, tables.py:96). Nothing fill-derived enters selected.json.
- Table 4's families need no fills: `_T4_SNAPSHOTS` (tables.py:686-698) selects from `market_gap_snapshots` joined to venue_markets/games; `gap_outcomes` is a LEFT JOIN used only for the display column `clv_mid_p`. Families A/B run on `HEADLINE_PANEL = gap_mid` (tables.py:94) restricted to `feed featured` (tables.py:87). Evidence C: market_gap_snapshots 2,347,281 rows. Correct.
- Clause 4 is right: 150 is a gate threshold coded in `CRITERIA` (gate.py:119-125, `Criterion("fill_events", ..., 150)`), "a fill event" is its definition string (gate.py:237-242 `_FILL_EVENT`), and 09-21/09-28 is the confirmation cut-off (R7, preregistration "Calendar" line 75). All three are invariant 2 / R1, and gate.py:9-11 says so verbatim: "editing a threshold, a family or a definition here is a dated user decision and a pre-registration amendment, never a tidy-up."

WHY CLAUSE 3 FAILS (three independent reasons):

(1) The gate has no from-bound and cannot be given one without an invariant-2 decision. Every gate query is `where o.variant_id = :variant and o.replay = false and o.placed_at <= :now` (gate.py:251-254, and identically at 308, 352, 393, 437, 587). gate.py:21-23 states the design: "The gate window is the whole paper run up to `now`, not one ISO week: the counts are 150 fills across 40 games, which no single week produces." There is no `:start` parameter anywhere in gate.py. Excluding week 1 from criteria 1-6 therefore requires editing those queries — which gate.py:9-11 and roadmap invariant 2 ("as coded in `harness/report/gate.py`", roadmap.md line 89-91) both classify as a dated user decision — or deleting/relabelling rows, which is roadmap invariant 5 (non-additive DB changes: DELETE, hard-forbidden). The claim's "without a user decision" is exactly what the code forbids.

(2) The protocol's other half, "re-scores", is also unavailable to the gate. `harness replay` writes only replay-tagged rows (harness/replay.py:19-21 "every row it writes is tagged `replay = true`"; :214 `_insert_signals(..., replay=True)`; :270-273 counts `where o.replay = true`), and every gate criterion filters `o.replay = false`. A re-score can therefore never restore a single fill event to criteria 1-6. So for the gate the amendment collapses to pure deletion of evidence, on a criterion currently at 1 queue_model fill event across 1 game (brief line 21: order 157, the only queue_model fill) against a threshold of 150 fills / >=40 games / both sports / >=80 % ws-clean (gate.py:276-281).

(3) The amendment buys nothing where the claim says it is not needed, and the claim's clean t4/t2 split does not hold for t2. `week_bounds` (tables.py:185-194) returns [Monday 00:00 CT, next Monday 00:00 CT) — one ISO week. The Mon 2026-09-21 week-2 report is computed on ISO 38 data only, so week 1's status is already irrelevant to the freeze; the amendment is a no-op for selection and a loss for the gate. Worse, t2 is not a clean non-execution track: `_T2_ORDER_CLV` (tables.py:422-429) reads `order_clv` joined to `orders` on `placed_at` in the window, and `_table2` sets `executed = {variant for variant, _, _ in raw}` (tables.py:478) then skips the snapshot fallback for those variants (tables.py:479-481). Removing the execution track's orders silently flips sharp_direct — the pairing anchor for every family-C contrast — and constrained and sharp_two_sided from `order_clv` basis to `gap_outcomes` basis. That is a change in how family C's contrasts are computed, i.e. the "benchmark and BH families" invariant 2 names, not a neutral exclusion.

(4) Supporting: there is no fix, so there is no "pre-fix range". Protocol item 1 (preregistration line 55) is templated on Amendment 1, a landed bug fix. The n=1 cause is the fair_stale churn (7,825 of 7,997 cancels, brief line 20; plan.py:446), which the phase 4.5 report (reports/2026-09-09-phase4.5.md line 8) carried to the user as a strategy question — "Your call whether the cadence or the staleness bound moves; the loop will not change either" — and the user has not answered. Any fix is an executor-settings or variant-YAML change: protocol item 2 (line 56) lists "executor settings" as a strategy change needing a new id or a new hashed `orders.config_hash`, `stale_s: 180` lives in harness/variants/sharp_direct.yaml:15 (roadmap invariant 1, hard-forbidden), and `exec_max_open_orders = 150` is in the Amendment 2 frozen executor block (preregistration line 100). And protocol item 3 (line 57) makes anything registered after Mon 2026-09-21 09:00 CT exploratory and unconfirmable in week 3. So the fix that would create the boundary is itself a gate; declaring the boundary first is backwards.

(5) Context the claim omits: Amendment 4 (preregistration line 122) already declares runs 344-4327 a pre-fix range touching table 2 and family C, and its deploy was 2026-09-08 11:44 CT. The single queue_model fill (order 157, placed 2026-09-08 09:36 CT, brief line 21) sits inside that already-flagged range. And the adversarial review's open question 2 (2026-09-07-autopilot-adversarial-review.md line 170) recorded the outcome in advance: without the NO-side variant "the gate's fill count is probably unreachable in three weeks" — the NO-side was added and the count is still 1 after three days.

Net: the escape hatch is not executable for the half of the track it is proposed for, and is unnecessary for the half it is not. The honest statement is that the week-2 selection is intact but the go-live gate is on track to fail criterion 1 on volume, and the only levers are user decisions.

materiality: Every checkable claim holds, but the finding's own conclusion is "nothing is broken, no user decision needed, proceed" — its recommended action (render the report, run `harness gate`, commit, add an addendum note) is identical to the status-quo Monday duty, so it changes nothing the owner does in the next 1-2 weeks. Verified: (a) R7 (roadmap.md:55) freezes only the week-2 SELECTION artefact `docs/reports/2026-w38-selected.json`; (b) weekly.py:142-171 `select_cells` builds that artefact from t4's `bh` column and t2's `holm(pinnacle_t5)` column only; (c) t4's source query `_T4_SNAPSHOTS` (tables.py:686-697) joins market_gap_snapshots -> venue_markets -> games with a LEFT JOIN to gap_outcomes and touches no orders/fills table, and evidence.md C shows market_gap_snapshots at 2,347,281 rows, so the selection track genuinely has data regardless of fills; (d) HEADLINE_PANEL = "gap_mid", HEADLINE_FEED_KIND = "featured" (tables.py:87-96); (e) the amendment protocol at preregistration:55 does permit a loop-recorded measurement amendment provided no threshold/family/grid/cut-off moves, which is the invariant-2 line (roadmap.md:89-91). The reason severity is wrong is the code's own docstring: gate.py:20-23 states "The gate window is the whole paper run up to `now`, not one ISO week: the counts are 150 fills across 40 games, which no single week produces," and gate.py:13-16 states `GateResult.passed` "can never be true from this code" because `legal_decision` and `live_trading_env` are False by construction. A Monday reading of fill_events 1/150 is therefore the designed behaviour of a never-weekly, never-passing gate, not a protocol emergency — there is no R7 or invariant-2 exposure to defuse. Two corrections worth carrying: (1) no "Amendment 5" exists — grep of the preregistration record and the journal returns nothing past Amendment 4 (preregistration:117, pricing order/budget, 2026-09-08), so the finding is proposing an amendment while citing it as an existing range; and (2) the premise that week 1 is a "pre-fix range" for the execution track is the weakest link, because fixes 35-41 (roadmap.md:337-361) are research/RFQ/annotator-layer label fixes, while the 1-fill outcome is caused by the fair_stale cancel policy (7,825 fair_stale cancels, median 12.2 min in book, evidence.md G; plan.py:446), which is a behavioural setting, not a mislabelled measurement — re-scoring cannot manufacture fills. The material residue the finding buries in its last line is the opposite of its headline: at 1 queue_model fill per 7,997 orders over 3.5 days, criteria 1-7 will still be insufficient at the week-3 confirmation on 09-28, so the user's unanswered fair_stale/pricing-cadence strategy question (brief line 28, carried since the phase 4.5 report) is the decision that actually needs an answer before Mon 09-14 — and that belongs in the viability question, not as a critical phase-6 protocol item.

refuted_findings.title: Before Friday 18:00 CT: the RFQ listener is the one live ops risk the loop can remove without a deploy
refuted_findings.claim: With fix 38 the listener still stores ~3,000 rfqs rows a minute (~1.7 KB/row from fix 38's 74,608 rows / 128 MB), roughly 5 MB/min or ~7 GB/day on a 47 GB database already growing 8.94 GB/day on the rotational disk the executor reads from, while every quote declines (no_fair 7,739, same_game 381, single_leg 1) so H5 is measuring nothing; fix 40 is in flight but any deploy before the window risks the fix-37 lock race that took the executor down four minutes on 09-11.
reasons: evidence: Every named citation exists and is quoted accurately, but the load-bearing magnitude does not survive the reviewer's own evidence file. Verified as stated: roadmap.md:360 literally says "still stores ~3,000 rfqs rows a minute"; roadmap.md:358 gives 74,608 rows / 128 MB in 7 min (=1.7 KB/row, and evidence.md C's 159 MB / 93,470 rows = 1.7 KB/row agrees); evidence.md I gives no_fair 7,739, same_game 381, single_leg 1 (8,121 total, 100 % declined) and H5 (specs/2026-09-06-adversarial-review.md:110; design §8.2) is graded from rfq_quotes, so it is measuring nothing; evidence.md A confirms pgdata on sda ROTA=1; evidence.md C confirms 47 GB and db.growth_gb_per_day 8.94; journal 110 confirms the schema step failed twice and the executor was down 05:20-05:24 (four minutes) with roadmap.md:357 fix 37 still open; roadmap.md:52/:64 confirms R4's 15-minute pre-kickoff bar; journals 109 and 110 confirm the listener was switched off by hand at 03:41-03:45 and 05:33. REFUTATION: the rate does not add up. rfqs held 74,608 rows / 128 MB when the listener went off at 05:33 (journal 110); the listener came back on with fix 38 at 06:38 (journal 112); evidence.md C at the ~07:30 pull shows 93,470 rows / 159 MB. That is +18,862 rows / +31 MB over ~52 minutes of listener-on = ~360 rows/min, ~0.6 MB/min, ~0.9 GB/day - about 8x below the claimed 3,000 rows/min, 5 MB/min, 7 GB/day, and the contradicting number sits in the evidence file the reviewer cites. Physical table size is monotone here (fix 38's prune is 21 days old and unquoted per commit 2c687d2), so this is not a pg_stat estimator artifact. The roadmap's 3,000/min derives from journal 112's counter (frames_seen 32,676 / stored 5,833 in three minutes = 1,944/min) taken in the first minutes after subscribe, which is precisely the venue's replay of the whole open RFQ set (journal 109: 2,423 frames in one minute; roadmap.md:355 adds a 500-frame replay cap) - a subscribe backlog, not a steady state. Two further overstatements: journal 112 records the fix-37 lock race already worked around by hand at the 06:38 deploy ("docker compose stop app-serve before the recipe... the schema step passed first time"), so a pre-window deploy carries a proven mitigation rather than an unmitigated four-minute outage risk; and fix 38 already removed the executor-contention symptom (app-ws CPU 64 % -> 1.1 % per journal 112, 2.88 % at the evidence pull, executor 6.7 s at 06:42), so "the one live ops risk" overstates the current state - evidence.md D1's 336 s max loop is the 03:31 pre-fix-35 sample, not a current one. The qualitative core (100 % declines, H5 measuring nothing, an off switch the loop can use without a deploy) stands.

alternative: Four independent checks against the same evidence file and repo contradict the claim's load-bearing numbers.

(1) The 7 GB/day is derived from a frame counter, not a row counter, and is contradicted by the physical table size in the same evidence file. `store_rfq` is an UPSERT keyed on `event.rfq_id` (harness/venues/kalshi/rfq.py:372-398: `row = session.get(Rfq, event.rfq_id); if row is None: ... session.add(row)`), and `frames_stored` is incremented per frame that reaches it (harness/venues/kalshi/rfq_socket.py:325-326), so replayed `rfq_created` frames (the venue replays the whole open RFQ set on every subscribe — fix 35 item 2, rfq_socket.py:119 "already quoted -- stored, never recomputed") and every `rfq_deleted` for a known id increment the counter while creating zero new rows. Journal 112's own counter reads `frames_seen 32,676 / stored 5,833` in 3 min = 1,944 frames/min, not 3,000; roadmap.md:360's "~3,000 rfqs rows a minute" is itself an over-read of that counter.
Physical measurement: journal 110 records `rfqs` at 74,608 rows / **128 MB** at 05:33 CT; evidence.md section C records `rfqs` **159 MB** at 07:27-07:33 CT. The listener was off 05:33-06:38 and on with fix 38 from 06:38 (journal 112). That is **+31 MB in ~52 minutes of listener-on = 0.60 MB/min = 0.86 GB/day**, an upper bound (the 03:16-03:44 run also wrote rows before 05:33, and the 21-day retention prune has not fired, so 159 MB is a true high-water mark). The claim's 5 MB/min / 7 GB/day is ~8x high. Against `db.growth_gb_per_day 8.94` (evidence.md line 83) that is ~10% of existing growth, not ~78%. The claim's 93,470 row figure is also pg_stat `n_live_tup`; evidence.md:962 records that `select count(*) from rfqs` timed out, so the row count is an estimate while the 159 MB is not.

(2) Disk is not the binding constraint. evidence.md A: `/volume1` 11T, 3.4T avail (69% used). Even at the claim's own 16 GB/day combined, that is >200 days of headroom; at the measured 9.8 GB/day, >340 days. Nothing about disk bites before Friday 18:00 CT.

(3) The measured executor cost of the fix-38 listener is negative, not positive. evidence.md D1: 2026-09-11 p95 `exec.loop_ms` 10,033 ms vs 15,169 (09-10) and 16,205 (09-08) — the best day of the run, with the listener on since 06:38. `exec_heartbeat` p95_loop_ms 7,112 ms (evidence.md:460), at/under the 7.5 s ceiling. docker stats: app-ws 2.88% CPU, 79.2 MiB, BLOCK read 2.43 MB / write 418 kB — the smallest block I/O of any app container (app-exec 13.5 MB, app-serve 16.9 MB). Journal 112: app-ws CPU 64% -> 1.1% after fix 38. The 335,763 ms `exec.loop_ms` max the claim leans on is the 03:30 dump + pre-fix-38 RFQ storm (journal 109), which fix 35 and fix 38 already addressed.

(4) The deploy-risk half has a same-day counterexample and misreads R4. The four-minute outage (journal 110) was `make deploy-nas` (full recipe) at 05:20 CT with no fix-37 mitigation. Fix 40+41 is specified as "app-only deploy plus app-ws recreate" (roadmap.md:360-361), and that exact recipe ran 76 minutes later at 06:38 CT: journal 112 records the fix-37 workaround applied by hand (`docker compose stop app-serve` before the recipe), "the schema step passed first time", `make deploy-nas-app` exit 0, executor 40.1 s then 6.7 s at 06:42 — no outage. (The residual risk is real: Makefile:120 shows `deploy-nas-app` does run `init-db` and stops only app-exec/app-run, not app-serve — but the mitigation is one command and has been executed successfully.) R4 (roadmap.md:52) forbids a deploy only while a matched game is in_progress, within 4 h after a kickoff, within 15 min before a kickoff, or 60-100 min before an NFL kickoff — for an 18:00 CT kickoff that is 16:20-17:00 and 17:45-18:00, leaving a legal window from now until ~16:20 CT. "Any deploy before the window" is not what the rule says.

(5) "H5 is measuring nothing" inverts a recorded design decision. The 8,121 declines are the cheap path fix 35 item 1 deliberately built — "decline `no_fair`/`single_leg`/`same_game` before any `fair_values` read" (roadmap.md:357) — so each decline costs a series-ticker string test, not a 16,264-row `fair_values` scan. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-10-phase5-research-layer-design.md:162 (B-M7, the narrowing that produced fix 38) states outright: "H5's population is unchanged in substance: it was always the quotable combos." A 100% decline rate over a pre-NFL-week-1 population that is "almost all `KXMVECROSSCATEGORY` combos with no football leg" (journal 110) is the expected reading, and switching the listener off before Fri 18:00 CT removes the observation window most likely to contain the first quotable all-football combo — which is the opposite of the claim's recommended action.

refuted_findings.title: Executor ceiling, the 150 cap and the WebSocket churn are one item: the host
refuted_findings.claim: The p95 ceiling (7.5 s) was met on only one of four days; game-night p95 was 101-118 s with a single NFL game; the 150 shared cap bound in 41 of 53 hours; 50 WS disconnects in 3 h are sink statement timeouts under IO pressure that dirty books (dirty_markets 107-125 always; book_dirty was the second-largest skip reason on day 1), and a dirty book advances neither fill track; Saturday's slate will be several times Thursday's load; the Mac mini trigger is met and only the user can move.
reasons: evidence: Numbers check out; the causal synthesis does not, and one load-bearing citation is misread. (1) journal 107 (journal.md:1305) is cited as evidence that the 50 ws_disconnect/21 ws_connect in 3 h ARE sink statement timeouts; it does not diagnose them ("churn continues and is a plan-next input") and in the same entry states "No tape timeouts in the last hour." The QueryCanceled diagnosis comes from journal 90 (journal.md:1180, 7 rows 23:30-23:35 CT 09-09) and journal 92 (journal.md:1197, 40/23 in 7 h, 06:12 CT 09-10) — both BEFORE journal 93 (journal.md, 06:14-06:24 CT 09-10), which identifies unsummarized BRIN ranges as the root cause of exactly "the WS sink's statement timeouts (40 disconnects in 7 h)" and applied autosummarize on all nine BRINs on the NAS. Journal 107's window (20:17-23:17 CT 09-10) is ~17 h after that fix, so the 90/92 mechanism cannot be carried onto it unrevised. (2) The "disconnects dirty books" link is uncited and contradicted by the available series: journal.md:1261 uses exec.dirty_markets 107-117 to show the executor's work was FLAT while wall clock went 5-6x, and dirty_markets sat at 107-117 in the 07:00 hour when the loop ran avg 3.9 s / p95 4.8 s; evidence.md ws metrics 6 h give ws.gaps avg 0.0 max 0.0 and recorder.trade_gaps 0.0. The near-universal dirty rate is dominated by the exec_book_max_age_s = 120 leg of plan.py:246-256 (settings.py:66) on illiquid tickers, not by WS churn. Also the "107" in "dirty_markets 107-125" is from journal 101, not from the cited evidence line (exec 6 h: avg 122.8, max 125.0). (3) The headline thesis ("one item: the host") fails for the 150-cap leg: D3 shows max 150 in every hour 08:00-15:00 CT on 09-10, hours journal.md:1261 records at avg 5.1-6.4 s / p95 7.8-12.7 s — a healthy host. The cap binding is a policy/throughput item (7,825 of 7,997 orders cancelled fair_stale, median 12.2 min in book), invariant to host load, and a host move does not relieve it. (4) The fill drought is better explained by queue position than by dirty books: controller note 10 gives avg queue_ahead 15,336 / 8,524 / 5,353 contracts at 0.8 / 4.6 / 5.4 c inside the mid, note 9 gives 92 % of orders placed >24 h before kickoff, and brief line 21 gives 646 no_watcher fill rows / 18,512 contracts across 224 orders — the counterfactual track DID advance, so books were not dirty often enough to freeze the simulation; the money track was stopped by the fair_stale cancel. (5) Minor: "with a single NFL game" — journal.md:1259 records two games in progress at 20:07 ("LAR-SF (game 2 ...) and game 371"), plus executor tape-lag on KXNCAAFTOTAL-26SEP12ASUTXAM-51; "101-118 s" mixes evidence D2's 114.8 s with journal 101's 118 s for the same 19:00 hour; "Saturday several times Thursday" is unverified in brief/evidence (no per-day slate breakdown) though journal.md:272/275 support it independently ("60-event Saturday peak"; "roughly 5,000 a day on a weekday and up to 60,000 on a Saturday"); the R4 paraphrase drops "or 60 to 100 min before an NFL kickoff" (roadmap.md:52). Verified verbatim and retained: verify.md:117 with settings.py:54 exec_period_s 15 -> 7,500 ms; D1 16205/6188/15169/10033 ms (only 09-09 passes); D2 101062/114768/72603, max 256171; controller note 4's 41 of 53 hours and D3's 150.0 averages at 21:00/22:00 on 09-08 and 09-10; settings.py:64 "shared across the executed variants"; plan.py:246-256 dirty() docstring; loop.py:800-804 "neither track advances" (field-visible: order 157's 20 order_watch_samples all book_dirty=t with queue_remaining and nw_queue_remaining frozen at 6401.00); journal.md:773 fair_stale 508 / book_dirty 501 / no_book 98; journal.md:1265 + roadmap.md:315 trigger met 20:10 CT, "The loop never moves on its own".

alternative: The claim's individual numbers check out, but its thesis — that the loop ceiling, the 150 cap and the WS churn "are one item: the host" — fails on two of its three legs, and the remedy it implies (move to the Mac mini) fixes neither. (1) DIRTY BOOKS ARE NOT HOST-CAUSED. exec.dirty_markets was 107-117/hr during the 09-10 game night under 5 GB swap resident, IO wait 25-32 % and memory pressure full avg300 16.0 % (journal 101), and is 122.8 avg / 125 max now with swap-out 0, memory pressure full avg60 0.08 %, vmstat wa 0, load 0.78 on 8 CPUs / 99 % idle (evidence A:10-14, D6/exec). The metric went UP as the host got ~180x less stalled: correlation with host health is ~0. Mechanism: plan.py:246-256 calls dirty() true when harness/execution/book.py:578-585 `book_age_s(book, now) > exec_book_max_age_s` (120 s; plan.py:99, settings.py) — seconds since THAT ticker's own newest applied orderbook row, i.e. market inactivity, deliberately designed in F36 (docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-09-07-autopilot-adversarial-review.md line 46). Confirming it is not tape damage: over the same 6 h window ws.gaps avg 0.0 max 0.0, recorder.trade_gaps 0, exec.tape_lag_tickers 0.0, exec.ws_event_age_s avg 0.9 s max 9.3 (evidence J, D6). And 7,388 of 7,997 orders (92 %) were placed >24 h before kickoff on markets (5,811 ncaaf) that do not print every 120 s (evidence note 9); intents span only 135 venue markets (brief), so ~90 % of tracked markets read dirty in every host regime. (2) DIRTINESS IS NOT WHAT BLOCKS FILLS. The same books produced 646 no_watcher fill rows / 18,512 contracts on 224 orders (brief). The blocker is the fair_stale cancel — 7,825 of 7,997 orders, median 12.2 min in book (evidence G) — driven by the pricing cadence, not the loop: pricing.budget_exhausted on 109/243 priced ticks on 09-10 (45 %) and zero fair_values rows 01:30-07:30 CT (evidence controller notes 1-2). The loop escalated exactly this to the user on 2026-09-09 (docs/superpowers/autopilot/reports/2026-09-09-phase4.5.md:8) and it is still unanswered. (3) THE 150 CAP IS A CONSTANT, NOT CAPACITY. harness/config/settings.py:64 `exec_max_open_orders: int = 150  # D10: shared across the executed variants`, consumed at plan.py:107 and gated at plan.py:551. The per-variant max_open of 25 is recorded but non-blocking because apply_caps is false for sharp_direct and sharp_two_sided (plan.py:545-551; harness/strategy/run.py:6, 371-372; evidence §I strategy_variants: "apply_caps is true ONLY for constrained"). Intended 3x25 = 75, actual 150. A Mac mini leaves 150 at 150. (4) "SEVERAL TIMES THURSDAY'S LOAD" IS UNSUPPORTED FOR THE PATHS THAT HURT. harness/config/settings.py:21 `ws_max_tickers: int = 500` and ws.subscribed_tickers is already pinned at avg 500.0 / max 500.0 (evidence J) — the subscription cannot grow, only reallocate. The executor's per-loop market set is markets of live intents ∪ working orders (loop.py:413-415) with working orders capped at 150, and Thursday already carried the Saturday NCAAF book. What does scale is DB write volume. (5) THE TRIGGER'S DIAGNOSED CAUSE WAS REMOVED TWO MINUTES AFTER IT FIRED. Journal 101's own ruling: "the box's working set exceeds its RAM and the executor is paying in page faults", with the media stack at ~1.3 GiB of a 7.7 GB box; journal 102 stopped all 16 media containers at 20:12 CT, freeing ~1.5 GB. Journal 107 (23:17 CT): half-hourly p95 fell 256 s -> 56 -> 64 -> 11.5 -> 13.2 -> 15.2 -> 9.1 s, "recovered fourfold", "The box is no longer memory-bound". exec_heartbeat now reads p95_loop_ms 7,112 ms (evidence line 460) — under the 7,500 ms ceiling of verify.md:117, though at 0 open orders. Roadmap.md:315 defines the trigger as p95 over 7.5 s "for two consecutive game windows with fixes 31-32 in place, a second starvation incident, or sustained swap traffic outside deploys". Fixes 31/32 deployed 06:36 and 07:13 CT on 09-10 (journals 95, 98; roadmap rows 31-32), so LAR-SF is window 1 of 2; the trigger fired on the swap clause, whose cause is gone. (6) WHAT SURVIVES, AND A BETTER HOST ARGUMENT THE CLAIM MISSES: pgdata is on the single rotational HDD (evidence A:24) while random_page_cost is 1.1, an SSD value, and effective_io_concurrency is 1 (evidence B, note 6) — that is the real hardware case, and it is also fixable in place. A host move does not bound db.growth_gb_per_day 8.94 on a 46.3 GB database (evidence C) with a 119 GB NVMe; retention (phase 6 archive-and-drop) owns that.

refuted_findings.title: The Monday replay-vs-live duty will almost certainly miss its 2 % band; pre-declare it as an integrity anomaly
refuted_findings.claim: R14 requires `harness replay --execute` over the last game day to reproduce live order and fill counts within 2 %; the live executor skipped 521 loops and averaged 27.5 s per loop (p95 118 s) in the 19:00 hour on 09-10 while the replay runs on an exact 15 s grid, so counts will diverge by construction, and per the calendar that is an anomaly to journal, not a headline.
reasons:
alternative: The claim fails on all three of its legs — the number, the mechanism, and the recommendation — and it misses the one divergence source that is genuinely "by construction."

1) THE NUMBER IS MISREAD. `loops_skipped 521` is not a 19:00-hour figure. `harness/execution/store.py:724-741` is the heartbeat upsert: `loops = exec_heartbeat.loops + 1` (line 732) and `loops_skipped = exec_heartbeat.loops_skipped + excluded.loops_skipped` (line 737), documented at store.py:747-748 as "accumulate in the statement rather than in the process, so a restart continues the count instead of resetting it." `loop.py:1213-1219` returns the skip count for *that one loop*; the lifetime total lives in the row. Evidence.md:460 pairs it with `loops 17138`. So the live executor executed 17,138 of ~17,659 grid periods since the 09-08 deploy — it held the 15 s grid for 97.05 % of periods over three days, missing 2.95 %. The reviewer quotes the ~3 %-of-lifetime number as if it were one hour's damage.

2) THE 19:00 HOUR DOES NOT SAY WHAT IS CLAIMED. Evidence.md D2, 2026-09-10 19:00: n 44, avg 27,533 ms, **p50 10,165 ms**, p95 114,768, max 163,406. The median loop finished in 10.2 s, inside the 15 s period — no skip. The 27.5 s mean is a tail artifact (max 163 s). A heavy-tailed mean is the wrong statistic for "how many periods were missed"; the p50 and the 2.95 % lifetime skip rate are the right ones and they agree with each other.

3) THE MECHANISM IS WRONG: THE EXECUTOR IS LEVEL-TRIGGERED, NOT EDGE-TRIGGERED. A skipped loop defers a decision by 15 s; it does not delete it. `harness/execution/loop.py:406` sets `lower = now - timedelta(seconds=s.intent_ttl_s)` = 900 s, and `store.candidate_signals` (store.py:142-152) is documented as "Candidate signals of the executed variants inside the intent TTL **that have no intent yet**." Every signal is therefore offered to ~60 consecutive loops and deduped on intent existence; losing one of 60 changes nothing. Placement is re-derived from current state each loop (`plan.py:602`) and ordered by `(-edge, signal_created_at, signal_id)` (plan.py:603-604) — a sort key with no wall-clock or arrival-order term, so a 15-30 s phase shift does not reorder the queue. And the driving events are on a ~2 min cadence, not 15 s: evidence.md §F shows game-16 fair_values refreshing every 1-3.5 min (median ~2 min, 46 rows/run). A 15 s grid oversamples a 2-minute event stream; a 15 s live jitter against a 220 s `fair_stale` threshold (plan.py:446, `max(stale_s=180, stale_allowance_s=220)`) is a 7 % timing error on a threshold whose crossings are set by the pricing runs — which replay reproduces exactly via `pricing_clock_for_run` (replay.py:8-13, 190-194).

4) THE RECOMMENDATION IS ALREADY THE WRITTEN POLICY. "pre-declare it as an integrity anomaly, not a headline" is verbatim the existing calendar text: roadmap.md:305 — "Outside the band is an integrity anomaly, not a headline." The R14 ruling already priced it: phase3 design spec line 103 — "R14 strict test with a 2 % duty band (cost a red duty on a WS-gap day, journaled; reverse by widening the duty band only)." And the exact concern was formally put to a reviewer and adjudicated: docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-09-08-phase3-sdd-ledger.md:287 — "concerns 1-2 go to the reviewer against R14 … if replay cannot reproduce live on a real day by construction, that is an Important" — with the ruling at :291 fixing the two real by-construction causes (replay's delta set and the REST-anchored ticker) and recording "cost if wrong: replay tolerance re-measured on the first Monday duty." The proposed action item is a no-op against three existing documents.

5) THE TIMING EVIDENCE IS STALE FOR THE DUTY IT PREDICTS. The Monday 09-14 duty replays the last game day (Sat/Sun 09-12/13), not Thu 09-10. The 19:00 hour cited ran with the sixteen media containers up; they were stopped 09-10 20:12 CT (journal 102, roadmap.md user-TODO line), after which loops ran 7-9 s avg / 9-15 s p95 (journal 101/107, brief line 23) — visible in D2 itself: 22:00 avg 7,885 / p95 13,234; 23:00 avg 6,463 / p95 9,047, both under the 15 s period. The host may also move to the Mac mini today.

6) WHAT THE REVIEWER MISSED — the real by-construction divergence, and it is bigger. `replay._execute` builds a **single-variant** executor: `Executor(..., variants=[variant.variant_id])` (harness/replay.py:250). Live, `exec_max_open_orders = 150` is "shared across the executed variants" (harness/config/settings.py:64), gating placement at `still_open < s.max_open_orders` where `still_open` counts every executed variant's resting orders (plan.py:591-609). Evidence.md D3 shows that cap binding hard: `av 150.0` for 09-10 21:00 and 22:00 (and 09-08 21:00/22:00), with `mx 150` in ~30 of the 53 hours listed. Live, sharp_direct (2,651 orders = 33 % of 7,997) and constrained (391 = 5 %) were crowded out of those 150 slots by sharp_two_sided (4,955 = 62 %); in a single-variant replay the replayed variant has all 150 to itself. That is a placement-count asymmetry measured in tens of percent on cap-bound hours, not the ~3 % the grid skew can produce, and it is structural rather than stochastic.

A fair summary: the duty may well come in red, but the reviewer's stated cause is a ~3 % effect they inflated by misreading a lifetime counter as an hourly one, the effect is further damped by a level-triggered loop over a 900 s TTL, the remedy they propose is already written into the calendar and the R14 ruling, and the dominant cause is a different one they did not name.

materiality: The prediction is probably correct but it is mis-prioritised as "important", because it changes no decision the owner faces in the next 1-2 weeks, and its stated cause and remedy are both likely wrong.

1) The recommendation is already the written policy, verbatim. roadmap.md:305 ("Outside the band is an integrity anomaly, not a headline") and the R14 ruling at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-07-phase3-paper-execution-design.md:103 ("R14 strict test with a 2 % duty band (cost a red duty on a WS-gap day, journaled; reverse by widening the duty band only)") already pre-declare a red duty as journaled-not-headline, with the reversal named. The finding's action ("run the duty, journal the deviation, do not hotfix") is the existing calendar entry. Nothing the owner does or believes changes.

2) Half the check passes trivially. The band covers "order and fill counts". Per evidence D4, filled contracts are 38.92 on 2026-09-08 10:00 and 0.000000 in every hour of 09-09, 09-10 and 09-11; the paper book has 2 queue_model rows on 1 order total (brief §Fills). The fill comparison on the last game day is 0 vs 0.

3) The cited cause is the small term and the cited remedy probably does not fix it. harness/replay.py:249 builds the replay executor with `variants=[variant.variant_id]` — one variant — while harness/execution/plan.py:609 gates placement on `still_open < s.max_open_orders`, where `still_open` is accumulated over all open orders the executor sees and `max_open_orders` is the single shared 150 (settings.py:64, "D10: shared across the executed variants"). Evidence D3 shows that cap pinned: max 150 in 40 of 53 hours, avg 150.0 in four of them; sharp_two_sided holds 4,953 of 7,997 orders (62 %). A single-variant replay gets all 150 to itself where live competed with two others, so for sharp_direct or constrained the cap term alone should move counts by tens of percent — swamping loops_skipped 521 / 17,138 loops = 3.0 % (evidence exec_heartbeat). If so, the duty is red on a Mac mini too, and "the host move is the remedy" is false.

4) The premise may have expired before the duty runs. The Monday 09:45 duty replays "the last game day", which on Mon 09-14 is Sun 09-13 (brief: week 1 ends Sun 09-13; NFL 270 scheduled). The 27,533 ms avg / 114,768 ms p95 figure is the 09-10 19:00 hour on the NAS with the media containers running (evidence D2); those were stopped 09-10 20:12 CT and the owner planned the Mac mini migration for 09-11 (roadmap User-side TODOs; journal 101/102). The 09-10 22:00 and 23:00 hours already fell to 7,885 / 6,463 ms avg.

5) No gate or go/no-go hangs on the duty's colour. The week-1 gate criteria are the separate list in verify.md (settlement mismatches 0, CLV band, R12 80 % share); a red replay row blocks nothing.

What survives is a one-line pre-declaration, cost XS, correctly scoped as info. The genuinely material question this finding brushes past — that a per-variant replay against a shared 150-order cap may make the R14 duty structurally uninformative on every host, leaving the fill model (n = 1 live fill event) with no working determinism check — is a different finding with different evidence and should be routed as its own item rather than folded into this one at "important".

refuted_findings.title: Missing from phase 6: record a live response shape before coding against a new endpoint
refuted_findings.claim: Eight of the twenty-one carried fixes since phase 4 were live-shape surprises the tests could not catch (Kalshi V2 limits, create/amend response, confirming-read 404 and stale 200, order-group delete semantics, the communications channel volume twice, and the Anthropic structured-output keyword subset), each costing a deploy cycle on a host where every deploy is a storm.
reasons:
evidence: Line citations resolve and the counts "eight" and "twenty-one" are arithmetically right, but two load-bearing elements fail.

(1) The third cited evidence is inverted. No file in tests/fixtures/ was added after 2026-09-10; `git log --diff-filter=A` dates every kalshi_*/odds_*/espn_* fixture to 2026-09-06 (975264c, 81f15fe, 839648e, 93717bc, 8c4e231, ca02d95, 7f093d7) or 2026-09-10 (8c14712), the nws_* pair to 2026-09-10 (39b52ee), and both anthropic_* files to 238c4b0, 2026-09-10 10:27 CT, commit subject "phase 5: controller artefacts for T6 (Anthropic proving call and its cached repeat)". That is a live recording made a day BEFORE the fix-39 400 (2026-09-11 05:26 CT, journal 110 l.1335), consumed by tests/test_research_client.py:30-31 and tests/test_veto_worker.py:625-630. So the title's remedy was already practiced on the Anthropic endpoint and did not prevent fix 39 — because fix 39 was a REQUEST-schema defect, not a response shape: journal 110 l.1335 says "the SDK's `parse` helper strips exactly those keywords for class schemas ... and a raw dictionary reaches the API unstripped." A recorded response fixture cannot cover that. (The reviewer's underlying intuition has a different, real basis: the phase 4 authed plan used a hand-queued FakeTransport body for /account/limits, docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-08-phase4-kalshi-authed.md:1821, not a recorded live response — but that is not what was cited.)

(2) Five of the eight are not "live-shape" surprises, and the journal says so explicitly. Fix 27: journal 73 — "the path is right, the venue's read-after-write lag is the cause", and its ruling calls it "a different cause: lag, not shape". Fix 28: journal 76 — "Same venue behaviour as at place, read-after-write lag, surfacing as a stale 200 instead of a 404" (only its `initial_count_fp`/`count_fp` sub-item is shape). Fix 29: journal 80 — "a sequence defect in the smoke, not an adapter defect"; roadmap.md:349 says the reference DID document DELETE as permanent and "the design §1.5 sequence assumed otherwise", i.e. a design/doc-reading failure. Fixes 38/40: frame volume and category mix (journal 110 l.1334: 11-14k frames/min, 74,608 rows in 7 min; journal 112: fix 40 is cross-category combos carrying one NFL leg), not a shape. Genuinely response-shape: fixes 23 and 24, plus part of 28 — 2.5 of 8.

(3) "each costing a deploy cycle" overcounts. 23+24 shipped as one hotfix (roadmap.md:343 "hotfix from main with 24"; :344 "with 23"); 38+39 shipped in one app-only deploy (journal 112, 7c3d555 at 06:38 CT); fix 40 is not yet deployed (roadmap.md:360 "hotfix from main now with fix 41 ... app-only deploy"). Five deploys executed plus one pending, not eight.

(4) "a host where every deploy is a storm" mismatches these deploys. All six are `make deploy-nas-app`, not the full recipe: journal 76 (6e3b33f, 00:50:22-00:52:40 CT), journal 80 (d347ee8, 09:10:32-09:11:53, app-exec healthy at +2 min), journal 82 (4c554ea), journal 112 (7c3d555, executor 40.1 s / 39.9 s then 6.7 s). The storm numbers in brief l.23 and journal 109/110 (loops 90-130 s, 235-336 s) are for the FULL `make deploy-nas` compounded by the 03:30 dump and the RFQ replay.

What survives: the line references are all correct (roadmap.md:343=23, :344=24, :347=27, :348=28, :349=29, :358=38, :359=39, :360=40), the two journal-110 quotes are verbatim, 8 enumerated items is right, and 21 carried fixes since phase 4 is right (fixes 21-41 inclusive per brief l.29; rows 16 and 20 at roadmap.md:339-340 are correctly excluded as pre-phase-4 and user-action).

alternative: The claim fails on three measurable counts and its remedy is already in the process and already demonstrated not to work for the cases cited.

1) "Each costing a deploy cycle" is wrong by a factor of ~2, and the deploys were the cheap kind. The eight fixes map to at most five deploy events, four of them app-only: 23+24 rode the wave-3 deploy 417eecd that was already going out for fixes 21/25/26 (journal 71 lists all four merged in one wave; journal 72: "started 00:07 CT, exit 0, done 00:09 CT", image build cached, marginal cost of 23+24 = zero); 27 -> 6e3b33f app-only (journal 75/76); 28 -> d347ee8 app-only, "09:10:32-09:11:53" = 81 seconds (journal 80); 29 -> 4c554ea app-only 10:41:03-10:48:47, and the journal attributes the 7m44s to something else: "slow because the drill restore shares the NAS disk" (journal 82); 38+39 -> one app-only deploy 7c3d555, 06:35-06:39 (journal 112); 40 rides with 41, app-only plus an app-research/app-ws recreate (roadmap.md:360-361).

2) "A host where every deploy is a storm" is a generalization from the wrong deploys. The storms on record are full-recipe phase deploys with migrations: 0488e22 (journal 109: first loops 91 and 129 s, IO wait >40 %, pulse guard tripped) and 5f18601 (journal 110: exec down 05:20-05:24 from the lock race, first loop 99.9 s). The deploys that carried these eight fixes recovered in minutes: 417eecd p95 8.7 s at +2 min (journal 72); d347ee8 app-exec and app-serve healthy at +2 min (journal 80); 4c554ea executor p95 3.8 s (journal 82); 7c3d555 executor 40.1/39.9 s then 6.7 s at 06:42 (journal 112). The storm root causes are separately owned by fixes 32 (BRIN autosummarize, journal 93 — "the cause of the legacy page's 35-50 s, the check skips, the WS sink timeouts and much of the snapshot storm"), 34 (no warm-up window in the self-guard) and 37 (schema step racing live builders). Charging that cost to the shape fixes double-counts.

3) The failure surface was the designed pre-production gate, not production. All five Kalshi items were found by the demo smoke against the demo venue while the harness is in paper mode: journal 73 "the demo venue is `unavailable` by the smoke's own path (…); prod untouched"; journal 80 "No order was created; nothing rests… Prod tripwire 0 non-GET"; journal 82 "demo smoke PASS 15/15, exit 0". The verify.md demo-smoke row (verify.md:169) is exactly a live-shape capture run, and journal 71 records that fixtures for both V2 response shapes were written from it. The loop already does record-then-code; it records by driving the venue rather than by storing a payload first.

4) The remedy addresses 2 of the 8, and for one endpoint it was performed and still missed. Only fixes 23 (usage_tier/bucket_capacity) and 24 (CreateOrderResult) are response-shape misses. The other six are not shapes: 27 is read-after-write lag (404 twice within 270 ms) and 28 is a stale 200 at +130 ms — journal 73 records the reference was consulted at the time (ctx7 kalshi_openapi_yaml, 00:11 CT) and was correct: "the path is right, the venue's read-after-write lag is the cause"; a recorded payload cannot encode latency or read-your-writes. 29 is a sequence defect in our own script, and the docs were right — journal 80: "Reference (ctx7, 09:14 CT): DELETE /portfolio/order_groups/{id} 'permanently removes the group'. The design addendum §1.5 sequence places the expiring order after cancel_group in the same group: a sequence defect in the smoke, not an adapter defect." 38/40 are traffic volume and leg composition (11-14k frames/min, three quarters deletes, journal 110), which no recorded response shape expresses; and 40 is a measured refinement of 38's own filter found by the counters 38 shipped (journal 112: frames_seen 32,676 / stored 5,833 / dropped_nonfootball 13,497), so counting it as a second independent surprise inflates the total. 39 is decisive against the remedy: phase 5 T6 DID make a live Anthropic proving call and commit its response, tests/fixtures/anthropic_structured_websearch.json and anthropic_cache_hit.json, commit 238c4b0 2026-09-10 ("controller artefacts for T6 (Anthropic proving call and its cached repeat)"), and the 400 still shipped, because the proving path used the SDK's parse helper (which strips the unsupported keywords) while annotate/veto/rationale pass raw dicts (journal 110). Recording a response shape does not validate a request schema.

5) The claim's framing ("missing from phase 6") also misses an existing rule: SKILL.md:99 already requires "current documentation for every external API (ctx7), used as reference only: extract shapes and constraints" at plan-next, and journals 73 and 80 show it being used. The gap is not a missing practice; it is that for authenticated write endpoints the capture step runs after the adapter's echo checks are written rather than before.

6) On the real cost driver: the 27/28/29 sequence spans 2026-09-09 00:16 to 10:56 CT, but the dominant intervals are user gate waits, not deploys — journal 76 gate at 00:56 CT answered in journal 78 at 08:29 CT (7h33m) and journal 80 gate at 09:15 CT answered in journal 81 at 10:24 CT (1h09m), against 81 s and 7m44s of actual deploy.

minor_findings.title: Postgres is tuned for an SSD on a rotational disk; moot after the host move, cheap if staying
minor_findings.claim: pgdata sits on sda (RAID1 rotational) with random_page_cost 1.1, effective_io_concurrency 1, wal_compression off and no container memory limits; the 119 GB NVMe cannot hold a 47 GB database growing 9 GB/day, so the tuning lever is settings, not a data move, and R17 makes it reversible by editing the compose command.
minor_findings.question: nas_sacrifice
evidence: evidence.md A: pgdata bind on /volume1 (sda ROTA=1); nvme0n1 119.2G with 109G overlay; container limits mem=0
evidence.md B: random_page_cost 1.1, effective_io_concurrency 1, wal_compression off, shared_buffers 512 MB
phase3 design spec line 87: Postgres command values (R17); line 103 'reverse by editing the compose command'
evidence.md A: postgres cumulative block read 1.89 TB in 3 days
minor_findings.recommendation: Only if the user stays on the NAS past week 2: test random_page_cost 3-4 and wal_compression on against the scratch restore (P6-09) first, apply in a quiet window, watch exec.loop_ms for a day. Cost S. When: week 3, conditional.

minor_findings.title: One journal entry counted counterfactual fill rows as fills; verify rows should filter fill_method
minor_findings.claim: Journal 92's SEA-NE addendum reports '75 fills for 1,471.42 contracts' while exec.filled_contracts summed over three days is 38.92 and the only queue_model fill is order 157 on 2026-09-08; the 75 are no_watcher/snapshot_cross rows in the fills table, so at least one verify pass read the counterfactual tracks as fills (the phase 5 report itself got it right: 'no fills since 16:25').
minor_findings.question: quality
evidence: journal 92 addendum (line 1227): '434 paper orders placed, 75 fills for 1,471.42 contracts'
evidence.md controller note 5: exec.filled_contracts summed over 3 days = 38.92; fills queue_model 2 rows on order 157
harness/execution/store.py:579-589 MONEY_FILL_METHODS excludes no_watcher and snapshot_cross
reports/2026-09-10-phase5.md §4: 'no fills since 16:25'
minor_findings.recommendation: Add `fill_method = 'queue_model' and replay = false` to every verify.md fills row and to the daily line; re-state the corrected number in the next journal entry (append-only). Cost S. When: before Mon 09-14.

minor_findings.title: Phase 6 item 7's trigger is already met; the proposal is due, the execution stays a gate
minor_findings.claim: /volume1 is 69 % used (31 % free), under item 7's 40 % free trigger, so the loop owes the archive-and-drop proposal now; urgency is low because the harness database is 47 GB growing 8.94 GB/day, which reaches the 25 % free gate (about 650 GB of headroom) in roughly 70 days and the 2 TB ceiling in about 215 days, assuming the media stack does not grow.

roadmap.md:308 daily line: gate below 25 %
